The scanner's 32 KB+ scratch is the codec arena (codec_arena_borrow()), which is free while nothing plays: the build stops the audio core first and waits for it to let go.
  • Playing from a list. A library queue is (order, first, count, position): 16 more bytes in play_queue_t (and 12 in the rollback snapshot), and the same for 100,000 songs as for ten (the folder queue's 3 KB pool and order array are unused then). Entries are positions in the range; the path the queue hands the storage task is a handle, @lib/<order>/<position>, which the storage task turns into the file when the track starts or the gapless look-ahead asks for it (lib_resolve: order file, track record, folder chain and names: four small files, one open at a time, an estimated 20 ms on the card; it is asked while the current track plays, so the audio ring is not at risk). Shuffle is the stateless keyed permutation of the ADR (a balanced 4-round Feistel network over the next even power of two, cycle-walked), so Shuffle Songs over the whole library keeps no array, visits every song once, keeps the current song current when shuffle is switched on or off, and re-keys for each round of repeat-all (never opening with the song just played). A gapless successor that the audio core took but the plan no longer names re-bases the permutation on that song. queue_len / queue_pos and the queue's entries are 32 bit now. Shuffle Songs forces a shuffled queue without changing the Shuffle setting; the folder queue and its 128-track window are as before.
  • Unplayable files (D6). Greyed in every list; Select says why instead of opening it. The queue does not skip them itself: the storage task refuses an unplayable handle with Can't play: ..., and the player's existing rule (a track the queue moved on to that cannot be played is skipped; a whole lap of them under repeat-all ends in the error) does the rest, so Next, auto-advance and Shuffle step past them with the same bounded loop.
  • Resume. The record is written from the real path (the storage task keeps the last two resolved handles' paths for the player, player_set_path_resolver), so a library track resumes as a folder queue of its own folder, at its frame. The queue itself (the album or the shuffle) is not restored; a track that has not been resolved when its record would be written waits for the next save. Library queues keep no shuffle seed across a boot.
  • Building. The first open of a top-level list without an index (and Shuffle Songs) starts the build itself, Music > Update Library rebuilds on demand (decision: an explicit action in Music rather than Settings; Settings is where the Bluetooth branch changes). Progress is the file count (n songs found) with busy dots, not a percentage: the walk and the parse are one pass, so the total is not known until it ends; the sort and the write after it have no per-file callback and no cancel point. Cancel and "another request is waiting" (a Play press, a folder listing) stop the scan at its next file; the old library is untouched and lib.tmp is removed. Nothing is written before Library needs a writable card is ruled out: a write-protected card is answered up front, and a write the card refuses later (the Y2's reopen read-write failing) is reported the same way.
  • Not built: playlists (the entry says None yet), letter jumps (the fast-scroll letter overlay is shown; the jump tables are in the manifest), the fingerprint check at boot and incremental rescans (L3), Right on an artist jumping to its albums (Right / Left skip tracks, as on every other screen).
  • Host. The simulator's card is a folder, not a FatFs volume, so its build of the library uses lib_ff_posix.h, the dozen FatFs-style calls the library makes, over POSIX files (hal/host/lib_ff_posix.c, paths kept inside the card folder); the unit tests run the real FatFs on a disk image and the Y2 and RP2350 builds use theirs. The tour card is made by tests/tools/make_library_card.py: real FLAC test vectors with their tags replaced, an MP3, an AAC track, three silent 3 s WAVs; NEUPOD_LIB_SLOW_MS (simulator only) slows the scan so the progress screen can be photographed.

  • Measured. Host, POSIX files with a warm cache (the tour card plus real FLAC test vectors): 276 tracks in 131 ms and 1,016 tracks in 322 ms for the whole build (11 sort runs, 99 KB of scratch); L1's 100,000-file run on the FatFs image is unchanged by L2 (12 s). The device is not measured yet: the ADR's own figures (10-20 ms per parsed file) put about 260 FLACs at roughly 5 to 8 seconds, see Storage.

  • Index format 3 (12 November 2026, UI review LB-2b). The sort key also skips a leading "A " and "An " (as it already skipped "The "), so "A Perfect Circle" is under P. The order changes, so LIB_VERSION is 3: an index from a firmware before this fails the version check ("Library needs rebuilding") and the Music lists rebuild it by themselves on the next open, exactly as for format 2.

docs.title: ADR-0018: UI resolution profiles
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner decision 11 Nov 2026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The UI was written for the Phase 1 panel, 320x240: UI_W / UI_H / UI_ROW_H constants plus pixel literals in every screen, Montserrat 14 / 20 / 48, two 320 x 24 render buffers. The Y2 Linux testbed (testbed/y2) has a 480x360 panel and runs the same firmware as a hosted build. Two ways to get the UI there: render at 320x240 and scale the frame up (blurry text, wasted pixels, a scaler in the display path), or render natively at 480x360.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The UI is resolution-independent through a metrics profile. ui_metrics_t (app/ui/ui_metrics.h) holds every pixel size and the fonts; ui_task selects the profile once from hal_display_width() / hal_display_height() (the largest compiled-in profile that fits; 320x240 otherwise). Screens read UIM->...; nothing else scales a length.
  • 320x240 is the product panel and its profile holds the exact numbers the UI had before: the host snapshots at that size are unchanged (compared byte for byte against the previous build, apart from the build hash text and timing animation).
  • 480x360 is for the Y2 testbed (and for testing the hires layout on the host): every length x 3/2, fonts one step up (Montserrat 14 to 20, 20 to 28, 48 stays; it is the largest size built; the fonts are the project's own Latin-1 builds, see UI), 9 rows per page in both.
  • Hires fonts and buffers are compiled only for hosted builds. CMake option NEUPOD_UI_HIRES (default ON for host and y2, OFF for rp2350 and esp32s3) gates the 480x360 profile, Montserrat 28 (lv_conf.h), the 480 x 36 render buffers, a 192 KB LVGL pool and the layout audit. The product build keeps its 72 KB pool and its 2 x 15 KB render buffers.
  • Native over scaling. The owner chose native rendering on 11 Nov 2026.
  • The host HAL display size is selectable at run time (NEUPOD_DISPLAY_SIZE=WxH, default 320x240), so the hires layout runs in the simulator and in CI. That, hal_display.h wording and nothing else changed under hal/.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RAM budget: RP2350 unchanged. The render buffers, LVGL pool, list row pool (UI_ROWS_MAX = 9) and every other static allocation of the product build keep their sizes. Hosted builds: render buffers 2 x 34 KB, pool 192 KB (measured peak 69 KB across every tour at 480x360).
  • Flash budget (RP2350): the product build has one profile, defined as a header constant, so every field read folds into an immediate and the metrics cost nothing; measured on 11 Nov 2026 (Release, neupod.elf): text 1,289,412 B before and after (0 B), .data 0 and .bss 489,348 B unchanged (the display, i2c and storage test images are byte-for-byte the same size). Montserrat 28 is now compiled out of the product build; it was enabled but unreferenced, so the linker had already dropped it (no size effect, it just keeps the guarantee explicit). An earlier version with a run-time pointer to the table grew the image by 2.8 KB, which is why the product build does not select a profile at run time.
  • Layout is checked, not eyeballed: tests/test_ui_metrics.c (static invariants of every profile), the tours at 480x360 with the layout audit (ui_audit.c, NEUPOD_UI_AUDIT=1) and hires_art_snapshot (pixel checks of the art boxes).
  • Known limits at 480x360: album art is still decoded to 64 x 64 (ART_MAX_DIM; raising it costs 8 KB per step of static RAM on the product build and changes the art snapshots) and scaled up 2.6x by LVGL; the splash wordmark stays at 48 pt; the bring-up scenes (gfx_strip, display tests) are 320x240 only.
  • Another panel size needs one profile (one initialiser in ui_metrics.c) and, if it is larger than 480x360, bigger UI_BUF_W_MAX / UI_BUF_LINES_MAX and the host HAL's 640x480 ceiling raised.
  • The input path is untouched: wheel, keys and the Y2 buttons all deliver the same events.

docs.title: Amendment: 600x450 (14 Nov 2026)
docs.text:
The Waveshare RP2350-Touch-AMOLED-2.41 and ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.41 dev boards have a 600x450 panel (4:3 again).

  • A third profile, ui_metrics_600.h: every length x 15/8, Montserrat 22 / 26 / 38 (and 48) and Lucide 30 / 45, 7 rows. It is a header, like the 320x240 one, so a product build can use it as its one constant profile.
  • The one-constant model stays. CMake cache variable NEUPOD_UI_PROFILE (320x240 default | 600x450) selects the single profile a non-hosted build compiles in (UI_BUF_W_MAX / UI_BUF_LINES_MAX follow: 600 x 30 for 600x450). Hosted builds (NEUPOD_UI_HIRES) carry all three and select at run time; NEUPOD_DISPLAY_SIZE=600x450 runs it on the host. The default Pico 2 W image: static RAM unchanged (.data identical, .bss +4 bytes; the Pico's RAM has only about 100 bytes to spare, and a first draft that used sscanf in the tour-script parser pulled newlib's locale data into .data and broke the link, so keep such calls out of product code), flash +1.4 KB (the touch poll, the panel/profile check, the area rounder).
  • ui_task checks the panel against the profile on every build (it used to skip that on the RP2350, which assumed a 320x240 panel) and warns on a mismatch.
  • Even-aligned flush windows (RM690B0 / SH8601 CASET / RASET): an LV_EVENT_INVALIDATE_AREA handler rounds areas to even start and even size, unconditionally; every profile has an even buf_lines (the 600x450 one 30, not the 45 that 15/8 of 24 would give).
  • Layout is checked as before: test_ui_metrics (the invariants run on every compiled-in profile), hires600_* tours with the audit, Touch input for the touch gestures.

docs.title: ADR-0019: Bluetooth audio output behind a stack-neutral boundary
Status
docs.text: Accepted (owner decisions, 12 Nov 2026): keep BTstack, and build the audio sink so the stack can be swapped cheaply. The owner's answers to the design questions are recorded at the end.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Stage 2a (Bluetooth) built pairing and the connection on the RP2350 + CYW43439 with BTstack. It is behind hal_bt_* in hal/include/hal_radio.h, and the BTstack code sits in one file, platforms/rp2350/hal/hal_radio_bt.c. That file mixes three things: BTstack's link logic (pairing state machine, SDP, TLV glue), the CYW43 transport and its run loop, and the Pico SDK hooks.
  • There is no audio yet. hal_radio_a2dp_connect() / _disconnect() are declared but not implemented.
  • On 12 Nov 2026 the Y2 testbed streamed A2DP to AirPods Pro and a Sony WI-C200. It used BTstack over the MT6582's /dev/stpbt (testbed/y2/tools/y2-a2dp, a standalone tool) and played a tone and a FLAC from the card. Two platforms now have a working BTstack controller, each with a different transport and run loop.
  • Licence. BTstack is free for non-commercial use only (Bluetooth → Licence). The owner does not expect neuPod ever to be sold (12 Nov 2026), so BTstack is acceptable. It still has to stay replaceable: a licensed BTstack, Zephyr's host or ESP-IDF Bluedroid (ADR-0007 update) are the alternatives.

docs.title: 1. One boundary: hal_bt_*, extended for audio
docs.text:
Everything above the HAL (app/runtime/bt_service.c, the player, the audio engine, the UI) sees hal_radio.h only. No BTstack type, header or constant crosses it. That rule already holds; the decision is to keep it for audio. Stage 2b adds, replacing the hal_radio_a2dp_* stubs:

Addition Purpose hal_bt_stream_open() / _start() / _suspend() / _close() A2DP stream on the CONNECTED link. Asynchronous; progress through events. hal_bt_codec_t (codec, rate, channels, mode, bitpool_min/max, kbps) The negotiated configuration, for the badge and the stats. The enum names SBC, SBC-XQ (and AAC / aptX for a stack or module that has them). HAL_BT_EVT_STREAM (OPENING, OPEN, STREAMING, SUSPENDED, CLOSED, FAILED + reason) Stream state. HAL_BT_EVT_VOLUME (0..127, absolute) AVRCP absolute volume from the headset. hal_bt_volume_set(0..127) Our volume to the headset. HAL_BT_EVT_KEY (PLAY, PAUSE, PLAY_PAUSE, NEXT, PREV, STOP) AVRCP passthrough from the headset buttons. hal_bt_track_info() Title, artist, album, duration and position for AVRCP metadata (2c). hal_bt_stats_t Encoded frames, packets sent, ring underruns, drift corrections, link quality where the controller reports it.

PCM does not go through hal_bt_*. It goes through the core 1 to core 0 ring of ADR-0013 (4 Nov amendment). The encoder side drains the ring. The audio engine treats Bluetooth as one more output: it selects "Bluetooth", fills the ring, and never knows which stack encodes it.

docs.title: 2. BTstack in one adapter, transports per platform
docs.text:
The BTstack code is split into:

  • hal/common/bt_btstack/ (platform-neutral, built by every platform that uses BTstack): the link state machine moved out of hal_radio_bt.c, the A2DP source, the AVRCP target and controller, the SBC encoder feed and pacing (the source-side pacing model in Bluetooth), the TLV bridge onto hal_bt_storage_t, and the implementation of every hal_bt_* function.
  • Per-platform glue (bt_port.h: init the transport, give the run loop, post to it, local address, power):
  • platforms/rp2350/hal/bt_port_cyw43.c: the CYW43 transport and async_context run loop, as now.
  • platforms/y2/hal/bt_port_stpbt.c: btstack_uart_stpbt + btstack_chipset_mtk_consys (promoted from the testbed tool) and the POSIX run loop on its own pthread.

Swapping the stack means writing a new hal/common/bt_<stack>/ against the same hal_radio.h and the same bt_port.h. Nothing above the HAL changes, and nor do its tests.

docs.title: 3. The host simulator implements the whole API
docs.text: hal/host/hal_radio.c grows the stream, codec, volume and key events (and a simulated drop) so every UI and player behaviour below runs in host tests and tours without a radio. The simulator and the BTstack adapter are two implementations of one contract. A contract test (tests/test_hal_bt_contract.c) drives both where it can: the simulator in CI, BTstack against a fake controller (as test_hci_preinit does in the y2-a2dp tool).

docs.title: 4. The Y2 becomes a Bluetooth platform
docs.text: The firmware on the Y2 gets real Bluetooth through bt_port_stpbt.c, instead of the "not present" stubs in platforms/y2/hal/hal_radio.c. The WMT bring-up (stock wmt_loader once per boot, 6620_launcher, the property area, the device nodes) moves into the Y2 init scripts ahead of the firmware, and hal_bt_init() opens /dev/stpbt. The testbed rules hold: MTK blobs are staged from the backup, never committed; NVRAM is never written. y2-a2dp stays as the bench tool.

docs.title: 5. The UI is part of stage 2b, not an afterthought
docs.text:
Every state that the boundary can report has a screen, and every one is in a host tour with a snapshot:

Where What Status bar Bluetooth icon: grey = remembered headset not connected, white = connected, accent colour = streaming. Hidden when Bluetooth is unavailable. Now Playing The format badge shows the negotiated codec on Bluetooth output (SBC 44.1, SBC-XQ); the source format stays in the stats. On Bluetooth the volume bar is the headset volume. Volume With absolute volume the wheel sends hal_bt_volume_set() and the software volume stays at 0 dB; the headset's own volume changes move the bar. Without it, the wheel is the software volume, as on I2S. One mapping table, host-tested. Headset buttons HAL_BT_EVT_KEY becomes the same player actions as Play / Right / Left, on every screen. Link lost while playing The player pauses at once (ring emptied, position kept). A banner reads Headset disconnected for 3 s. The output stays Bluetooth: nothing plays from the wired output by itself. Settings > Bluetooth Paired, no audio yet is gone. The headset row shows Connected - SBC-XQ / Streaming / Not connected / Failed: <reason>. A new Audio output: Auto / Wired row (Auto = Bluetooth whenever a headset is connected; saved on the card). The right-hand pane adds codec, bitpool, kbit/s, underruns. Devices Unchanged apart from the wording above. Pairing a second headset while one is remembered asks to replace it (one headset, as now). Settings > About Bluetooth stats line (frames, underruns, drift corrections). Errors Every new hal_bt_fail_t reason gets its phrase in hal_bt_fail_text() (19 characters max) and a tour snapshot.

Tours: --tour-bt is extended with bt-streaming, np-bt-badge, np-bt-volume, bt-dropped and bt-key-next, at 320x240 and 480x360 (ADR-0018).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• hal_radio_bt.c is split before the A2DP work starts. That is a no-behaviour-change refactor of stage 2a, proven by the existing 2a tests and the bench Pair / reconnect / Forget on the WI-C200 (RP2350) before anything new is added.
  • The Y2 can prove the A2DP source, pacing, AVRCP and the whole UI on real headsets while the RP2350 path is still RAM-constrained. Bugs found there are in shared code, so the fix lands on both.
  • A different stack later costs one adapter and its glue. A QCC/BM83 module would be an adapter that speaks the module's UART protocol instead of HCI, behind the same API.
  • The core 1 rules (ADR-0011) are unchanged: core 1 only fills the ring; all Bluetooth work is on core 0. The closure check covers the ring.
  • RAM budget: the boundary itself costs nothing (header types, one event struct grows by about 24 B). RP2350: SBC encoder state and media buffers are measured in 2b and come out of free SRAM (about 14.9 KB). The PCM ring reuses the I2S ring storage (ADR-0013 amendment). Y2: not constrained. Flash, RP2350: A2DP + AVRCP + SBC encoder, measured in 2b.

docs.title: Owner decisions (12 Nov 2026)
docs.text:
1. Split now. The BTstack link logic moves out of platforms/rp2350/hal/hal_radio_bt.c into hal/common/bt_btstack/ before 2b, as a no-behaviour-change refactor.
  2. Link lost while playing: pause and stay on Bluetooth (position kept, banner); no fallback to wired output.
  3. Output selection: automatic, with an Audio output: Auto / Wired row to force wired.
  4. Volume: AVRCP absolute volume to the headset with the software volume at 0 dB; software volume when the headset has no absolute volume.
  5. Y2 as a Bluetooth platform: yes, the real stack goes into the Y2 firmware (taken as the default; not asked separately).

docs.title: Amendment 12 Nov 2026: stage 2b as built
docs.text:
Details and the RAM / flash figures are in Bluetooth. Differences from the decision above, all deliberate:

  • hal_bt_set_pcm_source() hands the stack the consumer side of the PCM ring (a small type in hal/include/hal_bt_pcm.h). PCM still does not travel through hal_bt_*; the stack pulls it from the ring on its own thread.
  • 44.1 kHz only. One SBC endpoint at 44.1 kHz; tracks at other rates are refused on the Bluetooth output. 48 kHz and the hi-res decimation of ADR-0013 are a follow-up.
  • Declared in 2c (see below): HAL_BT_EVT_VOLUME, hal_bt_volume_set, HAL_BT_EVT_KEY, hal_bt_track_info; the Now Playing volume bar and the headset buttons.
  • Two new failure reasons, HAL_BT_FAIL_STREAM ("audio refused") and HAL_BT_FAIL_CODEC ("no common format"); the status-bar glyph uses the text colour for "connected" because the bar is light.

docs.title: Amendment 12 Nov 2026: stage 2c as built, and reconnect
docs.text:
Details in Bluetooth. Differences from the decision above:

  • The volume path is the AVRCP controller role (the headset is the target of absolute volume); the AVRCP target carries the buttons and the metadata. hal_bt_volume_supported() / hal_bt_volume_get() are added to the boundary, HAL_BT_EVT_KEY also has FF and RW, and hal_bt_track_info() returns false when the stack is busy.
  • Volume cap on connect (owner decision, 12 Nov 2026): a headset whose first absolute-volume report on a connection is above 50 % (NEUPOD_BT_VOLUME_CAP_ON_CONNECT, 64 of 127) is turned down to 50 %, never up; later changes are the user's. Taking over the headset's volume releases the software attenuation, so a headset a phone left at 100 % would otherwise play full scale.
  • A headset-initiated AVDTP START (a stem click on a suspended stream) is delivered as HAL_BT_KEY_PLAY; every AVRCP pass-through and every remote START / SUSPEND is logged.
  • STOP from the headset pauses (the place is kept). No volume is remembered per headset.
  • Stage 3 reconnect is built early on the owner's request: after a lost link and at power-up, with backoff, ended by any user action; playback is not resumed.

docs.title: ADR-0020: Hold, the lock that replaces the iPod's slide switch
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner decisions 12 Nov 2026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A pocket player gets pressed by its own pocket. The iPod answered that with a slide switch ("Hold") that made the wheel and buttons do nothing. neuPod has to answer it on every platform it runs on:

  • the Y2 testbed has a Power key on its side and no slide switch;
  • the Pico 2 W bench rig has neither (UART console keys only);
  • the final board is the iPod 6G donor, which has the real slide switch.

Until now the Y2 had its own, partial answer inside the HAL: a short Power press put the screen to sleep (input swallowed except Power and Centre/Menu), a 2 s hold shut the player down. The screen dimmed after an idle time (UI-5, first half) but never went fully off.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
One Hold state, set from several places, enforced in one place (the UI frame).

  • Where it is enforced. ui_frame_input() (app/ui/ui_frame.c). While Hold is on, wheel turns and button presses and releases are swallowed before any screen sees them: they cannot act (Play/Pause included), cannot click, and cannot move anything. They only restart the idle clock (the screen wakes) and show a reminder ("Locked, hold Power to unlock"). Headset (AVRCP) keys do not go through the UI and keep working: they are deliberate. The Y2's side volume keys are hardware keys like the rest and are locked too (ui_locked(), checked where the Y2 handles them). Hold is RAM only: it is not saved over a power-off (a boot starts unlocked unless the switch says otherwise).
  • Auto-lock. When the screen goes off (below), Hold turns on by itself. Settings > Display > Auto-lock (On by default, saved) turns that off; Hold is then only set by hand.
  • Screen off (UI-5, second stage). After the dim (Settings > Display > Auto-dim / Dim after, unchanged) the backlight goes fully off after Screen off after (default 3 min after the dim; Never, 15 s, 30 s, 1, 2, 3, 5 min; counted from the last input when Auto-dim is off; saved). The input that wakes a screen that was off is not delivered to the screen, locked or not. A short Power press (released within 0.4 s) also turns the screen off at once, and the next input wakes it. The panel is not put to sleep: only the backlight goes (hal_display_backlight(0)), as before on the Y2.
  • The Power key. Reported by the HAL as a level (hal_input_power_key()), turned into INPUT_POWER_DOWN / _UP events by the input task (which never loses an edge: a lost release would count as a 10 s hold), timed by the UI (app/ui/ui_hold.c, unit tested):
Held What happens under 0.4 s (a tap) screen off now (and Hold on, with Auto-lock) 0.4 s to 2 s a line under the status bar fills and a pill says "Keep holding to lock" / "... to unlock"; releasing early does nothing 2 s, still held Hold toggles: a confirmation ("Locked" / "Unlocked"), a haptic click where fitted, the lock icon in the status bar 5 s still held: "Release to cancel · shutting down in 5" with a red line that grows; releasing cancels 10 s power-off is requested (hal_system_poweroff())

The power-off countdown only exists where hal_system_can_poweroff() is true (the Y2; the host simulator pretends). The Y2 keeps its contract: the request runs the firmware's orderly stop, starts /sbin/poweroff detached and exits with status 77 so S91neupod-fw does not respawn it. What changed is the timing (10 s, was 2 s) and who decides (the UI, not the HAL). Charging-only mode is untouched: its own loop still reboots on a 2 s hold (y2_charge). * The hardware switch. hal_input_hold_switch() reports NONE / OFF / ON. A change becomes INPUT_HOLD_SWITCH and sets the same Hold state (on = locked, off = unlocked); a switch found on at boot locks at once. The Power gesture still toggles too, so the two agree after any change. Platforms without a switch report NONE: the Y2 and the Pico rig. The final board's GPIO is a TODO(hw). * No Power key (Pico 2 W bench): Hold is gesture-only there. The console key l toggles Hold (INPUT_HOLD_TOGGLE), and the reminder says "Console key l unlocks" instead of "hold Power 2 s to unlock". The bench rig cannot power itself off, so no countdown. * Host simulator: F1 is the Power key (hold it), and tour tokens pwr:down, pwr:up, sleep:MS and sw:on / sw:off drive the Power key and the switch from scripts.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RAM budget: about 100 B of statics (Hold state, the pump state, the overlay's object pointers); the overlay's four LVGL objects exist only while something is shown (a few hundred bytes of the LVGL pool, freed after). The input queue grows from 16 to 64 events (+384 B, see UI-6 in Runtime). Measured sizes are in the pull request.
  • Flash: three glyphs (lock, unlock, power) in the three UI fonts, the Hold logic and the Licences data (see the pull request for the figures).
  • Y2 behaviour change: the HAL no longer sleeps the screen or swallows input by itself, and a 2 s hold no longer powers off (it toggles Hold; 10 s powers off). docs/y2.md describes the new behaviour.
  • A press that wakes the screen is lost on purpose, locked or not: that is the price of a pocket-proof player.
  • A button held down when Hold comes on (a fast-forward in progress) still gets its release: the frame remembers which presses a screen saw and delivers exactly those releases while locked, so nothing is left pressed.
  • Tests: ui_hold (the timing model), ui_frame_keys (what the frame swallows and when), ui_logic (the off stage), input_events (the hand-over and the console key), y2_input, and the hold_tour / hires_hold_tour runs (ring, lock, swallowed keys, countdown, simulated power-off, switch, screen off, wake, unlock, the new Display rows) with the layout audit at 320x240 and 480x360.

docs.title: Amendment 12 November 2026: the visuals are the lock pill and the Power-hold line
docs.text: The overlay box of this ADR (a boxed headline, a second line and a progress bar over the middle of the content) is replaced by the design review's HL-1 (UI design review, section 3.8): a dark pill at the bottom of the screen with one line of text, and a 3 px line under the status bar (accent while a Power press fills towards the toggle, red for the power-off countdown). Nothing behind them is dimmed or blended, so only the pill and the line are repainted. The gestures, timings, the swallowed input, the switch and the power-off contract are unchanged. The texts: "Keep holding to lock · 10 s = off" (no "10 s = off" where the platform cannot power off), "Locked" / "Unlocked", "Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock" for a swallowed key, "Release to cancel · shutting down in N", "Powering off". The lock icon is a Lucide icon in the status bar's right-hand group. RAM: the pill, its label and the line are built once with the frame (a few hundred bytes of the LVGL pool) instead of being built and deleted per use.

docs.title: Amendment 2026-11-19: Lock hold setting
docs.text:
Settings > Display > Lock hold (Off, 1, 2, 3, 5 s; stored as SETTING_LOCK_HOLD, NPlh, a u8 of seconds) sets how long Power must be held to toggle Hold. It replaces the fixed 2 s of the table above. Default Off (owner request: on the bench rig an accidental lock got in the way; an absent or unknown stored value is Off, so existing users get Off too). The store stays at version 2 (one more item, worst case about 43 of 48; an older firmware keeps an unknown tag untouched).

  • Off. The Power gesture never toggles Hold. A tap still puts the screen to sleep and 10 s still powers off with the countdown from 5 s. The hardware slide switch is always honoured, and so is the console key l, a deliberate dev override like the switch. Turning Lock hold Off while locked unlocks (with the usual "Unlocked" confirmation); a lock set by the switch or the console key afterwards stays until the same route (or Lock hold) undoes it.
  • Ring while Off. Where the platform can power off, a press past 0.4 s shows the accent line filling towards the start of the countdown (5 s) with the pill "Keep holding to power off"; where it cannot there is no ring (the press is only a tap). With 5 s the toggle and the countdown start together at 5 s: the ring completes, Hold toggles, the countdown shows.
  • Auto-lock. It only engages while Lock hold is not Off (nothing in the gesture could undo it). With Lock hold Off the Auto-lock row is greyed, reads Off, and Select does nothing; the stored Auto-lock choice is kept and returns when Lock hold is turned on. A user who had the old default (Auto-lock On, 2 s fixed) now has Lock hold Off and must set it to 2 s to get the old behaviour back.
  • Reminder text. "Locked · hold Power N s to unlock" with the chosen N; with Lock hold Off or no Power key, "Locked · console key l unlocks" (also shown on a locked-by-switch device with the setting Off; the switch itself is the way back there).
  • Model: ui_hold_t.toggle_s (0 = off, kept in struct padding), ui_hold_set_toggle_s(), ui_hold_progress_t.to_off. Host tour token lockhold:N.

docs.title: ADR-0021: Power: sleep when idle, power off after a day, power off when the battery is empty
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner decisions 15 Nov 2026; the four rules in "Decision" were set by the lead and are marked as such)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The player must be able to sit on a shelf for a week and still power up, and the owner must never have to remember to switch it off. ADR-0020 turns the screen off and locks after a few minutes, but the rest of the machine keeps running: the CPU, the Bluetooth controller, the card. The Y2 testbed draws tens of milliamps in that state, which is a flat battery in a few days.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Idle means suspend, a day of suspend means power off, an empty battery means power off. One pure policy decides; each platform says what it can do.

  • Idle. After Sleep after with nothing happening the player sleeps. Settings > Display > Sleep after: Never, 10, 30 (default), 60 min, saved (NPsl; an older settings file has no such item and gives the default, so the settings file version is unchanged). Idle is counted by app/power/power_policy.c (unit tested, power_policy) from the last input of any kind (a key, the wheel, the touch panel, including the input that wakes the screen).
  • Paused counts as idle (lead decision): a paused player sleeps; its place is already saved (ADR resume), and Play after the wake continues from it.
  • Playing does not: while audio plays the count is held at zero, so after a two-hour album the 30 minutes start when it ends, not when the last key was pressed.
  • Busy does not: a library build or scan, a Bluetooth pairing, connect or scan, a Wi-Fi join, a haptic calibration, or a card request or write in flight. There is no USB file transfer on any platform yet; it belongs in the same list when one appears.
  • Never on external power (lead decision): USB or a charger holds the count at zero (hal_power_external()).
  • A day asleep: power off (lead decision). The sleep is asked for with a 24 hour limit; when the limit passes (HAL_WAKE_TIMER) the core takes the normal power-off path. The resume position is saved across boots, so the next power-on comes back where the player was.
  • Empty battery: clean power-off (lead decision). Off external power, a valid battery reading at or below 3 % (or a cell below 3.3 V) for 30 s in a row shows "Battery empty" for 3 s, writes the settings out and takes the normal power-off path. An unknown reading, a missing gauge or a charger resets the streak: unknown is never empty. The rule does not depend on idleness.
  • Where the policy meets the platform. hal_power.h: hal_power_can_sleep(), hal_power_sleep(max_ms, &why) (blocks; why = key, timer, external power, other), hal_power_external(). A platform that cannot sleep answers can_sleep false and the core, after the same idle time, calls hal_system_poweroff() where hal_system_can_poweroff() is true (the RP2350 AMOLED board and the ESP32-S3 board have a soft latch, so they power off), and does nothing where it is not (the policy does not even ask: power_service_can_act()).

docs.title: The sleep sequence (UI task, ui_frame.c and power_service.c)
docs.text:
The UI task owns it: it owns the idle clock, Hold and the display. In order:

  1. power_service_sleep_prepare(): nothing is playing (checked again); the Bluetooth stream stops and the controller is powered off through the stack-neutral radio interface (hal_bt_power(false), new in hal_radio.h; BTstack: hci_power_control(OFF), which on the Y2 closes /dev/stpbt and so powers the chip's Bluetooth function off), remembering whether a headset was linked; the settings (which hold the resume position) are written out and the card synced, waiting at most 4 s for the storage task to be idle. If the card stays busy the sleep is dropped (a write in flight must not be cut by a suspend), Bluetooth is put back, and the count restarts. Wired audio needs nothing: the output stages power down a few seconds after the last sound, long before 10 minutes (docs/audio.md).
  2. The screen goes off exactly as the idle stage does it (forced off, Hold on under Auto-lock), then hal_display_sleep(true).
  3. hal_power_sleep(24 h).
  4. The wake: hal_display_sleep(false); the Bluetooth controller back on if it was, and, if a headset was linked, the existing power-up auto-reconnect runs (its 5 minutes of tries, " connected" toast); the idle count restarts. Then by reason:
  5. Key: the screen stays dark and locked as it was. The input that woke the system is still queued for the input task and arrives like any input that wakes a dark screen: it only lights the screen and is not delivered, locked or not (ADR-0020). If it never arrives (2 s) the screen lights by itself.
  6. Timer: the normal power-off path. If the platform cannot power off, it carries on awake.
  7. External power / other / the system would not sleep: nobody pressed anything, so the screen lights at once.

docs.title: Y2 (Linux 3.4.67, MediaTek, Android-style power management)
docs.text: hal_power_can_sleep() is true when NEUPOD_SUSPEND is not 0 (/etc/neupod-fw.env, the kill switch: 0 makes the core power off instead), /sys/power/state offers mem, and /dev/alarm opens. The firmware holds the wake lock neupod while awake. A sleep, on a helper thread (not an RTOS task; the signal and RTOS rules of the Bluetooth thread apply): arm /dev/alarm with ANDROID_ALARM_RTC_WAKEUP at now + 24 h (ANDROID_ALARM_SET; the ioctl numbers are written out locally from the driver's uapi layout, y2_suspend.h), wake_unlock neupod, then mem to /sys/power/state; wait on the key, touch and ring nodes (own descriptors, poll) and on the two clocks (CLOCK_BOOTTIME keeps counting while suspended, CLOCK_MONOTONIC does not: the difference is the time slept). The thaw: wake_lock neupod first, then on to state (cancels the standing suspend request and late-resumes the panel), then the alarm is cleared. The race this answers: after any wake the kernel re-suspends as soon as the waking device's own wake lock lets go, because the request mem still stands; our lock, retaken within microseconds of the thaw (the helper is runnable the moment userspace thaws, and the input event holds its device's lock until read), is what stops that, and on ends the request. If nothing suspends within 12 s (another wake lock) the lock and on are put back and the call answers HAL_EBUSY. Only a key press counts as input during the first seconds, because a controller powering down may emit releases or positions. hal_millis(), hal_micros() and the FreeRTOS tick (a thread sleeping in usleep) follow CLOCK_MONOTONIC and so never see the sleep: nothing jumps, nothing stalls. External power is power_supply/{usb,ac}/online; a plug-in during sleep ends it (if the hardware wakes on it, a bonus). Plugged into a PC over USB the Y2 reports external power and therefore never sleeps: test the suspend on battery.

docs.title: Other platforms
docs.text:
• Host: simulated (hal/host/hal_power.c): the sleep logs and blocks until something is pressed at the window, or NEUPOD_HOST_SLEEP_WAKE_MS (an injected Select press), or NEUPOD_HOST_SLEEP_MAX_MS (timer); NEUPOD_SUSPEND=0 turns it off; NEUPOD_HOST_EXTERNAL_POWER=1 simulates a charger. Tour tokens idlesleep:N (sleep once after N s of idleness), batt:N (the gauge reads N %) and ext:on / ext:off.
  • RP2350 AMOLED board, ESP32-S3: hal/common/hal_power_none.c: no suspend yet, so after the idle time they power off (soft latch).
  • Pico 2 W (frozen, about 100 B of static RAM spare): the whole feature is compiled out (NEUPOD_POWER_MGMT=0 from the top-level CMakeLists.txt: no setting, no row, no policy, no sequence, no hal_bt_power). It can neither sleep nor switch itself off, so there is nothing for it to do.

docs.title: Failure paths (review fixes)
docs.text:
• A sleep that did not happen (HAL_EBUSY / HAL_ERR): the screen is not lit for it. Everything is put back as it was before the sleep (Bluetooth on, the screen off and locked if it was, otherwise lit and unlocked again), and the count restarts. Two failures in a row stop further tries for an hour (power_guard_*, unit tested). Only an external-power or unknown wake lights the screen by itself.
  • A last look before the screen goes: if an input is queued or a charger appeared during the preparation (which can take seconds), the sleep is abandoned, Bluetooth is put back and the count restarts; the input is handled as usual.
  • A power-off the platform refuses (hal_system_poweroff() false although it says it can: a USB-powered dev board, where the latch cannot cut power) is latched as "external power": nothing tries again (no more GPIO pulses or blocked UI) until the gauge shows a discharge (rate of at least -2000 milli-percent/h, the UI's own "discharging" threshold, or the cell 100 mV lower than at the refusal) or 6 h pass. The same latch, and a gauge rate above +2000 (the Y2's rate is synthetic, plus or minus 10 %/h from the supply status; the MAX17048's is its CRATE register: both are the figures the UI already uses for "charging"), count as external power for the battery rule too. A refused critical power-off withdraws the "Battery empty" notice and logs "on external power". A refusal that was not USB (the RP2350 AMOLED board also refuses while the Power key is held over 3 s) latches the same way, so idle and empty-battery power-off stay off for up to 6 h or until the gauge shows a discharge. A user's 10 s Power hold calls the power-off directly and is unaffected.
  • Y2, a firmware stopped mid-request. state stays mem if the firmware is killed after the request and before the thaw, and the next start would find the panel early-suspended. hal_power_init() therefore writes on right after taking the wake lock (idempotent), and the exit handler writes on before releasing the lock.
  • Y2, the timer. Decided by CLOCK_BOOTTIME reaching the limit, or, if that clock did not run on across the sleep, by the alarm driver's own clock (ANDROID_ALARM_GET_TIME) reaching the armed time. Any event at all from the wheel node (mtk-tpd) after the system has been seen to sleep is a key wake (dark, locked, not delivered); before that only a press counts.
  • Stale events. An event queued shortly before the sleep may light the screen just before the wake key does: harmless (the wake key is swallowed either way).
  • NEUPOD_SLEEP_MAX_S (Y2, bench only, in /etc/neupod-fw.env) shortens the 24 h limit so the timer wake can be tried in minutes.
  • With no card (RAM-only settings) the preparation does not wait for a flush; it re-checks that the storage task is idle after the card sync, right before suspending.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Failure stance. Unknown battery, a failed gauge, an unreadable charger sensor: never power off or sleep because of it (the battery rule needs a valid reading; "external power unknown" counts as not on a charger, which only matters for the sleep, and the sleep is always safe to repeat). A sleep that cannot be prepared or entered is abandoned, nothing half done is left (Bluetooth is put back), and the count restarts. The kill switch fails to the power-off path.
  • RAM budget: hosted and ESP32 builds: a few hundred bytes of statics in the UI (wake and notice state) and the power service (policy state, 4 bytes of flags); the setting sits in the padding of ui_state_t. Pico 2 W: 0 (compiled out). Measured sizes are in the pull request.
  • Unverified on the device (the owner does the bench step with the unit on battery): that mem behaves as early suspend or as a plain suspend, that the key, touch and ring nodes wake the system, that the panel and backlight come back after on (the display HAL re-pushes the whole picture and re-writes the backlight on wake), the Bluetooth chip's power cycle, the real draw in suspend, and the length of the whole cycle. See docs/bench.md.
  • Tests: power_policy (every rule, the wrap, a stamp ahead, a clock that jumps back), ui_frame_keys (the screen's part of the sequence with fakes), y2_suspend (kill switch, sysfs writes, ioctl numbers, the verdicts from the clocks), y2_power (external power), and the host tours power_tour, power_off_tour, power_nosuspend_tour, power_charger_tour, power_battery_tour.

docs.title: ADR-0022: One player UI on every device and app
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner decision 24 Nov 2026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: neuPod runs on several targets: the Pico 2 W rig, the Waveshare RP2350 and ESP32-S3 AMOLED dev boards, the Y2 testbed and the desktop simulator, with the final RP2350B board to come. It also runs as a phone app (mobile/, iOS and Android). Each of these differs in screen size, input, memory and platform services. Without a rule, each port drifts into its own UI. The phone app already follows a narrower version of this rule ("firmware behaviour is law", docs/app/TEAM-BRIEF.md). This ADR makes it the rule for the whole project.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• There is one neuPod UI. Every device and every app shares the same player: screens, menus and navigation, the wheel and its acceleration, the letter jump, list contents and sort order, the text shown, Now Playing, album art choice and Cover Flow. Someone who knows one neuPod knows them all.
  • The firmware is the reference. app/ui, app/audio and app/library define the behaviour. Other implementations, such as the phone app, port it exactly and check the port against the compiled C (vectors, snapshots). Where the firmware is silent, the owner decides, and the decision is written down for every target.
  • Differences are allowed only for hardware or platform reasons, and only at the edges of the player:
  • screen size and density: the resolution profiles of ADR-0018;
  • input: click wheel, touch, side keys;
  • memory: for example, the frozen Pico 2 W keeps a 64 x 64 art thumbnail and has no Cover Flow;
  • radios and peripherals present: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, battery gauge;
  • platform services: lock-screen controls, notifications, OS permissions, where the music lives.
  • A difference is a setting or a build option, not a redesign. It is named where it lives (a CMake option, a setting, a platform adapter) and documented on that target's page. It changes what is available, not how the player behaves. A feature the hardware cannot support is left out or greyed out. It is not replaced by a different design.
  • Changes land everywhere. A change to the player UI goes into the firmware and every app that ports it, or the gap is recorded as a backlog item for each target that lacks it. A gap with no hardware reason is a bug to close, not a difference to keep.
  • App-only surfaces use the device's look. Where an app needs something the device has no screen for (a folder picker, a permission prompt, an OS setting), it uses the device's visual language and wording.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RAM budget: none. This is a rule about behaviour; each feature's ADR still carries its own budget, and memory is a valid reason for a difference.
  • Reviews of UI changes check every target, not just the one the change was made on. A PR that changes the player on one target names the matching change or backlog item for the others.
  • Known gap today: the ESP32-S3 and RP2350 AMOLED dev-board builds use the Pico's small art thumbnail and have no Cover Flow, because NEUPOD_ART_HIRES is on only for hosted builds. Where a board has the memory (PSRAM), this is a gap to close, not a hardware difference.

docs.title: ADR-0023: Reuse the donor headphone jack flex; park optical S/PDIF
docs.text: Status: accepted (4 Nov 2026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The 6G headphone flex carries a 3.5 mm TRRS jack (CTIA/Apple order: Tip L, Ring 1 R, Ring 2 ground, Sleeve mic), the hold switch and the "Mikey" inline-remote decoder (I²C 0x72). The requirements asked for a single jack serving headphones and line level, mono/stereo recording, and an optional mini-TOSLINK optical output in the Apple style. The case hole is sized for the donor jack.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Reuse the donor flex and jack. No new jack on the board; the board carries the flex's FPC connector (pitch measured from the donor).
  2. Inline remote is decoded either by Mikey over I²C (as Rockbox does) or by biasing the mic conductor (~2.2 kΩ to 2.0–2.7 V) and reading an ADC: centre ≈ 0 Ω, vol+ ≈ 240 Ω, vol− ≈ 620 Ω. Plug detect from the jack switch or Mikey.
  3. Recording is mono mic through the jack. Stereo line-in on the same jack is possible only by switching the L/R conductors to the codec ADC with a dual SPDT analogue switch (TS5A23157 class, one GPIO) in a "line-in mode"; whether to fit it is decided with the codec (ADR-0012). Stereo in is otherwise over USB-C audio.
  4. Optical S/PDIF is parked. The combo jack body (Everlight PLT133/T10W class) is taller and longer than the donor jack and cannot share the flex. It returns only if a custom case is made. No GPIO is reserved.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One GPIO freed on every board; the optical parts leave the parts list.
  • Headphone-detect and hold-switch handling stay as in the Rockbox 6G port (hold on a PMU GPIO there; a plain GPIO here).
  • The thin-shell depth constraint no longer depends on the jack.

docs.title: neuPod phone app: specification
docs.text:
A music player for iOS and Android that looks and behaves like a neuPod, and later talks to one.

Status: specification, 21 November 2026. Nothing is built. The working instructions for building it are in TEAM-BRIEF.md and the checklist is PROGRESS.md.

docs.title: Owner decisions (21 November 2026)
docs.text:
1. The app is both a full player on the phone and, later, a companion to a neuPod device.
  2. Music comes from three places, in this order of delivery: files on the phone first; then the owner's NAS; then the card in a neuPod.
  3. Built in Flutter, one codebase for both platforms.
  4. iOS is built and tested for real: the owner has a Mac and an Apple developer account.

Owner decisions in phase 0 (21 November 2026), after the platform research in decisions/:

  1. Ogg Vorbis and Opus on iOS are played through bundled Xiph decoders (libogg, libvorbis, libopus, BSD-3), because iOS has no decoder for them that apps can use.
  2. No Cast in R1. Casting from Android needs the app's own network connection. The output icon covers the phone speaker, wired, Bluetooth and, on iOS, AirPlay (the system does AirPlay's networking).
  3. iCloud files that are not downloaded are listed with a Download action. The app never fetches them itself; a tap asks iOS to download the file.

  4. Platform limits, accepted: on iOS a scan cannot keep running after the app is closed, so it resumes at the next launch (Android keeps going). Tracks from Android's shared music collection get embedded art only, because folder art would need a restricted image permission. Android 11+ cannot pick the storage root or Download, so the folder screen says so. Sample-rate passthrough is best effort and reported, never claimed (Android 14+ USB DACs where the phone supports it, an iOS preferred-rate hint, never over Bluetooth). The active output on Android 10 to 12 is inferred, because there is no public API before Android 13. MP3 and AAC files without encoder-delay metadata cannot be gapless on any engine.

  5. The app is the device (owner, 21 November 2026). The full-screen view is the front of a neuPod: the 4:3 screen above a touch click wheel with the four click buttons (Menu, previous, next, play/pause) and the centre button, in the device's proportions, scaled to the phone's width. Turning the wheel scrolls with haptic detents, and pressing a button or the centre gives a haptic click. It is drawn fresh, never copied from Apple's artwork, with no Apple logo and no "iPod"; the store-review risk stays with the owner at submission (Open question 1). This settles Open question 2 and most of Open question 3.

  6. The wheel sets the volume on Now Playing (owner, 21 November 2026), as on the device, on both platforms. It sets the phone's own system volume (no separate app volume): Android through AudioManager, iOS through a hidden MPVolumeView, the common workaround, since iOS has no public API for it. The device's volume bar replaces the progress bar while the wheel turns. If Apple breaks the workaround, the fallback is to be asked for, not guessed.
  7. Sort rule: the app matches the firmware's code (owner, 21 November 2026), lib_collate_key() in app/library/lib_collate.c, and the rule is written down under The library. The owner may change it later, in the firmware and the app together.
  8. Search is typed with the wheel (owner, 22 November 2026), as text is on the device. It never opens the phone's keyboard. It uses the firmware's text entry in search mode (docs/ui-input.md, model in app/include/wheel_input.h): the letter ring and mode chips, with live results as the user types. The chips are the firmware's six: abc, ABC, 123, #!?, space, del (owner, 22 November 2026; the design drew five, without #!?). The screen is in the device view design, "Search, by the wheel".

  9. Gate 2, first choices (owner, 22 November 2026), from the screenshots of the device view: fit A (the body fills the phone; device view design Open question 1), and the body finish follows the mode (silver in Light, black in Dark) with no separate Silver/Black setting (Open question 5). Also: the phone's own status bar is shown above the device; the neuPod wordmark stays on the body (Open question 8); rating stars live on Now Playing's page 2 only, as a Rating row set with the wheel; Search keeps its 24-character cap.

    Gate 2, remaining choices (owner, 22 November 2026). Device view Open questions: the accessibility text sizes stay capped at 5 rows (3); holding Play/Pause does nothing extra (4); our own proportions stay (6); routes: the phone speaker shows no icon, USB and other wired outputs show the jack plug, and AirPlay and other wireless outputs show a new generic external-speaker icon in the device's style (never Apple's AirPlay glyph) (7); a left-edge swipe is Menu on iOS (9); the click sound is a system sound that follows the ringer switch (10); Search stays in the Music menu (11); Search shows up to three live results, fewer at the larger text tiers (13). UI styles: Classic Light is adjusted to 4.5:1 where the designer's exact values fall short (the selection bar's upper stops under white text, rail letters, ink3 on grey surfaces), and Bluetooth saved versus active gets a cue besides colour; Home's right pane with nothing playing shows a placeholder cover, "Nothing playing" and the song count; tapping a side cover in Cover Flow centres it; the Music menu's preview pane shows for every item, not only Albums. Settings: the list under Settings plus the click sound switch (off by default) and a haptics switch. Direct touch (device view Open question 2) and drag-to-seek were judged by feel on the owner's phones at gate 1 and are settled by decision 18: candidate 2 (wheel plus screen), and the progress bar is not draggable. 14. Cover Flow matches the device (owner, 22 November 2026). Cover Flow is a second view of the Albums list, as on the device (app/ui/ui_library.c, LB-6 in the UI review): the same albums in the same order (by title, the firmware's Albums list order), not by artist then year. Under the centred album's title it shows the device's caption in both styles, Artist · Year · n songs as flow_texts builds it: no artist for a compilation, no year when there is none, 1 song or n songs, and no count when there are none. This replaces "albums by artist then year" here and the UI styles mock-ups' song count in Modern only. 15. Untagged files match the device (owner, 23 November 2026). A file's missing tags fall back as the firmware's library builder does (index_file in app/library/lib_build.c, ADR 0017 D5): the album is the name of the folder holding the file, the artist is Unknown Artist, and the title is the whole file name, extension included (01 Dust.flac). Nothing else is read from the path: there is no Artist/Year Album/NN Title.ext parsing (no artist, year or track number from folder or file names) and no , The handling of folder names. Album names or folders that differ only by (Disc n) stay separate albums. This replaces the folder-convention fallback proposed here. 16. Custom mode (owner, 25 November 2026). The mode setting becomes Light, Dark, Auto, Custom. Light, Dark and Auto are unchanged. Custom sets the colour and the transparency of the body, the wheel and the centre button separately, with a colour wheel as the picker; a custom look carries its own screen choice (Light, Dark or Auto); where a part is see-through a picture of a neuPod board shows from underneath, chosen from a small built-in set (only neuPod's own boards, never Apple's). Style stays a separate setting and works with all four modes. Three starter looks ship: Harbour, Sea glass and Clear case. The design is Custom mode (backlog AP-1); its other recommendations are proposals until the owner confirms them. 17. Nothing scrolls (owner, 25 November 2026). The app always fits the phone's screen and never shows a scroll bar, vertical or horizontal. Inside the device's 4:3 screen, new screens avoid scrolling too where they can. 18. Gate 1: touch and seek (owner, 22 to 23 November 2026), after the slice ran on an iPhone 15 Pro and a Pixel 7. Direct touch is candidate 2: the wheel plus taps and drags on the screen. Candidate 1 (wheel only) is removed. Seeking is by the wheel's seek mode only: the progress bar is not draggable. The iPhone survives a restart, the wheel feel and haptics are right, and the wheel sets the volume on Now Playing. 19. Unplayable songs (owner, 25 November 2026), from PR #159. A song is unplayable when the device would mark it damaged or the phone's player cannot decode it. Its row follows the UI styles design: greyed, with the reason at the right (Damaged file, Opus, can't play), and no toasts (the device today shows the codec and toasts the reason; the firmware follows the same design later). The selection bar lands on it, as on the device, and Select opens nothing. Unplayable songs are left out of the queue, so none stops it, and Shuffle Songs never starts on one (backlog UI-24 for the device). 20. Ratings and play counts (owner, 25 November 2026), from PR #160 (decision 0011). - Identity: a track's ratings and play counts are keyed as on the device, by the file's path and size, and a rescan that sees a file move (the old path gone and one new file with the same audio fingerprint) carries them to the new key. The fingerprint has no tag bytes in it, so a retag that changes the size carries them too (FLAC, MP3, MP4/M4A, WAV; Ogg, Opus and raw AAC files are not opened by the scanner, as on the device, and get no carry-over). - Skip counts are dropped for now, on the app and the device (the firmware has none). - Backups: ratings and play counts are kept in their own small database, which iCloud and Google backups include; the library database, which a rescan rebuilds, stays out of backups. 21. Android's shared music collection (owner, 26 November 2026), from PR #162 (decision 0012). - Duplicates: a file inside a picked folder is listed once, by the folder; the collection leaves it out. Adding or removing a folder over songs already listed carries their ratings and play counts to the new path (decision 20's carry-over). - Music only: the collection lists what Android marks as music (IS_MUSIC); ringtones, notification and alarm sounds, recordings and podcasts are left out. - Words: Settings > Library shows Add Music on This Phone while it is off; once on, it is listed as a folder is, as Music on This Phone, with Turn Off where a folder has Remove (asking first, as Remove does).

Everything else in this document is the designer's proposal until the owner confirms it. Proposals that most need a decision are collected under Open questions.

docs.title: What it is for
docs.text:
The owner is re-ripping about 300 CDs to FLAC as the library for the neuPod. The app gives the same library, the same menus and the same look on the phone he already carries, and becomes the easy way to manage a neuPod once the device has a network interface.

Goals

  • Play a large lossless library from the phone, gaplessly, in the background, with the controls people expect on the lock screen and on headsets.
  • Feel like a neuPod: the same menu structure, vocabulary and visual styles (Classic and Modern), adapted to touch and to a portrait screen.
  • Work fully offline with no account.

Not goals

  • Streaming services, a store, social features, recommendations, lyrics, podcasts (podcasts are a later device feature).
  • Video.
  • Editing tags or files. The app reads the library; it never changes the owner's music files.
  • Tablets and desktop layouts in the first release.

It has failed if

  • it ever alters, moves or deletes a music file without being asked;
  • playback gaps between tracks of a continuous album, or stops when the screen locks;
  • it sends anything about the library off the phone;
  • it looks like a generic player with a neuPod logo on it.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Release What it adds Depends on R1: local player Everything in this document's "R1" sections: files on the phone, library, playback, both styles Nothing. This is the work to do now. R2: NAS Browse, stream and download from a home server An owner decision on the server (see Open questions); R1 R3: companion Find a neuPod on the network, browse and play its card, send music and playlists to it, remote control, device settings The device's HTTP API, which does not exist yet (it is step W2 in Wi-Fi); R1

R2 and R3 are outlined at the end so R1 is built with room for them. They are not to be started without the owner.

docs.title: Getting music onto the phone
docs.text:
• Android: the user picks one or more folders with the system folder picker; the app keeps read access to them. It also offers the device's shared music collection.
  • iOS: the app has its own Documents folder, visible in the Files app and in Finder when the phone is plugged into a Mac, so a library is copied in by dragging folders. The user can also pick a folder elsewhere in Files (for example on iCloud Drive or an attached drive) and the app keeps access to it.
  • The app never copies music it can read in place, and never writes into a music folder.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text: Must play: FLAC (up to 24-bit / 192 kHz), ALAC, MP3, AAC (M4A), WAV, Opus and Ogg Vorbis. These match the device's required codecs. A file the platform cannot decode is listed greyed with the reason at the right (Opus, can't play), exactly as the device does; it is never hidden and never stops the queue.

docs.title: The library
docs.text:
• Built by scanning the chosen folders and reading tags: title, artist, album artist, album, track and disc number, year, genre, compilation flag, duration, sample rate and bit depth, embedded art.
  • Where tags are missing, the device's fallback (owner decision 15): the album is the folder's name, the artist Unknown Artist, the title the whole file name (extension included); nothing else is taken from the path. Folder.jpg (or cover.jpg) is the album art.
  • The discs of one album (one album tag, disc number tags) are one album with disc sections, as on the device; album names or folders that differ only by (Disc n) stay apart, as there.
  • A track whose album artist is Various Artists, or whose compilation flag is set, belongs to Compilations and is not listed under each contributing artist's albums.
  • The scan runs in the background, shows progress, can be cancelled, and survives the app being closed (on iOS it resumes at the next launch; owner decision 8). A rescan only reads files that are new or changed. Removing a folder removes its tracks from the library and nothing else.
  • Sizing target: 20,000 tracks. First scan of 5,000 FLAC files in under five minutes on a mid-range phone; a rescan with no changes in under ten seconds. (Targets are proposals; measure and report.)
  • Sort rule (owner decision 11): names sort by a collation key built as the firmware's lib_collate_key() does. A sort tag is used when present, otherwise the name. One leading article is skipped, in any case, when something follows it: The, A or An ("The Beatles" under B, "A Perfect Circle" under P). Letters compare without case and with accents folded. Order: symbols first, then digits, then letters. The fast-scroll letter is the first letter of the key, # for a digit or symbol. docs/ui.md still says "A "/"An " are not skipped; the code is the reference until the owner changes both.
  • Ratings (0 to 5), play counts and last played are kept per track in the app's own database, keyed as on the device (path and size), and survive a rescan, a file move within the library and a retag; that database is in phone backups (owner decision 20). Skip counts were dropped (owner decision 20: the device has none).

docs.title: Browsing
docs.text:
The same structure as the device:

  • Home: Music, Playlists, Settings, Shuffle Songs, Now Playing (only while something is loaded).
  • Music: Cover Flow, Playlists, Artists, Albums, Songs, Genres, Compilations.
  • An artist: All Songs, then the albums with cover, year and song count.
  • An album: header with the cover, artist, year, song count and total time; numbered tracks, with disc headings.
  • Songs: two lines per row, title over artist and album.
  • Cover Flow: a second view of the Albums list, in its order (by title), with the device's caption Artist · Year · n songs under the centred album (owner decision 14); the centred album opens on tap.
  • Fast scroll: a letter index on long lists.
  • Search, typed with the wheel (owner decision 12): the field, the letter ring turned by the wheel with the mode chips under it, and the best matches live as the user types; Play/Pause goes to the full results, grouped as artists, albums and songs, and Menu returns to typing with the text kept. It never opens the phone's keyboard.

Long names end in an ellipsis in lists and scroll as a ticker where the device scrolls them (the focused title on Now Playing).

docs.title: Playback
docs.text:
• A play queue with Play, Play Next and Add to Queue from any track, album, artist, genre or playlist. The queue is visible and can be reordered and cleared.
  • Gapless between consecutive tracks of the same format; verified by test, not by ear alone.
  • Shuffle (off, on) and repeat (off, all, one), with the same glyphs as the device's status bar.
  • Seek with the wheel's seek mode; the progress bar is not draggable (owner decision 18). Skip back restarts the track after three seconds, otherwise goes to the previous one.
  • Background playback with lock-screen and notification controls, artwork and scrubbing; headset and Bluetooth transport buttons; correct behaviour on interruptions (a call pauses; unplugging headphones pauses; another app taking audio pauses).
  • Resume: reopening the app restores the queue, the track and the position.
  • Volume is the phone's own volume. The app has no volume of its own; on Now Playing the wheel sets the system volume and shows the device's volume bar (owner decision 10).
  • The output in use (phone speaker, wired, Bluetooth or AirPlay) is shown by an icon, as on the device. No Cast in R1 (owner decision 6).
  • No resampling or processing in the app. Where the platform lets the app pass the file's sample rate through to an external DAC, do so and say what was achieved in the format line; do not claim bit-perfect output that has not been measured.

docs.title: Playlists
docs.text:
• On-The-Go: add from any row; reorder; clear; save as a named playlist.
  • Named playlists: create, rename, reorder, delete.
  • Import and export .m3u8, with paths relative to the library folder, so playlists can move between the phone and a neuPod's card.

docs.title: Now Playing
docs.text: Art, title, artist, album and year, the small format line (FLAC 16/44.1), progress with elapsed and remaining, shuffle and repeat, rating stars, and a route to the queue. In Modern the backdrop and the accent come from the album art, by the same rule as the device: the dominant colour, clamped until white text on it reaches 4.5:1.

docs.title: Look and feel
docs.text:
• Two styles, Classic and Modern, each in Light and Dark, with the colours and skins in the UI styles design. Mode follows the phone's setting by default; style is chosen in Settings.
  • Custom mode (owner decision 16). A fourth mode in which the user sets the colour and transparency of the body, the wheel and the centre button, with a board picture showing through a see-through part. The editor, the rule that keeps the legends at 4.5:1 on any colour, the board pictures and the data model are in the Custom mode design.
  • The device view (owner decision 9). The phone shows the device's front: the 4:3 screen, running the device's screens with the UI styles design's values (drawn at 600x450, so they carry over), above the click wheel. The wheel behaves as on the device: turning scrolls, with acceleration and the fast-scroll letter tile on long lists; the centre is Select; Menu goes back; previous, next and play/pause work as on the device, including press-and-hold to scan. Each wheel detent is a light haptic tick, and each button press is a firmer haptic click. An optional click sound, like the original's clicker, can be turned on in Settings.
  • The layout and the wheel's numbers are in the device view design: geometry as ratios of the phone's width, the fit on tall and short phones, body finishes, hit zones, press-or-turn, detents and acceleration (a port of the firmware's ui_accel_feed()), holds, haptics, direct touch, the three text tiers, accessibility and the phone's status bar. Its recommendations (the fit, the body finish, direct touch, the phone's status bar shown, the large-text tiers, the wordmark) were proposals for the owner, settled at gate 2 (owner decision 13); direct touch and drag-to-seek were settled at gate 1 (owner decision 18).
  • Search is typed with the wheel's letter ring, never the phone's keyboard (owner decision 12). It sits in the Music menu (device view design Open question 11, owner decision 13).
  • Type is Montserrat (SIL OFL), icons are Lucide (ISC), as on the device. Every third-party asset and package is listed on an in-app Licences screen.
  • Feedback follows the device's three places where they translate: a row confirms with a brief flash and a tick; a greyed row carries its reason; something lost or about to be lost gets a centred panel. No toasts for routine things.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Style; mode (Light, Dark, Auto, Custom; owner decision 16); Custom look, the list of up to six custom looks and their editor (Custom mode design); library folders (add, remove, rescan); gapless on or off; skip-back behaviour; click sound (off by default, as the device view design says); haptics (the design's rule: off whenever the phone's own setting is off); reset ratings and play counts (with a panel to confirm); About; Licences (owner decision 13).

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text: The wheel and buttons have screen-reader equivalents (the list is navigable row by row, and the wheel is an adjustable control with actions for Select, Menu, previous, next and play/pause). Every control has a screen-reader label; the app honours the system text size up to the largest standard setting without clipping; text contrast is at least 4.5:1 in every style and mode; nothing depends on colour alone; touch targets are at least 44 points.

docs.title: Privacy and safety
docs.text:
• R1 makes no network connection at all. No analytics, no crash reporting service, no accounts. iOS downloading an iCloud file after the user taps Download (owner decision 7), and AirPlay (decision 6), are the system's networking, not the app's.
  • The app requests only the permissions it needs to read the chosen folders, play in the background, show media controls and, on Android, show the background library scan's notification (decision 0009).
  • Signing keys, provisioning profiles and store credentials are never committed. The repository is public.

docs.title: How it is built
docs.text:
• Flutter, current stable, one codebase in mobile/ at the repository root. Licence MPL-2.0, like the firmware.
  • Layers, each testable without the ones above it: a pure-Dart domain (library model, queue, shuffle and repeat rules, sorting and naming rules); data (database, scanner, tag reader, art cache); audio (the player and the platform media session); UI.
  • Packages (audio engine, media session, tag reading, database, state management) are the team's choice. Each choice is recorded in a short decision note with the alternatives considered. A package must be actively maintained, licensed compatibly with MPL-2.0 distribution on both stores, and checked against its current documentation, not chosen from memory.
  • The domain rules that the device also implements (sort order, the untagged fallback, compilation rules, queue behaviour) follow the firmware's behaviour as documented in UI and the ADRs, so a library looks the same in both.

docs.title: How it is tested
docs.text:
Level What Where Unit Domain rules, scanner, tag fallbacks, playlist import and export, the accent-colour rule Every PR Widget and golden Every screen in Classic and Modern, Light and Dark, at a small and a large phone size and at the largest text size Every PR Integration Pick a folder, scan, browse, play, background, resume; on an Android emulator and an iOS simulator Every PR (CI: Linux for Android, a Mac runner for iOS) Audio Decode each fixture in tests/assets/audio and compare with its checksum where the platform allows; gapless join measured on a generated two-track fixture CI where possible, otherwise the bench Device The owner's iPhone and an Android phone: real library, lock screen, headset buttons, Bluetooth, interruptions, an hour of continuous play End of each phase, recorded with the date Scale A generated 20,000-track library: scan time, memory, scroll smoothness End of the library phase

The repository's audio fixtures (tests/assets/audio) are reused; a generated library with the owner's folder convention and awkward names is added for scanner tests. The owner's own music is never committed.

docs.title: R2 outline: NAS
docs.text: Browse and play from a home server; download albums for offline use; show clearly what is on the phone and what is remote. R1 keeps the library model source-neutral (a track has a source and a location) so this is an addition, not a rewrite. The server type is an open question.

docs.title: R3 outline: companion
docs.text: Discover a neuPod on the local network; show its battery, storage and what it is playing; remote control; browse and play its card; send albums and playlists to it and remove them; exchange ratings and play counts; set its settings; later, firmware update. All of this needs the device's HTTP API. That API is to be specified in an ADR written with the firmware, not invented by the app. Wi-Fi currently describes that step as "device HTTP API and a C# companion app for library sync"; whether a separate desktop companion is still wanted is an open question.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
Not decided. Do not settle these by guessing.

# Question Proposal 1 App name and store listing. A music player whose name contains "Pod" may meet trademark objections at store review. Not legal advice; the owner should take a view before submitting Build as "neuPod"; nothing is submitted to a store without the owner 2 An on-screen click wheel. Apps that reproduce the original wheel have been removed from the App Store: Rewound, a click-wheel iPod skin for the iPhone, was pulled in December 2019 (MacRumors), and the App Review Guidelines bar apps "confusingly similar to an existing Apple product, interface … or advertising theme" (cited as 5.2.5). Store review is the owner's risk at submission (Open questions 1 and 9) Decided 2026-11-21 (owner decision 9): a touch click wheel with haptics, in a drawn-fresh device view 3 Portrait layout: the split Home with the art pane, the status bar, where Now Playing lives (a full screen, or a mini-player above a tab bar) Mostly settled by owner decision 9: the screen is the device's 4:3 screen. How the device fits tall and short phones is decided at the design gate 4 Bundle and application ID Decided 2026-11-21: net.stuartfraser.neupod 5 Minimum OS versions Decided 2026-11-21: iOS 18 and later; Android 10 (API 29) and later 6 Which Android phone is the test device Decided 2026-11-21: the owner's Pixel (model and version to be recorded) 7 NAS type for R2: a Jellyfin-style server, plain SMB, or WebDAV Ask when R1 is done 8 Desktop C# companion in the Wi-Fi plan: still wanted alongside the phone app? Ask when R3 is planned 9 Distribution: TestFlight and an internal Android track only, or public store releases TestFlight and sideloaded APK until the owner decides 10 Sync of ratings and play counts between phone and device R3
