You are the designer for neuPod, an open-source music player (repo: StuartF303/neuPod, public). You already produced the firmware UI styles design in docs/design/2026-11-21-ui-styles/ (README with exact values, HTML mock-ups at 600x450 and their PNGs). Now design the phone app's device view: the layout framework the app team will build the iOS and Android app on. Work in the same way and the same format as that folder.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
• docs/app/README.md: the app specification, especially owner decisions 9 to 11 ("The app is the device", wheel volume, sort rule), Look and feel, Browsing, Now Playing, Accessibility, and Open questions 1 and 3.
  • docs/design/2026-11-21-ui-styles/README.md and its mockups/: Classic Light and Modern Dark, the status bar, the three feedback places, the music screens. These run unchanged inside the app's 4:3 screen.
  • docs/ui.md (wheel behaviour, acceleration, fast scroll, Now Playing seek and volume as built in the firmware) and docs/adr/0004-donor-ipod-classic-6g.md (the physical device's shell).

docs.title: The owner's decision (21 November 2026)
docs.text: The app's full-screen view is the front of a neuPod: the 4:3 screen above a touch click wheel with the four click buttons (Menu, previous, next, play/pause) and the centre button, in the device's proportions, scaled to the phone's width. Turning the wheel scrolls with haptic detents, and presses give a haptic click. On Now Playing the wheel sets the phone's system volume and shows the device's volume bar. Search opens the phone's keyboard.

docs.title: Hard rules
docs.text:
• Drawn fresh. No Apple logo, no "iPod" anywhere, nothing traced or copied from Apple's product photography or artwork. Our own geometry, our own rendering, the neuPod name. The button glyphs are Lucide (ISC) or drawn for this design; the type is Montserrat (SIL OFL).
  • The screen content is the existing UI styles design: do not redesign the screens, only how they sit in the device.
  • Contrast at least 4.5:1 for text; nothing by colour alone; touch targets at least 44 pt.

docs.title: What to produce
docs.text:
A new folder, docs/design/<date>-app-device-view/, with a README giving decisions, rules and exact values, plus mockups/ as standalone HTML and PNG. Draw at three phone sizes in points: 375x667 (short, home button), 393x852 (common), 440x956 (large), plus the largest-text variant where it matters.

  1. Device geometry. Body outline, corner radii, and the 4:3 screen rectangle with its bezel. All expressed as ratios of the phone's width so the app can lay it out at any size. State the scale from the 600x450 screen designs to the on-phone screen, and the minimum the screen may shrink to.
  2. Fitting the phone. How the device sits on tall and on short phones, with the safe areas, notch, Dynamic Island, home indicator and Android gesture bar. Draw two candidates: the body stretched to fill the height, and the device at its true proportions with the surround filled. Say what the surround is in each style and mode.
  3. Body finishes. One per style and mode drawn (Classic Light, Modern Dark), and a rule for the missing ones (Classic Dark and Modern Light are not designed yet; UI styles Open question 1). Whether the body follows the style and mode, or is a separate setting.
  4. The click wheel. Diameter and centre-button diameter as ratios. The four button positions and glyphs. The hit zones, including the dead band between the ring and the centre, and the angle that counts as a press versus a turn. Visual states: idle, finger down on the ring, button pressed, centre pressed, disabled.
  5. Wheel behaviour, as numbers the engineers can implement.
  6. Degrees per detent, i.e. per list step.
  7. The acceleration curve matching the firmware's, and when the fast-scroll letter tile appears.
  8. Press-and-hold times for previous and next (scan) and for play/pause.
  9. Which haptic fires on what: detent tick vs press click, and the iOS and Android haptic styles to use.
  10. The optional click sound.
  11. What a two-finger or edge touch does.
  12. Direct touch on the screen. Two candidates: the wheel only, or the wheel plus tapping rows and dragging lists on the screen. Draw how each looks when used, and give your recommendation.
  13. Screens in the device. Home, Songs (a long list with the letter tile), an album with disc headings, Cover Flow, Now Playing (at rest, while the wheel sets volume, and in seek), a centred panel, and Search with the keyboard up (where the device goes when the keyboard covers the wheel). Each in Classic Light and Modern Dark, at 393x852, using real names from the existing mock-ups.
  14. Largest text size. How the 4:3 screen honours the phone's largest standard text setting without clipping. The proposal is fewer, larger rows; draw it and give the row counts per size.
  15. Accessibility. How VoiceOver and TalkBack users drive it: row-by-row navigation, and the wheel as an adjustable control with named actions for Select, Menu, previous, next and play/pause. The labels to use.
  16. The phone's own status bar vs the device's status bar: whether the phone's is hidden, shown above the device, or merged. Recommend one.

End the README with Open questions, as the UI styles README does: anything for the owner to decide, each with what you drew meanwhile. Do not settle owner questions by guessing.

docs.text:
App code, the firmware, the store listing, and R2 and R3. When you're done, the app team builds the design-gate screens from this folder (docs/app/TEAM-BRIEF.md, gate 2) and the owner chooses between your candidates on real screens.

docs.title: Set-up notes
docs.text:
• scripts/app/bootstrap-mac.sh --no-agent finishes cleanly. On the first run, brew install failed with "Cannot link ca-certificates" and then "Cannot link ruby", because Homebrew had left an old version of each package (and of libevent, libunistring, pcre2 and utf8proc) beside the new one. brew cleanup <formula> on each fixed it.
  • The temurin@17 cask runs a .pkg installer that needs the owner's password, which can't be typed at an ssh prompt without a terminal. It was run in a separate tmux window and the owner typed the password there.
  • iOS CI runs on GitHub-hosted macOS runners.

docs.title: Goldens (screenshot tests)
docs.text:
The golden PNGs under mobile/test/ui/{components,screens,device}/goldens are made and compared on one machine only: the goldens job of .github/workflows/app.yml, on the GitHub-hosted macos-26 image (the label the ios job uses, never -latest). Text rasterises differently on Linux and on each macOS release: after the build Mac moved from macOS 26.5 to 27.2.1, every component and screen golden made on 26.5 failed there by 0.00 to 0.21 % of its pixels, all on glyph edges, while the runner (macOS 26.7.2) reproduced 144 of them byte for byte (2026-11-22). So a local Mac is not the reference.

  • In CI the goldens job runs flutter test test/ui/components test/ui/screens test/ui/device/goldens with NEUPOD_GOLDENS=compare and fails on any mismatch. On failure it uploads the golden-failures artifact (each failed golden's master, test and diff images). It is one of the jobs app-gate waits for.
  • The Linux check job runs the same tests without comparing pixels (overflow and exceptions still fail them).
  • Locally, flutter test doesn't compare golden pixels and prints a note saying so. NEUPOD_GOLDENS=compare flutter test ... compares them, but a failure of about 0.1 % on glyph edges can be your Mac, not the app. --update-goldens writes nothing outside GitHub Actions.
  • The job summary and the "Runner image" step log the image version (ImageVersion), which changes under the macos-26 label when GitHub updates the image. If every golden suddenly fails by about 0.1 % on glyph edges with no app change, compare it with the run that made the PNGs and regenerate.

To regenerate (after an intended UI change, or an image update):

  1. Push the branch, then run the workflow by hand with the input set: gh workflow run app.yml --ref <branch> -f update_goldens=true (or Actions > app > Run workflow, tick update_goldens). Only the goldens job runs, about 2 minutes. CI never pushes commits.
  2. Download the goldens artifact: gh run download <run-id> -n goldens -D /tmp/goldens. It keeps the paths below mobile/test (ui/components/goldens, ui/screens/goldens, ui/device/goldens).
  3. Copy it over the tree: cp -R /tmp/goldens/. mobile/test/, check git status and look at every changed PNG (only the screens you meant to change should differ), then commit them (test(app): regenerate goldens ...) and push. The next PR run's goldens job compares against them.

Never commit failures/ folders.

docs.title: State of main
docs.text:
• Phases 0 to 2 done; gate 1 and gate 2 closed. Gate 1 (owner decision 18): direct touch is candidate 2 (wheel plus taps and drags), seek is by the wheel's seek mode only, the progress bar is not draggable. Candidate 1 and the drag switch are gone from the code. The owner ran the slice on an iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 27.2.1) and a Pixel 7 (Android 17).
  • Phase 3 (library), mostly done: tags (FLAC, MP3, M4A, WAV), embedded art and the art cache, firmware collation, source-neutral tracks, background scan with progress, cancel, Android foreground service, incremental rescan, folder removal, generated test library, read-only guarantee, discs and compilations.
  • Phase 3 remaining (all unticked in PROGRESS): Android shared music collection; iCloud files that are not downloaded (Download action, scan never hangs); ratings, play counts, last played and skip counts that survive a rescan (a user-owned table with a real migration and the guard test updated; add the confirmation noted on the folder item); unplayable files greyed with a reason; the 20,000-track scale test (DriftLibraryView loads every row per read, give it real queries first); the phase 3 device check.
  • Merged since the last handoff: #141 to #150 (library), #154 (Spec Kit pilot spec), #155 (Custom mode design).

docs.title: Open owner decisions
docs.text:
From Custom mode, Open questions (nothing built yet; AP-1, progress in that folder's PROGRESS.md):

  1. Custom look row always shown under Mode, or only while Mode is Custom.
  2. Board pictures: which boards, rendered or photographed, by when (boards/ is empty, so it cannot ship without one).
  3. The starter looks' exact colours (Harbour, Sea glass, Clear case).
  4. Six looks, as the no-scroll rule gives.
  5. Largest text: looks list and a look's rows move with the wheel, or split over two screens.
  6. Settings is at seven rows; group the rest (Playback, About)?
  7. Most transparency: 85 % body, 60 % wheel and centre.
  8. Wordmark badge on a see-through body, or no wordmark.
  9. Android status bar ink on a mid-tone body.
  10. Clashing with Modern's art-led accent.
  11. Does a real neuPod ever need to know the look (companion, R3).

docs.title: Device builds
docs.text:
The owner's iPhone and Pixel are the targets. Team ID for iOS signing: the owner's personal team, set locally; never commit it. From mobile/, one heavy build at a time through ~/bin/neupod-buildlock:

  1. flutter build ios --config-only --no-codesign
  2. xcodebuild on ios/Runner.xcworkspace (scheme Runner, Release or Debug) with DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<team> and -allowProvisioningUpdates.
  3. xcrun devicectl device install app --device <id> <Runner.app>.

Android: flutter build apk and adb install. Delete mobile/build and .dart_tool afterwards.

docs.title: Spec Kit pilot
docs.text: specs/001-amoled-full-art (UI-25, full album art on the AMOLED boards: spec, plan, tasks; speckit-* skills, .specify/). It is firmware work, not the app. Tasks are all unticked. It is a pilot of the method; judge it after the first feature is through.

docs.title: Known flaky things
docs.text:
• Network. DNS to github.com sometimes fails, which breaks the sqlite3 native-assets download during flutter test or a build. Retry; nothing is wrong with the code.
  • iOS CI timeout. On #150 a slow macOS runner took 17 minutes to build and the 40-minute job was cancelled mid-tests. The ios job is now 60 minutes (the Integration tests step keeps its own 25). If it still cancels, read the step times before raising anything.
  • Check that "green" means tests ran: confirm counts are real, not all skipped.

docs.title: How the lead works
docs.text:
• Merge only after gh pr checks <n> --watch shows every check passing on the reviewed head. Squash-merge once green (standing OK). Never force-push or rebase; never pipe gh pr merge through tail or grep.
  • Every subagent brief says "do not run gh pr merge" and "never kill processes you didn't start".
  • Check what agents claim (files exist, test counts real). Re-review fix commits of native, firmware-port and data-safety code.
  • Models: Opus for native code, exact firmware ports, data safety, hard CI and their reviews; Sonnet for UI from exact specs, tests and docs; Haiku for mechanical chores.
  • Goldens are regenerated only in CI: gh workflow run app.yml --ref <branch> -f update_goldens=true, then download the artifact (docs/app/ENVIRONMENT.md "Goldens"). Never locally.
  • The build Mac has 8 GB RAM and a small disk: ~/bin/neupod-buildlock <command>, delete mobile/build and .dart_tool after, remove merged worktrees.
  • Branch protection on main: PR required (0 approvals), firmware jobs required, enforce admins, no force-push.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
(One line per thing the next session must know. Newest first.)

  • 2026-11-26: Scale test and spec suites (feat/app-scale-and-spec-suite). test/spec now runs with no skips: every suite is wired to the app (wheel acceleration and touch, text tiers and screen scale, the library rules over the drift library view, the scanner over a generated folder through test/support/host_library.dart, a dart:io storage root that skips hidden names as both platforms' walks do). Where a spec test disagreed it was changed to the firmware or the owner's decisions: an untagged file's title is its file name and (Disc n) names stay two albums (decision 15), an album without track numbers is in title order (alb_cmp). WheelInput.turnedPositions was added for the touch suite. The generator's "untagged" ALAC file was really tagged (the fixture has tags); it now strips them with the new M4A tag writer. Scale test: decision 0013.

  • 2026-11-26: iCloud follow-ups (lead calls under owner decisions 7 and 19, decision 0004). A queued song that iOS has evicted since it was queued is skipped, as an unplayable song is: neupod_audio's engine checks the file's download state from metadata (LocalFile.swift: placeholder, downloading status, dataless flag) before it opens the current or the pre-scheduled next item, and fails it as Not downloaded, so AVFoundation never fetches it; the lock screen's embedded art is read only from a file on the phone. neupod_audio's privacy manifest now declares the file timestamp API (lstat, 3B52.1 and C617.1). Search: its index was already rebuilt after a finished scan (searchFunctionProvider watches the library view); its rows now also read Downloading once asked for, as the lists do. requestDownload has a 30 s Dart timeout; the plugin's notes of old downloading errors are dropped once a request settles and capped at 256.

  • 2026-11-25: iCloud files not downloaded (owner decision 7, decision 0004). Lead call, UI: the Download action is Select on the greyed Not downloaded row itself (the device has no row buttons and decision 19 puts the reason on the row); its reason then reads Downloading until the scan finds the file. No new screen, menu or control. The device has no iCloud, so this is a platform difference (constitution I), iOS only. Follow-ups done in the next PR (below). LibraryLoader now loads again when a finished scan rebuilds the library view, so an open list shows what the scan found.

  • 2026-11-25: Android shared music collection (#162, decision 0012): neupod_storage addSharedCollection() and root kind sharedCollection (id mediastore:audio); the walk is one MediaStore query (IS_MUSIC != 0, all external volumes), entries open through openFd like SAF documents. No schema change (sources.kind media_store). The scanner leaves out a collection item inside a picked folder (tree URI to volume and path, lib/data/scan/shared_collection.dart), as owner decision 21 chose (26 Nov). Android integration test media_store_test.dart: the instrumentation rule in MainActivityTest.java grants the permission and inserts a WAV only when neupodSeedMediaStore=true (the script passes it for that file); CI step and job timeouts raised for the 7th file. The permission dialog itself is not driven in CI.

  • 2026-11-25: Ratings and play counts (decision 0011, owner decision 20; library schema version 5 adds tracks.audio_fingerprint, scan version 6; the new stats.sqlite is schema version 1 and is in phone backups through neupod_storage backedUpDataPath() and the Android backup rules): the firmware's play tracker, rating and plays rules are ported and checked against vectors from the compiled C (scripts/app/gen-plays-vectors.sh, a CI step diffs them). Follow-ups: the audio engineer to report a track start from neupod_audio (a restart of the same queue entry, Previous after 3 s or repeat one, is not a new start yet, so not counted again); Most played, Top rated, Unplayed and Settings > Reset ratings and play counts (phase 6) read track_stats; the star colours differ from the device's (accent and line grey there; filled and outlined in the inks here), a UI styles question for the owner. make-migrations cannot read _testVersion ?? n: write the bare number while it runs (comment on schemaVersion).
  • 2026-11-25: Unplayable files (#159, owner decision 19). A song is unplayable when the device would mark it damaged or the phone's player cannot decode it. Every stored read failure (wrong format, damaged, can't open, can't read) is the device's LIB_PLAY_DAMAGED (index_file and play_from_meta, lib_build.c), worded Damaged file (lib_cant_play_str); Not downloaded stays the app's own; on iOS, Ogg and Opus read Ogg, can't play / Opus, can't play until the Xiph decoders land (owner decision 5). Greyed rows are selectable by the wheel and touch, as on the device (ui_list.c skips no row; the earlier note that the wheel skips them no longer holds); Select opens nothing; Search results grey them too. Decision 19 settles the differences from today's firmware: reason on the row and no toasts (UI styles design), unplayable songs left out of the queue, Shuffle Songs never starts on one; the firmware's backlog items are the lead's.
  • 2026-11-23: Album art (#148, schema version 4, scan version 5), known differences from the device: a Folder.jpg with the FAT hidden or system attribute (as Windows Media Player writes it) is skipped by the device (art_service.c line 380) but used by the app, which cannot see FAT attributes; the app reads at most 32 MB of a picture (decision 0010).

docs.title: Team brief: build the neuPod phone app (R1)
docs.text:
You are the lead of a small team of coding subagents. Together you build and test release R1 of the app specified in README.md: a local music player for iOS and Android, in Flutter, in mobile/ at the repository root.

Read the specification in full, then the UI styles design and its mock-ups, then CONTRIBUTING.md. PROGRESS.md is the only record of where the work stands: a new session, or one whose context was compacted, starts by reading it and carries on from the first unticked item.

R2 (NAS) and R3 (companion) are out of scope. Do not start them.

docs.title: Where to run
docs.text:
iOS can only be built and tested on macOS, so run this on the owner's Mac. Before anything else, check and report: flutter doctor -v, Xcode and its command-line tools, CocoaPods, an iOS simulator, the Android SDK and an emulator, and gh signed in. Install what is missing where that is routine; ask the owner before changing anything system-wide. If you are not on a Mac, say so and stop: do not build Android alone and call it done.

scripts/app/bootstrap-mac.sh installs the base toolchain (Xcode check, Flutter, CocoaPods, a JDK, the Android command-line tools) and starts you in a detached tmux session named neupod-app; scripts/app/run-agent.sh restarts you. Keep both working as the project's needs change.

docs.title: The team
docs.text:
You plan, delegate, integrate and decide. You do not write feature code yourself. Give each subagent one item, the parts of the specification that govern it, the files it owns, and what "done" means. Run independent items in parallel; keep one owner per file at a time.

Role Owns Architect Project scaffold, layering, package choices and their decision notes, CI Library engineer Folder access on both platforms, scanner, tag reading and fallbacks, database, art cache Audio engineer Player, gapless, queue, background playback, media session, interruptions, output route UI engineer (one or two) Styles and skins, components, screens, navigation, accessibility Test engineer Fixtures, the generated libraries, golden and integration tests, the audio and scale tests Reviewer A fresh subagent for every PR that has not seen the work; reads the diff against the specification

The test engineer writes the tests for an item from the specification, not from the implementation.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• The app shares one player UI with every neuPod device (ADR-0022): the firmware is the reference, and the app differs only where the phone's hardware or OS requires it.
  • Work only in mobile/, docs/app/, scripts/app/, the app's CI workflow, and the LICENSE.md rows the app needs. Do not change the firmware, the hardware files or their CI.
  • Branches, commits and PRs follow CONTRIBUTING.md, with scope app. Small PRs. Squash-merge when CI is green. Never force-push.
  • The repository is public. Never commit signing keys, provisioning profiles, keystores, passwords, API tokens, the owner's music, or anything personal. Add the ignore rules first.
  • R1 makes no network connection. No analytics, crash reporting service or advertising SDK, ever.
  • The app never writes to, moves or deletes a music file.
  • Choose packages from their current documentation and release history, not from memory. Record each choice and the alternatives in docs/app/decisions/. Keep the in-app Licences screen and LICENSE.md current.
  • No "iPod", no Apple marks, and no artwork copied from Apple's products, anywhere in the app or its listing.
  • Do not submit anything to a store or to TestFlight. The owner does that.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
Repeat until R1 is done:

  1. Pick the next unticked items in PROGRESS.md whose phase is open. Take as many as can run in parallel without sharing files.
  2. Brief a subagent for each, and the test engineer for its tests.
  3. Integrate: both platforms build; unit, widget, golden and integration tests pass on the Android emulator and the iOS simulator; static analysis is clean; formatting applied.
  4. Review with a fresh reviewer. Fix what it finds or record why not.
  5. PR, CI green, merge.
  6. Tick the items in PROGRESS.md with the PR number and date. Add a line under Notes for anything the next session must know.
  7. Go to 1.

At the end of each phase, run the device checks in the specification's test table on the owner's iPhone, and on an Android phone if one is attached, and record what was verified, on what, with the date. Steps that need the owner's hands (trusting the developer certificate, plugging in a phone, a signing prompt) are asked for once, in a batch.

docs.title: Gates: stop and show the owner
docs.text:
1. After phase 1 (the vertical slice). Stop. Show the app running on both platforms: pick a folder, scan, a Songs list, play, lock the phone, control from the lock screen. Report the package choices.
  2. The design gate, in phase 2. Before building every screen, build Home, a list, an album, Cover Flow and Now Playing in portrait, in Classic Light and Modern Dark, with real data. Where the specification leaves the portrait layout open, build the two best candidates. Stop and show screenshots side by side. Build the rest only after the owner chooses.
  3. Before R1 is called done. The final report, below.

Also stop and ask when: an item depends on one of the specification's Open questions; the specification is silent or contradicts itself on something that changes what the user sees; a platform cannot do what the specification requires (for example a format it cannot decode, or sample-rate passthrough); a package you depend on turns out unmaintained or wrongly licensed; or the same item has failed three times.

When you stop, leave main green and PROGRESS.md current, and say exactly what you need.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
Phase 0: set-up. Environment report. Reconcile PROGRESS.md with the specification and add anything missing. Scaffold mobile/, the ignore rules, CI (Android on Linux, iOS on a Mac runner, no signing), the decision notes for the audio engine, media session, tag reader, database and state management.

Phase 1: vertical slice. One thin path through every layer on both platforms: choose a folder, scan it, list the songs, play one, keep playing in the background with lock-screen controls. Plain styling. Then gate 1.

Phase 2: look and feel. Style and mode tokens from the UI styles design, the skins, the core components, the design-gate screens. Then gate 2.

Phase 3: library. Full scanner with tag fallbacks and the folder convention, discs, compilations, incremental rescan, art cache, ratings and play counts, the scale test.

Phase 4: playback. Queue, gapless, shuffle and repeat, seek, interruptions, output route, resume, all formats with the audio tests.

Phase 5: screens. Every browsing screen, search, fast scroll, Cover Flow, Now Playing, the queue, in both styles and modes.

Phase 6: playlists and settings. On-The-Go, named playlists, .m3u8 import and export, Settings, Licences, About.

Phase 7: finish. Accessibility pass, performance against the targets, an hour of continuous play on each device, a full pass of every screen in every style and mode, the user-facing mobile/README.md with build and install steps.

docs.title: Done
docs.text: Every item in PROGRESS.md is ticked or marked BLOCKED with an owner question attached, CI is green on main, and the final report lists: what was built; the measured numbers against each target; what was verified on which device and when; what is blocked and on what; every package used with its licence; and what R2 and R3 will need from R1 that is not there yet.

docs.title: 0001: Audio engine
docs.text: Status: Proposed (2026-11-21) · Owner: Audio engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Formats: FLAC up to 24/192, ALAC, MP3, AAC/M4A, WAV, Opus, Ogg Vorbis, on iOS and Android. A file the platform can't decode is listed greyed with the reason, and it never stops the queue.
  • True gapless between consecutive tracks, checked by a measured join test.
  • Queue: play, play next, add, reorder, clear. Seek. Shuffle and repeat stay in the Dart domain layer.
  • Background playback and interruptions: a call, headphones unplugged (becoming noisy), audio focus loss. The session side is in 0002.
  • No resampling or DSP in the app. Pass the file's sample rate through to an external DAC where the platform allows, and report what was achieved.
  • Play from an Android SAF content:// tree URI and from an iOS security-scoped bookmarked URL, not just plain paths.
  • No network connection at all, no analytics.
  • Licence compatible with distributing an MPL-2.0 app on both stores. Actively maintained.
  • Minimum OS (owner, 2026-11-21): iOS 18 and Android 10 (API 29). iOS 27 shipped on 14 September 2026. Every option below supports those versions.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
All facts were checked on 2026-11-21 against pub.dev's API, GitHub and the vendor docs listed under Sources.

Option Version (date) Licence Mins Formats on iOS Formats on Android Gapless SAF / bookmark No network / no DSP Maintenance just_audio (+ audio_service) 0.10.6 (2026-06-29) MIT, bundles Media3 under Apache-2.0 iOS 12, Android 16 AVQueuePlayer: FLAC, ALAC, MP3, AAC, WAV. No Ogg Media3 1.4.1 (Aug 2024): all except ALAC (device-dependent) Android yes. iOS: open reports of gaps and clicks on iOS 17+ and iOS 26, MP3 and FLAC (#1150, #1151, #1556) content:// passes through to Media3 DefaultDataSource (untested, #1383 open). iOS: file path only, the app holds the scope Local HTTP proxy only for headers, caching and stream sources. No float or high-res output option 4,151 likes, single maintainer, about 1 release a year lately media_kit + media_kit_libs_audio 1.2.6 (2025-12-13) MIT wrapper. libmpv and FFmpeg binaries are LGPL, downloaded at build time not checked FFmpeg: all 7 FFmpeg: all 7 mpv gapless-audio content:// through an fd helper. Bookmark: path mpv may resample unless configured. No media session, no focus handling 919 likes, last release 11 months ago, commits Aug 2026, 372 open issues audioplayers 6.8.1 (2026-06-27) MIT n/a platform platform No playlist or gapless API n/a n/a Active flutter_soloud 5.3.1 (2026-11-18) MIT / Zlib iOS 13, Android 21 Xiph codecs bundled, plus AudioToolbox for M4A Xiph bundled, plus NDK MediaCodec for M4A (so no ALAC) Sample-accurate scheduling, but no queue or player model not documented A game mixer that resamples to the engine rate, which breaks the no-DSP rule. No media session Very active Custom thin plugin: Media3 ExoPlayer (Android) and AVAudioEngine (iOS) Media3 1.11.1 (2026-09-11). AVFAudio ships with iOS Our code MPL-2.0. Media3 Apache-2.0. libogg, libopus and libvorbis BSD-3 Media3 minSdk 23. AVAudioEngine iOS 8+ AVAudioFile: FLAC, ALAC, MP3, AAC, WAV. Bundled Xiph decoders for Ogg Opus and Ogg Vorbis Media3: FLAC, MP3, AAC, WAV, Ogg Opus and Vorbis. ALAC needs a bundled decoder (see risks) Android: ExoPlayer playlist. iOS: buffers scheduled back-to-back on one AVAudioPlayerNode, so the join is sample-accurate by construction when consecutive tracks share a sample rate (see risks) content:// handled natively by Media3 ContentDataSource. On iOS it receives a file:// URL; neupod_storage resolves the bookmark and holds the scope (0004) No HTTP code paths used. We control the output format and session rate Media3 is Google's maintained stack. We maintain the plugin

just_audio (with audio_service). The quickest route, and the API matches the queue we need. It fails the spec on iOS in two ways. First, it plays through AVQueuePlayer, and its tracker has open, unresolved reports of audible gaps between items on iOS 17 and later, including iOS 26 with FLAC. The maintainer's conclusion is that the cause is inside AVQueuePlayer ("mysterious behaviour of Apple's AVQueuePlayer", #1151). Second, iOS can't play Ogg through it at all. On Android it pins Media3 1.4.1 and offers no float or high-res output setting. An AVAudioEngine rewrite of the iOS side has been an open request since 2021 (#334) and has no delivery date.

media_kit. The only off-the-shelf option that decodes all seven formats on both platforms, because it ships FFmpeg. Against it: no media session (it would need audio_service), no handling of interruptions or audio focus, mpv's own output and resampling chain, about 10 MB or more of LGPL native binaries fetched from GitHub at build time, LGPL relinking obligations in App Store builds, and 11 months without a pub release. It is the fallback if bundling Xiph and ALAC decoders ourselves proves too costly.

flutter_soloud and audioplayers. Not music-player engines. audioplayers has no gapless queue. SoLoud is a game mixer and resamples by design.

Custom thin plugin. On Android, Media3 does the work: gapless playlists, content://, audio focus, becoming noisy, and the session (0002). On iOS, AVAudioEngine scheduling makes gapless independent of AVQueuePlayer's behaviour. Bundled Xiph decoders close the Ogg gap that the system frameworks leave. The cost is native code for us to own on both platforms: route-change and engine-restart handling, seek by rescheduling, and position reporting.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Build a thin in-repo Flutter plugin (mobile/packages/neupod_audio, MPL-2.0) with a small Dart API: set queue, insert, move, remove, clear, play, pause, seek, skip, and streams of state, position, current index and format.

  • Android: androidx.media3:media3-exoplayer 1.11.x, with the player owned by a Media3 MediaSessionService (see 0002).
  • iOS: AVAudioEngine with one AVAudioPlayerNode. Decoding uses AVAudioFile for FLAC, ALAC, MP3, AAC and WAV, and bundled libogg, libopus and libvorbis for Ogg. Each track's PCM buffers are scheduled back-to-back. The session's preferred sample rate is set to the file's rate.

Why: it is the only option that can meet gapless on iOS, and all seven formats on both platforms, without LGPL binaries or an unmaintained dependency. Media3 does most of the Android work and is maintained by Google.

The phase-1 spike first runs the gapless join test on iOS with a plain AVQueuePlayer. If it passes for every format, the iOS side may use AVQueuePlayer for the system formats, which handles AirPlay and route changes for us, and keep AVAudioEngine only for Ogg.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• ALAC on Android isn't a platform format. It is missing from Android's supported-formats table, so it is device-dependent. Meeting the spec needs a bundled decoder. Either:
  • Media3's FFmpeg extension built with only alac. Google documents this path, but it is FFmpeg, LGPL-2.1, and we must build it from source.
  • Apple's open-source ALAC decoder (Apache-2.0) wrapped as a Media3 decoder. More code for us.

Lead decision (2026-11-21): Apple's ALAC decoder (Apache-2.0), wrapped as a Media3 decoder. It avoids building and shipping LGPL FFmpeg, and the firmware already has a C port of the same decoder (app/third_party/alac/), which the plugin can reuse. FFmpeg with only alac stays the fallback. - Mixed sample rates on iOS. Scheduling on one AVAudioPlayerNode is sample-accurate only while the rate stays the same. An album that changes rate between tracks needs the engine reconfigured or a converter at the join, which can leave a gap (or resample). Spike case: two tracks at 44.1 and 48 kHz back-to-back. - Ogg Vorbis and Ogg Opus on iOS have no system decoder for apps. No Apple document lists them. A third-party test on the iOS 27 simulator found that AVFoundation demuxes Ogg but has no Vorbis decoder. The same project reported Ogg Opus working on iOS 27, then reverted that change a day later. Safari's Ogg support since iOS 18.4 is WebKit's own and isn't exposed to apps. We meet the spec only by bundling the Xiph decoders, about 1 MB, BSD-3. - 24-bit/192 kHz FLAC on Android. The platform FLAC decoder is documented only to 48 kHz, "no dither applied for 24-bit". If the spike shows real decoders fall short, add Media3's libflac extension (BSD, built from source), which outputs raw PCM on every API level. Whether 24-bit PCM reaches the AudioTrack or is reduced to 16-bit by DefaultAudioSink must be checked. We may need float output enabled. - Sample-rate passthrough and bit-perfect output. No option can guarantee these. The platforms limit them: - Android 10–13: the system mixer resamples everything to the output's rate, usually 48 kHz. - Android 14+: setPreferredMixerAttributes with MIXER_BEHAVIOR_BIT_PERFECT exists for USB devices only, and vendor HAL support is optional. - iOS: setPreferredSampleRate is only a hint. Some USB DACs follow it; reports differ on whether output goes above 48 kHz. - Bluetooth and AirPlay: always re-encoded or at a fixed rate.

The format line must report the achieved output rate, never a claim. - MP3 and AAC gapless depends on encoder-delay metadata (LAME/Xing, iTunSMPB) being present and honoured. Files without it can't be gapless on any engine. - iOS AVAudioEngine stops on route and configuration changes, and the plugin must restart it and reschedule from the current frame. That is a source of bugs; test it on the device with Bluetooth, wired and AirPlay. - The Mac's toolchain is Xcode 26.5, which has no iOS 27 SDK or simulator, and phones in use run iOS 27. iOS 27 behaviour, such as Ogg in AVFoundation, can only be checked on a device, or after Xcode 27 is installed. Ask the owner. - We own native code in Kotlin and Swift. Media3 is Apache-2.0 and the Xiph libraries are BSD-3; both go on the Licences screen and in LICENSE.md.

docs.title: To verify in the phase 1 spike
docs.text:
1. Gapless: run the generated two-track join fixture (FLAC 16/44.1, FLAC 24/96, ALAC, AAC with iTunSMPB, MP3 with LAME header, Opus, Vorbis, WAV) through the iOS AVQueuePlayer and AVAudioEngine variants and through Media3. Measure the sample offset at the join, not by ear. Pass means 0 samples of inserted silence.
  2. Play content:// FLAC from a persisted SAF tree grant on an API 29 emulator and an API 36 emulator, after an app restart.
  3. Play a FLAC from an iOS security-scoped bookmark to an iCloud Drive or external folder after an app relaunch, on the owner's iPhone.
  4. Decode every fixture in tests/assets/audio on both platforms. Record per format: played, or the exact error. Include 24/192 FLAC on Android using the platform decoder only, and ALAC on the emulator and a real Android phone.
  5. Android output encoding for 24-bit FLAC: log the AudioTrack encoding and sample rate. On an Android 14+ phone with a USB DAC, try setPreferredMixerAttributes(BIT_PERFECT) and record the result.
  6. iOS: set the preferred sample rate to 96 kHz with a USB DAC, and log AVAudioSession.sampleRate after activation.
  7. Check that the release Android manifest has no INTERNET permission, and that nothing in the plugin opens a socket. On iOS, record a network trace during playback (it should be empty).
  8. Build size delta of the Xiph decoders, and of the ALAC decoder option chosen.

docs.title: Phase 1 implementation (2026-11-22)
docs.text:
Built as decided, in mobile/packages/neupod_audio (Pigeon 30.0.4 contract in pigeon/messages.dart). Where it differs from or defers part of the text above:

  • iOS schedules file segments, not hand-read buffers. Each track goes to the node with AVAudioPlayerNode.scheduleSegment(_:startingFrame:frameCount:at:); AVAudioFile reads and converts it on the engine's thread. Consecutive segments on one node join sample-accurately just as buffers do, with less code and no buffer pool to size. Only the current and the next track are scheduled. scheduleBuffer stays the path for the bundled Xiph decoders (Ogg, phase 4), which produce PCM themselves.
  • Mixed formats at a join: the next track is pre-scheduled only when its processing format (rate, channels) matches the connected one. Otherwise the engine is reconnected when the current track ends, which can leave a short gap. The join test in phase 4 measures both cases.
  • The AVQueuePlayer comparison spike was not run. Phase 1 needed one working path; AVAudioEngine is it. The measured join test (spike item 1) is the phase 4 item "Gapless, with the measured join test"; if AVQueuePlayer then proves gapless for every system format, switching the system formats to it is still open.
  • No network on Android, enforced in code as well as by the manifest: the player and the artwork loader use a data source that opens only content:// and file:// (LocalDataSource.kt), so Media3's HTTP, UDP, RTMP and data: sources are never reached.
  • The skip-back rule is native on both platforms (Media3's maxSeekToPreviousPositionMs = 3000; the same rule in AudioEngine.swift), because the lock screen's previous button reaches the engine without Dart.
  • Every setQueue carries a random queue id, echoed in every engine event, and the Dart player applies only events with its own id. So an event about an earlier queue, a stale empty snapshot, or a queue an earlier Flutter engine set while the Android service lived on, never moves the current one (mobile/lib/audio/neupod_player.dart). On Android the id rides in each item's metadata extras, so it lives in the session, not in the plugin.
  • iOS position after the system stops the engine: the node has no render time then, so the engine keeps a render anchor (position and CACurrentMediaTime when rendering last started or a gapless join happened) and extrapolates from it. A route or format change, or an interruption, records the true position and the next play reschedules from it. The unplug burst (a route change and a configuration change, in an undocumented order) is handled by one shared test in both handlers; the residual risk, if currentRoute lags the first notification, is in 0002. Engine events report isPlaying (sound now) apart from the play intent, so Dart does not extrapolate while playback is suppressed.
  • An unplayable entry never stops the queue: the engine reports the error with the entry, and the Dart player skips to the next one once.
  • On Android the session also prepares the player again whenever it is idle with an error from a track other than the current one (ErrorRecovery.kt). Without it, a play that retried the failed track, followed at once by the skip, could leave the player idle on the next track. The plugin decides from a MediaController's masked state, which cannot see the retry's error coming. This was a CI flake on PR #111, reproduced with a forced ordering and now covered by an integration test.
  • Not yet (later phases, seams left): Ogg on iOS, ALAC on Android, repeat-one gapless (repeat is a Dart rule, so the engine will need the mode to pre-schedule the same track), output-route reporting, measured sample-rate passthrough. The iOS session's preferred sample rate is already set to the file's rate as a hint.

docs.title: Later (noted in review, 2026-11-22)
docs.text:
• Late scheduling of the next segment. Today the next track is scheduled as soon as the current one starts, so an edit to the queue's next entry reschedules the current track from its position, a small blip. Scheduling the next segment a few seconds before the join would make most edits free.
  • A debug-only PCM capture hook (a tap on the mixer on iOS, an AudioProcessor or TeeAudioProcessor on Android) for the phase 4 measured gapless join test.
  • The bundled test tones ship in the app (integration_test/assets/test_media/, declared as assets for the debug screen and the integration tests). A release blocker, tracked in PROGRESS.md.

docs.title: 0002: Media session, background playback and output route
docs.text: Status: Proposed (2026-11-21) · Owner: Audio engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Playback continues with the screen locked and the app in the background, on both platforms.
  • Lock-screen and notification controls with artwork and a scrubber: play/pause, next, previous, seek.
  • Headset and Bluetooth transport buttons.
  • Interruptions: a call pauses, unplugging headphones (becoming noisy) pauses, and another app taking audio focus pauses.
  • Resume: the queue, track and position are restored on reopen. That lives in the domain layer; the session only has to accept a restored queue.
  • An icon shows the output in use: speaker, wired, Bluetooth or AirPlay. No Cast in R1 (owner decision 6).
  • No network: artwork comes from local files only. Only the permissions needed.
  • Fits the engine chosen in 0001: Media3 ExoPlayer on Android, AVAudioEngine on iOS.
  • Minimum OS (owner, 2026-11-21): iOS 18, Android 10 (API 29).

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
All facts were checked on 2026-11-21.

Option Version (date) Licence Mins Works with 0001 Lock screen and notification Buttons Interruptions and noisy Route detection Network code pulled in Maintenance Media3 session (Android) and MediaPlayer/AVFAudio frameworks (iOS), inside the 0001 plugin media3-session 1.11.1 (2026-09-11). iOS system frameworks Apache-2.0. OS frameworks API 23. iOS 7.1+ (MPRemoteCommandCenter) Native: the session wraps the same ExoPlayer Yes. Media3 builds the MediaStyle notification. iOS uses MPNowPlayingInfoCenter with artwork, and changePlaybackPositionCommand for scrubbing Yes. Media3 media-button handling; iOS MPRemoteCommandCenter ExoPlayer handleAudioFocus and setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy. iOS AVAudioSession interruption and route-change notifications We write it: Android AudioManager, iOS AVAudioSession.currentRoute DefaultHttpDataSource is linked but unused Google-maintained, about monthly releases audio_service 0.18.19 (2026-06-29). The 0.18.20 fixes are on the branch, unpublished MIT iOS 13, Android 19 Via a Dart BaseAudioHandler bridging to our engine. On Android that puts a second session layer (legacy androidx.media 1.7.0) beside Media3 Yes Yes Through audio_session, wired up by the app No flutter_cache_manager (http, for http art URIs) 1,335 likes, single maintainer, Android lifecycle issues open (#1180, #996, #1148) just_audio_background 0.0.1-beta.17 (2025-05-13) MIT as audio_service No, tied to just_audio Yes Yes Via just_audio No as audio_service Beta, 18 months since a release audio_session (as a helper) 0.2.4 (2026-06-29) MIT not checked (below proposals) Could configure the session from Dart, but two owners of AVAudioSession and audio focus invites conflicts n/a n/a Interruption and becoming-noisy streams getDevices(). On Android it lists all connected devices, not the active route none Active

Native, inside the engine plugin (recommended). Google's guidance for Media3 is to put the ExoPlayer and a MediaSession inside a MediaSessionService. That gives:

  • the foreground service and the MediaStyle notification, populated from session metadata (from API 33 the system renders it);
  • Bluetooth and headset buttons;
  • playback resumption from the system UI;
  • one consistent state, with no bridging.

On iOS the same plugin owns:

  • the AVAudioSession (.playback category, UIBackgroundModes: audio);
  • MPNowPlayingInfoCenter, with title, artist, album, duration, elapsed time, rate and MPMediaItemArtwork from the local art cache;
  • MPRemoteCommandCenter: play, pause, toggle, next, previous, and change playback position for lock-screen scrubbing;
  • interruption and route-change notifications. Old-device-unavailable means headphones were unplugged, so pause.

audio_service is the standard Flutter answer and works with any engine. Here it would duplicate on Android what Media3 already provides, behind a legacy compat session. It would add flutter_cache_manager and its HTTP stack to a no-network app. It also carries open Android engine-lifecycle bugs. It stays as the fallback if the team ever drops the custom engine for just_audio (0001's alternative).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Implement the media session natively inside the neupod_audio plugin from 0001:

  • Android: androidx.media3:media3-session 1.11.x, with a MediaSessionService that owns the ExoPlayer. Manifest entries: FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK, a service with foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback", and the Media3 MediaButtonReceiver with onPlaybackResumption backed by the persisted queue.
  • iOS: AVFAudio's AVAudioSession and MediaPlayer's MPNowPlayingInfoCenter and MPRemoteCommandCenter.
  • Output route:
  • iOS: AVAudioSession.currentRoute.outputs port type (built-in speaker, headphones, Bluetooth A2DP/LE, AirPlay, USB, car), refreshed on routeChangeNotification.
  • Android 13+ (API 33+): AudioManager.getDevicesForAttributes(USAGE_MEDIA).
  • Android 10–12: the best available signal, AudioDeviceCallback plus isBluetoothA2dpOn()/wired checks, as a documented approximation.

Why: one owner of player, session and focus per platform, no bridging layer, no HTTP-capable dependency, and both sides are maintained by Google or are OS frameworks.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• "Cast" can't be supported on Android in R1. Casting from an app needs the Google Cast SDK and the app's own network connection, which the R1 no-network rule forbids. The Android icon set is therefore speaker, wired, Bluetooth and USB. Resolved: owner decision 6 (README.md), no Cast in R1. iOS AirPlay is fine: the OS does the networking, and the route shows as airPlay. The AVAudioEngine path must use routeSharingPolicy = .longFormAudio for AirPlay 2, which the spike will verify.
  • The active route on Android 10–12 is inferred, not reported. No public API before API 33 returns the device the media stream is routed to. A rare mismatch is possible, for example Bluetooth connected but audio forced to the speaker.
  • Artwork must be passed as a file or content:// URI or as bytes, never an http URI. The Android release manifest has no INTERNET permission, so the OS enforces no network.
  • Android 13+ media-session notifications are exempt from the POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission. No extra prompt is expected; the spike will confirm on API 36.
  • We write and test the Dart ↔ native contract ourselves: state, position and queue-index streams.
  • iOS: the plugin must re-publish the now-playing info after every AVAudioEngine restart, or the lock screen goes stale.

docs.title: To verify in the phase 1 spike
docs.text:
1. Android API 29 and API 36 emulators: start playback, lock, and check that the notification and lock screen show art, title and a working seek bar. Swipe the app away and check that playback continues.
  2. iPhone (owner's): lock-screen and Control Centre show art and title, and the scrubber seeks to the right position. Playback survives 30 minutes locked.
  3. Headset and Bluetooth: single press toggles, double press goes next, triple press goes previous, on both platforms. On Android also test playback resumption from a Bluetooth play press after the service has died.
  4. Interruptions: an incoming call (simulated on both emulators/simulators, real on the device) pauses and doesn't auto-resume unless the system says so. Unplugging wired headphones or disconnecting Bluetooth pauses. Another media app taking focus pauses.
  5. Route icon: speaker, wired, Bluetooth, USB DAC (Android) and AirPlay (iOS) each show correctly. Switching mid-track updates the icon within 1 s and, on iOS, playback continues after the engine restart.
  6. Confirm no POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt is needed on API 33+ for the media notification.

docs.title: Phase 1 implementation (2026-11-22)
docs.text:
Built as decided, inside mobile/packages/neupod_audio. Where it differs from or defers part of the text above:

  • Manifest entries live in the plugin's manifest (merged into the app's): FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK, the exported PlaybackService with foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback", and also WAKE_LOCK, a normal (no prompt) permission ExoPlayer's WAKE_MODE_LOCAL needs so playback does not stall with the screen off. No POST_NOTIFICATIONS.
  • The Flutter side is a MediaController connected to the service, so the app, the notification and the buttons drive one player. Items cross the session boundary without their URI, so the URI travels in RequestMetadata.mediaUri and the session restores it. Only the app's own package may set the queue; the system UI, Bluetooth and other controllers may only control playback.
  • Playback resumption is deferred to phase 4 (the "Resume" item): the MediaButtonReceiver and onPlaybackResumption need the persisted queue, which does not exist yet. Until then a Bluetooth play press after the service has died does nothing.
  • Interruptions, minimal now: Android uses ExoPlayer's audio-focus handling and becoming-noisy pause. iOS:
  • An interruption's start (even while paused) marks the schedule stale, and the next play reschedules from the true position.
  • The "unplugged" test: a personal output (headphones, Bluetooth, USB, AirPlay, car) has gone and none is in the new route. Moving between personal outputs (AirPods to CarPlay, Bluetooth to AirPlay) does not pause.
  • oldDeviceUnavailable pauses when the test holds against the previous route.
  • AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange, which unplugging also posts, pauses when the test holds against the outputs in use. Otherwise it restarts from the current position one run-loop turn later, unless the route change paused meanwhile.
  • Both handlers apply the same test, so the outcome does not depend on which notification comes first, provided AVAudioSession.currentRoute already shows the new route when the first one runs. If it lags (not documented either way), the configuration change could see the old route and restart on the speaker for a moment before the route change pauses. To check on the iPhone in phase 4.
  • Completion callbacks that a system stop fires for the old segments are ignored (the schedule's generation is bumped), so they cannot advance or end the queue.
  • The session is deactivated with .notifyOthersOnDeactivation when the queue ends or is cleared.

Resuming after a transient interruption, and checking all of this on a real iPhone (the simulator has no real route changes or calls), are phase 4. - Commands and observers are released on plugin detach: the MPRemoteCommandCenter targets and the NotificationCenter observers are removed. - The lock screen's artwork comes from the item's artUri (the art cache, later), else from art embedded in the file: Media3 extracts it itself; on iOS the plugin reads AVAsset's common artwork metadata. - Route detection is not built yet (phase 4, "Output route icon").

docs.title: 0003: Tag reader
docs.text: Status: Proposed (2026-11-21) · Owner: Library engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Fields: title, artist, album artist, album, track and disc number, year, genre, compilation flag, duration, sample rate, bit depth, embedded art (location and type, bytes read only when the art cache needs them).
  • Containers: FLAC (Vorbis comments, PICTURE), ALAC and AAC in MP4 (ilst incl. aART, cpil, disk, trkn, covr), MP3 (ID3v2.3/2.4, ID3v1 fallback, Xing/Info/LAME and VBRI for duration), WAV (LIST/INFO, id3 chunk), Ogg Opus and Ogg Vorbis.
  • Same field semantics as the firmware (app/audio/meta.c, mp4.c): first four digits of DATE/TDRC/©day as year, ID3v1 (n) genres resolved, TCMP/cpil/COMPILATION as flag, TPE2/aART/ALBUMARTIST as album artist. The spec wants a library to look the same on phone and device.
  • Robust: a damaged file yields "unreadable, reason" or partial tags, never an exception that stops the scan, never a hang, never unbounded memory.
  • Fast: headers only. Budget about 60 ms a file (5,000 FLACs in under 5 min), most of which is I/O.
  • Reads from a random-access byte source that can come from an Android SAF document (file descriptor) or an iOS security-scoped URL, not only a dart:io path (see 0004).
  • Runs in a background isolate; no platform-channel call per field or per read.
  • Licence compatible with an MPL-2.0 app on both stores; actively maintained; read-only use (the app never writes tags).

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
Checked on pub.dev, crates.io and GitHub on 2026-11-21.

Option Version Last release Licence Platforms Fields Containers Byte source Maintained Own Dart parser (port of firmware meta.c/mp4.c, plus Ogg and WAV tags) n/a n/a MPL-2.0 (ours) all all, by design all, by design any (our interface) us audio_metadata_reader (pure Dart) 1.8.1 2026-10-14 MIT Android, iOS, desktop no compilation flag, no bit depth in the common model; aART not read; MP3 album artist mis-mapped (#102) all except WAV id3 unclear dart:io File only (sync RandomAccessFile) yes (commits 2026-10-28) lofty 0.25.5 (Rust) via flutter_rust_bridge 2.13.0, our own bindings 0.25.5 / 2.13.0 2026-10-25 / 2026-08-23 MIT OR Apache-2.0 / MIT all (needs Rust toolchain) all all, plus many more path, or File::from_raw_fd very (commits 2026-11-21) audiotags (lofty wrapper) 1.4.5 2025-04-15 MIT all partial via lofty path only no: last push 2025-06-12 metadata_god (lofty wrapper) 1.1.0 2025-08-18 MIT all partial via lofty path only no: last push 2025-08-18 flutter_media_metadata 1.0.0+1 2022-01-30 MIT - - - - no (Dart 2 only) id3 1.0.2 2021-11-08 MIT - MP3 only MP3 - discontinued dart_tags 0.4.1 2024-03-27 MIT all ID3 + MP4 only MP3, MP4 bytes stale Platform: MediaMetadataRetriever / AVAsset OS OS OS per platform Android: sample rate and bit depth only on API 31+; iOS AVFoundation does not read Ogg uneven, OEM-dependent URI/fd (Android), URL (iOS) OS

Own Dart parser. About 1,500-2,000 lines of Dart: FLAC metadata blocks, MP4 box walk (moov/udta/meta/ilst, stsd for ALAC/AAC rate and depth, mdhd for duration), ID3v2.2-2.4 with unsynchronisation and extended headers, the MPEG frame header with Xing/Info/LAME/VBRI, RIFF fmt/LIST INFO/id3, Ogg page reader with the Opus and Vorbis identification and comment headers and the last granule position for duration. FLAC, MP3, MP4 and the text and genre rules already exist in C under app/audio/ and are ported, not designed; WAV tags and Ogg are new. It reads through a small interface (readAt(offset, length), length) so the same code runs on an Android fd, an iOS path and test bytes, in any isolate. Every length read from a file is bounded against the file size and a cap, which is how the firmware parser is written already.

audio_metadata_reader. Active, MIT, pure Dart and closest off-the-shelf fit, but its common model lacks the compilation flag and bit depth, MP4 aART is not in its atom list, MP3 artist takes TPE2 before TPE1 (open issue

docs.title: 102), and a bad Vorbis DATE throws and drops all metadata (#121). It takes a dart:io File only. We would be
docs.text:
reading its format-specific objects and patching around the gaps, or forking. Kept as a test oracle (dev dependency only, never shipped): the scanner tests compare our output with it on the fixtures.

lofty via flutter_rust_bridge. The most complete and most fuzzed reader available, permissively licensed and very active. Costs: no maintained Flutter wrapper (both wrappers are stale), so we own the bindings; a Rust toolchain with Android NDK targets and iOS targets on every developer machine and on both CI runners; several MB of native code per ABI; a second language in the repo. It reads a path or a raw fd, so 0004 still works. This is the fallback if our parser fails the spike.

Platform readers. Rejected: two implementations with different answers, sample rate and bit depth missing below Android 12, no Ogg on iOS, and each call crosses a platform channel.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Write our own pure-Dart tag reader in mobile/ (data layer), ported from the firmware parsers and extended with Ogg Opus/Vorbis and WAV LIST INFO/id3. It gives exactly the fields and semantics the device uses, reads through a random-access interface that works with SAF file descriptors and security-scoped URLs, runs in a background isolate, adds no package, no native toolchain and no licence row, and its size is bounded because most of it exists in C already. audio_metadata_reader is used only as a test oracle. lofty through flutter_rust_bridge is the recorded fallback.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• We own correctness on malformed files. Mitigation: bounds checks on every length; a per-file time and byte budget; the scanner catches everything per file; a fuzz test (mutated fixtures) in CI; the fixtures in tests/assets/audio plus generated Ogg, WAV-with-tags and odd ID3 cases.
  • Two implementations of the same rules (C and Dart) can drift. Mitigation: a shared table of golden cases (file, expected fields) used by both test suites where practical.
  • Formats beyond the spec (AIFF, APE, DSF) are not read; they are listed greyed by the scanner as the device does.
  • Art: the scan records offset, length and kind (from its first bytes, not the MIME) of the best picture, as meta_art_offer does (decision 0010); bytes are read later by the art cache, so the scan stays header-only.
  • Sync reads in an isolate are fine; the isolate must never be the UI isolate.

docs.title: To verify in the phase 1 spike
docs.text:
1. Port FLAC + MP3 + MP4 readers; parse every file in tests/assets/audio; compare with audio_metadata_reader and with the firmware's host tests; differences explained.
  2. Time 5,000 FLACs (generated, with 500 KB embedded art) on the Android emulator and the owner's iPhone, read through the 0004 byte source: target under 60 ms a file, header bytes read per file under 128 KB when art is skipped.
  3. Ogg: Opus and Vorbis fixtures (generated with opusenc/oggenc), duration from the last granule (minus Opus pre-skip) within 1 ms of ffprobe.
  4. MP3 VBR without Xing: estimated duration flagged as estimated, as the firmware does.
  5. Fuzz: 10,000 mutated fixture files, no exception escapes, no file over 1 s, memory flat.
  6. If 1-5 fail or the port is over its time box, prototype lofty via FRB on both CI runners and record the binary size and build-time cost.

docs.title: Implementation so far (phase 1, 2026-11-22)
docs.text:
mobile/lib/data/scan/tag_reader.dart reads FLAC (STREAMINFO, Vorbis comments, an ID3v2 tag in front skipped) and MP3 (ID3v2.2 to 2.4 text frames with unsynchronisation and extended headers; first frame confirmed by the next; duration from Xing/Info minus the LAME delay and padding, or VBRI, else estimated and flagged) through a ByteSource (readAt, length), ported from app/audio/meta.c. Phase 1 keeps title, artist, album, track number, duration, sample rate and bit depth; text is not cut at the firmware's small buffer sizes (1,024 characters instead), and UTF-16 surrogate pairs are kept. The scanner opens files on the root isolate (neupod_storage.openHandle: a detached fd on Android, a file:// URI on iOS) and parses them in a background isolate with Isolate.run, 32 files per run. Failures become a reason on the track (not a FLAC file, file is cut short), never an exception that stops the scan; a 2,000-case mutation test checks that. The rest of this note (other containers and fields, art, the audio_metadata_reader oracle, timing at 5,000 files) is phase 3.

Also read in phase 1: the title sort tag (ID3 TSOT/TST, Vorbis TITLESORT), which the sort key uses (owner decision 11). Failures are stored as a reason code (UnreadableReason: not downloaded, can't open, can't read, wrong format, damaged); the UI words it, and the transient ones (can't open, can't read) are retried on the next scan. VBRI is accepted only with the firmware's vbri_parse checks (62 fixed bytes, non-zero frames, entries, scale and frames per entry, entry size 1 to 4).

Limits shared with the firmware, kept on purpose so both read the same tags: ID3v2.3 unsynchronisation is undone per frame only when the tag header flag is set (as id3v2_tags does), compressed or encrypted frames are not decoded, and a text frame over 400 bytes is skipped.

Display text and key text are separate (owner decision 11: the app matches the firmware's code). The reader decodes the whole tag for display (UTF-16 pairs kept, malformed UTF-8 as U+FFFD), and separately keeps the title and title sort tag exactly as the firmware's meta_text_to_utf8() stores them (firmwareText(), a port): into its 64- and 32-byte buffers, whole characters only, UTF-16 surrogates (pairs and lone ones) as ?, malformed UTF-8 copied through raw. A FLAC whose comment block is over 4096 bytes (TAG_SCRATCH in lib_build.c, which flac_parse then skips) has no key text, so its key falls back to the file name as on the device. The song key is lib_collate_key() (ported over raw bytes, collateKeyBytes) of that title, or of the file name with its extension cut by cut() to 64 bytes, with the sort tag. scripts/app/gen_tag_key_vectors.py builds small tagged files for each of these cases and records what the compiled firmware C makes of them; the app's test compares byte for byte. Text is not trimmed (the firmware keeps spaces, and they sort). The Songs list shows an untagged song's name without its extension (the folder-convention fallback comes in phase 3).
