docs.title: 0004: Folder access
docs.text: Status: Accepted (phase 1, 2026-11-22; see Implementation) · Owner: Library engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Android: pick one or more folders with the system picker (SAF ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE); keep read-only access across restarts (takePersistableUriPermission).
  • Android: also offer the shared music collection (MediaStore audio); permission READ_MEDIA_AUDIO on API 33+, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (with maxSdkVersion="32") below.
  • iOS: the app's Documents folder visible in Files and Finder (UIFileSharingEnabled, LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace); plus folders picked elsewhere in Files (iCloud Drive, external drive), kept with a bookmark of the security-scoped URL.
  • iOS: iCloud files that are not downloaded are detected and handled, not mistaken for missing or broken files.
  • Recursive listing with size and last-modified for 20,000 tracks: a no-change rescan under 10 s.
  • Random-access reads of file headers for the tag reader (0003) from a background isolate, without a platform-channel hop per read.
  • Hand the audio engine something it can open natively and gaplessly.
  • Never write, move or delete; request nothing beyond what reading needs. No network.
  • Minimum OS (owner, 2026-11-21): iOS 18+, Android 10 (API 29)+. Flutter 3.50 itself supports Android 24+ and iOS 15+.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
Checked on pub.dev, GitHub and the platform docs on 2026-11-21.

Option Version Last release Licence Platforms Tree pick + persist Fast listing (projection) Byte access iOS bookmark Maintained Own small plugin in mobile/ (Kotlin + Swift, Pigeon 30.0.4 for the API) n/a n/a MPL-2.0 (ours); Pigeon BSD-3 both yes, read-only flags yes, recursive in Kotlin, one call detached fd (Android), path (iOS) yes us saf_util + saf_stream 3.1.1 / 4.0.3 2026-09-30 / 2026-10-21 BSD-3-Clause Android only yes (persistablePermission) yes, DocumentsContract query with projection, one level per call getFileDescriptor (fd int), streams - yes file_picker (getDirectoryPath) 13.4.1 2026-11-21 MIT both pick only; no persisted iOS bookmark API no listing - no yes shared_storage 0.8.1 2024-02-16 MIT Android - - - - discontinued docman, saf, flutter_saf, document_tree_android 1.2.0 / 2.1.2 / 0.1.0 / 1.0.0 2025-01 to 2026-11 MIT/BSD-3 Android yes varies varies - small or new file_anchor (+ _ios, _android) 0.1.0 2026-09-13 MIT both yes unknown unknown yes one release, no users directory_bookmarks 0.1.2 2024-11-26 MIT Android, macOS (not iOS) - - - macOS only stale on_audio_query (MediaStore) 2.9.0 2023-05-15 BSD-3-Clause Android, iOS n/a MediaStore query - n/a stale media_store_plus 0.1.3 2024-09-22 MIT Android n/a write-oriented - n/a stale

Android listing, the fast path. DocumentFile.listFiles() then length()/lastModified() costs one binder query per file per attribute; the Android guide itself warns that iterating a large tree "might reduce performance", and field reports put a direct query hundreds of times faster. The fast path is one ContentResolver.query(DocumentsContract.buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree(tree, docId), [DOCUMENT_ID, DISPLAY_NAME, MIME_TYPE, SIZE, LAST_MODIFIED], ...) per directory, walked breadth-first in Kotlin on a background thread, results streamed to Dart in batches. 300 CDs is roughly 600 directories, so a rescan is about 600 queries plus a database diff. saf_util.list already does this query, one level per channel call; our plugin does the whole walk in one call.

Android byte access. ContentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r") then ParcelFileDescriptor.detachFd() gives an int fd owned by Dart; the tag reader does pread and close through dart:ffi (package ffi, BSD-3) in its isolate, with no channel traffic per read. (Alternative to test: open /proc/self/fd/N with dart:io.) MediaStore items use the same route with their content://media/... URI; on API 30+ the DATA path is also readable with READ_MEDIA_AUDIO, but not on Android 10 without requestLegacyExternalStorage, so we use the URI on every version.

iOS. Documents needs no permission: the two Info.plist keys make it appear under On My iPhone and in Finder. Other folders: UIDocumentPickerViewController(forOpeningContentTypes: [.folder]) (iOS 13+) returns a security-scoped URL that covers the whole tree "including any new items"; we store bookmarkData() (.withSecurityScope is macOS-only; iOS bookmarks of picker URLs are implicitly scoped), resolve it at launch, re-save if stale, and keep startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() active for each library root while the app runs. Children of the root are then ordinary paths that dart:io and AVFoundation can open from any isolate. Listing is FileManager enumeration with fileSizeKey, contentModificationDateKey, ubiquitousItemDownloadingStatusKey, inside NSFileCoordinator as Apple asks. iCloud items not on the device appear as hidden .Name.ext.icloud placeholders (or with status notDownloaded); we list them as tracks greyed Not downloaded with folder-convention names, and never download on our own (see risks).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Build one small in-repo plugin (mobile/packages/neupod_storage, Kotlin + Swift, API defined with Pigeon) with five calls: pickFolder(), listRoots() / removeRoot(), walk(root) -> stream of {relPath, size, mtime, uri, state}, openRead(uri) -> fd (Android) / path (iOS), and mediaStoreAudio(sinceGeneration) on Android. No maintained package covers iOS folder bookmarks, and the Android packages either list one level per call or are stale; the native code needed is a few hundred lines on each side. saf_util (BSD-3, active) is the fallback for the Android half if the plugin slips.

The audio engine gets a URI string: content://... on Android (Media3's DefaultDataSource opens content URIs itself, and the persisted grant belongs to the whole app process), file://... under an actively accessed root on iOS. The URI goes to neupod_audio (0001): Media3 opens content:// itself, and on iOS AVAudioFile opens the file:// URL. Only neupod_storage resolves bookmarks and starts or stops security-scoped access; the audio plugin never does, so neither can end access the other still needs. Not an fd and not a Dart byte stream (a Dart stream source would need a localhost HTTP proxy, which fits badly with "no network connection").

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• Android 11+ cannot pick the root of internal storage, the root of a reliable SD card, or Download as a tree. Music in Music/ or any subfolder is fine. The UI must say this when the picker refuses.
  • MediaStore source and folder art: READ_MEDIA_AUDIO covers audio only. Folder.jpg/cover.jpg next to the tracks are images, and READ_MEDIA_IMAGES is restricted by Play policy. Tracks from the shared collection get embedded art only; folder-art fallback works for SAF-picked folders. Resolved: owner decision 8. Spike: ContentResolver.loadThumbnail on the album URI may recover some folder art under READ_MEDIA_AUDIO.
  • iCloud not downloaded: reading or playing an evicted file makes iOS fetch it from iCloud. R1 promises no network connection. Resolved: owner decision 7, a Download action that asks iOS to fetch; the app never reads an evicted file without that tap. iOS 18.4+ reportedly changed when evicted files are refreshed (forum report, unanswered); test.
  • Scan surviving the app being closed: Android can keep a scan going in a foreground service or WorkManager. iOS cannot run an arbitrary long task after the user closes the app; the scan checkpoints and resumes at next launch, and keeps going while music plays in the background (the app is then not suspended). Resolved: owner decision 8.
  • The iOS picker grants read-write to the tree; read-only is enforced by our code only (no write API in the plugin). On Android we request FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION only.
  • Removable drives on iOS: a bookmark to an unplugged drive fails to resolve; the root shows as unavailable, its tracks stay in the library greyed until the user removes the folder.
  • Persisted SAF grants are capped (128, raised to 512 in Android 11, per AOSP and CommonsWare); we hold one per root.
  • Permissions requested: Android READ_MEDIA_AUDIO (33+) and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion="32", only when the user turns on the shared collection; none for SAF. iOS: none.

docs.title: To verify in the phase 1 spike
docs.text:
1. Android emulator (API 29 and 36): pick Music/Library, reboot, confirm the grant survives (persistedUriPermissions).
  2. Walk a generated 20,000-file, 2,000-directory tree: time the Kotlin walk and the Dart diff; target under 5 s total no-change rescan on the emulator; compare with DocumentFile to record the gap.
  3. detachFd + FFI pread from a background isolate: 5,000 header reads; check fds are always closed (count /proc/self/fd). Try /proc/self/fd/N with RandomAccessFile as the simpler alternative.
  4. Same fd path on a non-local provider (Google Drive if installed): openFileDescriptor may return a pipe (not seekable); confirm we detect and grey it. (Moot for R1: the picker is local-only, see Implementation.)
  5. neupod_audio plays a content:// tree URI and a MediaStore URI gaplessly on Android, and a bookmarked iCloud Drive file URL on iOS after relaunch.
  6. iPhone: drag a folder in Finder into Documents; pick an iCloud Drive folder with some files evicted; confirm the placeholder names and status keys on the current iOS; relaunch and resolve the bookmark; a USB drive unplugged.
  7. Android 10 device or emulator: MediaStore query with READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, URI reads work without legacy storage.

docs.title: Implementation (phase 1, 2026-11-22)
docs.text:
Built as decided, in mobile/packages/neupod_storage (Kotlin + Swift, Pigeon 30.0.4 as a dev dependency only), used by mobile/lib/data/platform/storage_folder_access.dart. Where it differs from the decision above, and why:

  • Calls. pickFolder, listRoots, removeRoot, startWalk / nextWalkBatch / cancelWalk, openFd (Android), appSupportPath (the private directory for the library database, so path_provider is not needed; see 0005) and debugAddRoot (iOS debug builds only). mediaStoreAudio is left to its own phase 3 item ("Android: the device's shared music collection"), so phase 1 requests no permission at all on either platform. (Phase 3: built as addSharedCollection plus a root of kind sharedCollection that the same walk calls list, see 0012.)
  • Walk as pages, not a stream. The walk is pull-based: each nextWalkBatch continues the breadth-first DocumentsContract walk (Android) or the FileManager enumerator (iOS) on a background thread until it has about N files. Dart wraps it as a Stream<List<StorageEntry>>; cancelling the subscription calls cancelWalk. This gives back-pressure and cancel with plain host-API calls, where a Pigeon event channel cannot take a root argument.
  • Callback-style async (@asyncCallback). Pigeon 28+ generates Kotlin suspend functions for @async, which would add kotlinx-coroutines-android to the app. The callback form needs no new shipped library.
  • No ffi package. FdStorageReader calls pread/lseek/close (the 64 variants where libc has them) through dart:ffi and DynamicLibrary.process(), with malloc/free from libc too, so nothing new ships. lseek to the end gives the length and fails on a pipe, which is how a non-seekable provider descriptor is detected and refused.
  • iOS bookmarks are kept in the plugin's own UserDefaults key, resolved and held open (one startAccessingSecurityScopedResource per root) when the plugin registers at launch, and re-saved when stale. Listing runs inside NSFileCoordinator with .immediatelyAvailableMetadataOnly, one coordinated read per page. iCloud placeholders (.Name.ext.icloud) and items whose downloading status is notDownloaded come back with state = notDownloaded and their real name; other hidden files are skipped. The privacy manifest declares the file timestamp (3B52.1, C617.1) and UserDefaults (CA92.1) reasons.
  • Test hook. debugAddRoot(path) stores a bookmark exactly as a pick does, so the iOS integration test covers bookmark storage, resolution after relaunch, walking and reading. It throws in release builds. The picker UI itself is driven on Android (adb, scripts/app/drive_saf_picker.py) but not on the iOS simulator.
  • Hidden entries. Names starting with . are skipped on both platforms (except iCloud placeholders on iOS).
  • Complete or not. The last page of a walk says whether every folder was listed (complete). It is false when a subfolder could not be read (Android: the child query failed; iOS: the enumerator's error handler fired), when the tree is deeper than 64 levels or a document id repeats (a provider loop), when the coordinated read fails, or when the root is no longer reachable at the end (an unplugged drive makes the enumerator simply run dry). The scanner deletes tracks for files missing from a walk only after a complete one.
  • Threading. Every ContentResolver call (roots, grants, walks) runs on one background executor and openFd on a second one, so a provider that blocks an open cannot stall a walk or the platform thread (removeRoot, startWalk and openFd are asynchronous in the API). On iOS all bookmark, access and walk state lives on one serial queue; bookmarks are resolved there at launch, not on the main thread, and a bookmark that did not resolve is tried again on every listRoots. removeRoot cancels the root's walks before giving up access.
  • On-device storage only (lead decision, 2026-11-22, under R1's no-network rule). The Android picker is opened with EXTRA_LOCAL_ONLY, so cloud providers (Drive and the like), whose reads are network fetches, are not offered, and entries flagged FLAG_VIRTUAL_DOCUMENT (no bytes of their own) are skipped. Spike item 4 (a non-local provider) is therefore moot for R1; the pipe check in FdStorageReader stays as a guard. On iOS the picker cannot be limited this way; iCloud Drive is covered by owner decision 7 (not-downloaded files are never read).
  • Handles. openHandle takes the StorageEntry and refuses a not-downloaded one by construction. A ReaderHandle is used exactly once (open or discard); pread is retried on EINTR, and failures carry errno.

docs.title: iCloud files not downloaded (phase 3, 2026-11-25)
docs.text:
Owner decision 7: such files are listed with a Download action; the app never fetches them itself, and a tap asks iOS to download the file. Built as follows.

  • Detection, metadata only (ICloudItem in NeupodStoragePlugin.swift). A file is not downloaded when any of these holds: it is a hidden placeholder .Name.ext.icloud; its ubiquitousItemDownloadingStatus is notDownloaded; or lstat shows the APFS dataless flag (SF_DATALESS), which File Provider sets on any file whose content is not local, so a third-party provider that reports no downloading status is caught too (the risk noted below). lstat and resource values read the inode and the provider's metadata; neither materialises the file. A placeholder is listed under the real file's name and URL, so the track's URI does not change once the file arrives. Size is 0.
  • Security-scoped bookmarks. The bookmark of a picked iCloud Drive folder covers the files in it whether or not they are downloaded; access is held for the root as before, so metadata reads, the download request and the later read all work under it. Nothing new is bookmarked per file.
  • Never blocking. The walk's coordinated read keeps .immediatelyAvailableMetadataOnly and now has a watchdog: if the coordination has not started within 15 s (another process holding a write, a provider not answering), the coordinator is cancelled and the walk ends incomplete, so the scan keeps what it had. Each walk lists its pages on its own serial queue, not the plugin's: a stuck enumerator holds up only its own walk, never listRoots, removeRoot, requestDownload or another root's walk. The Dart side gives up on startWalk and on each walk page after 2 minutes and on listRoots after 30 s (StorageException('timeout'); the scan then keeps what it had). Those are the limits: a listRoots stuck in the system (a bookmark resolving against a gone drive) still holds the plugin queue until the system answers, but no caller waits on it past 30 s. The scanner never opens a not-downloaded entry (openHandle refuses it by construction), nor a cover file that is not downloaded.
  • Listing. A new not-downloaded file is listed by its file name (the device's untagged fallback), greyed Not downloaded. A file read before and then evicted keeps its tags, size and audio fingerprint, so it is still listed by its title and its ratings and play counts are still found; eviction is not a move. While it stays away a rescan does not touch it; once it is local the next scan reads it, whatever its size and time say.
  • Art. A not-downloaded track offers no embedded-art source on its own file (the row keeps where its picture is, so the source and the cache key come back with the file); its folder's cover file is still offered. A walk that sees the cover file itself not downloaded clears it from the folder's tracks, even when the walk is incomplete. And on iOS the art cache's opener reads the source's download state first and refuses anything not on the phone, so a picture is never the reason iOS fetches a file, even before a scan has seen an eviction.
  • The Download action (requestDownload calls FileManager.startDownloadingUbiquitousItem(at:) for a file under a held root, and nothing else). Then downloadStates is polled every 2 s for the files asked for only, from metadata (downloaded, notDownloaded, downloading, failed from ubiquitousItemDownloadingError, missing), for at most 10 minutes, while the app is in front. When a file is downloaded the ordinary incremental scan runs, 2.5 s after the last file arrived (songs tapped one after another share one walk), and picks it up with its tags and art. If that scan still lists a file as not downloaded (its metadata lagging the state read), the row stays Downloading and it is scanned once more; then the library's word stands. A downloading error the file already had before the request is not reported as failed (iOS keeps the last error on an item until a new attempt replaces it): the plugin notes it at the request and reports only a different one.
  • Why a poll, not NSMetadataQuery. A metadata query sees only the app's own ubiquity container, which needs the iCloud entitlement and a container the app does not have; it cannot watch a folder the user picked in iCloud Drive. An NSFilePresenter per file would work but adds native state and lifecycle for the same result. Rescanning only on the next return to the front would leave the row stale while the user waits. The poll is a handful of metadata reads.
  • Data safety. startDownloadingUbiquitousItem is an OS action on the user's own file: iOS fetches its content unchanged. The read-only guard now forbids the iCloud calls that change a file's place or copy (setUbiquitous, evictUbiquitousItem) and allows the one download call, with its reason.
  • A queued song evicted later (lead call, 2026-11-26, under decisions 7 and 19). A song can be evicted after it was queued. neupod_audio's engine checks the file's download state from metadata (LocalFile.swift, the same three signs as the walk) before it opens the current item or pre-schedules the next, and fails one that is not on the phone as Not downloaded; the player skips it as it skips an unplayable song, so AVFoundation never fetches it. The lock screen reads embedded art only from a file on the phone. neupod_audio's privacy manifest declares the file timestamp API for its lstat. The simulator test queues a placeholder-only song before a real one: the real one plays.
  • Search rebuilds its index after every finished scan (it watches the library view), and its rows read Downloading once asked for.
  • Limits. requestDownload gives up after 30 s on the Dart side. The notes of a file's earlier downloading error are dropped once its request settles (downloaded, failed or gone) and capped at 256 files.
  • Tests. Unit: the scanner with walks that report files away and back; the state-to-step mapping and the controller with a fake platform; the row and the action in the shell. iOS simulator (integration_test/folder_access_test.dart): a real placeholder file in a bookmarked folder is walked, stated and scanned without being read, and a download request for it is refused or ignored without touching it. Also: a not-downloaded song's art has no source on its own file; a cover file evicted later is cleared after an incomplete walk; the iOS art opener refuses every state but downloaded; songs arriving together share a scan; the retry; a reload keeps the bar on the same song. A real evicted iCloud file, the status key and the dataless flag cannot be made on the simulator (no iCloud account; the flag is set only by the system): that is the owner's device check (PROGRESS, phase 3).

For the device check (phase 1) and phase 3:

  • Third-party File Provider extensions may present dataless files without ubiquitousItemDownloadingStatus; the walk then reports them as local, and reading them may make the provider fetch them. Check on the owner's iPhone with any provider apps installed.
  • Nested or duplicate roots (a folder picked inside another, or Documents picked as a folder) are not detected yet: their files would be scanned twice. Phase 3 (incremental rescan, removing a folder) handles it.

docs.title: 0005: Library database
docs.text: Status: Proposed (2026-11-21) · Owner: Architect

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Library of 20,000 tracks: artists, album artists, albums, discs, genres, compilations, embedded and folder art references.
  • Named playlists and On-The-Go, with .m3u8 import and export using paths relative to the library folder.
  • Rating (0 to 5), play count, last played and skip count per track, in the app's own database, surviving a rescan, a retag and a file move within the library.
  • Incremental rescan: size and mtime stored per file; a rescan with no changes in under ten seconds.
  • Search as you type over artists, albums and songs, grouped by kind.
  • Sort that matches the firmware's lib_collate_key() exactly (app/library/lib_collate.c): sort tag wins, a leading article skipped, ASCII case folded, Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A accents folded (ss, ae, oe, th, ij expand), then symbols (space first), digits, letters; key compared with memcmp, cut at 96 bytes.
  • Every query off the UI isolate; the scanner writes in bulk without stalling the UI.
  • Schema migrations that are generated or at least tested, since the database holds data the user cannot rebuild (ratings, playlists).
  • Testable in pure Dart unit tests on a Linux CI host, without a device or emulator.
  • Source-neutral track model (a track has a source and a location) so R2 (NAS) and R3 (device card) are additions.
  • Licence compatible with MPL-2.0 distribution on the App Store and Google Play; actively maintained.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
Facts from pub.dev and GitHub, checked 2026-11-21. Toolchain: Flutter 3.50.1, Dart 3.14.0.

Package Version (date) Licence · publisher Platforms FTS Off-UI isolate Migrations Host unit tests Maintained drift + sqlite3 2.35.4 (2026-11-08); sqlite3 3.9.1 (2026-11-08) MIT · simonbinder.eu (verified), Flutter Favorite Android, iOS, desktop, web FTS5 in the bundled SQLite on every platform NativeDatabase.createInBackground, computeWithDatabase make-migrations: schema snapshots, step-by-step code and generated tests Yes, NativeDatabase.memory() in dart test Yes: commits 2026-11-20 sqflite 2.4.6 (2026-11-10) BSD-2-Clause · tekartik.com, Flutter Favorite Android, iOS, macOS (desktop via sqflite_common_ffi) Uses the OS SQLite: FTS5 not enabled in Android's framework SQLite Platform channel / own thread Hand-written onUpgrade Via sqflite_common_ffi (a different engine path than production) Yes: commits 2026-11-15 ObjectBox 5.3.2 (2026-05-20); 6.0.0-preview.6 (2026-11-03) Apache-2.0 (binding; native core is a closed-source download) · objectbox.io Android, iOS, desktop No full-text search found; vector search only Yes Automatic model sync, UID-based Needs the native library downloaded on the host Yes: commits 2026-11-17 isar 3.1.0+1 (2023-04-25); 4.0.0-dev.14 (2023-08) Apache-2.0 · isar.dev all Word index Yes Implicit Native lib download No: last commit 2025-06-14, no release since 2023, README says v4 "not ready for production" isar_community 3.4.1 (2026-10-13) Apache-2.0 · isar-community.dev Android, iOS, desktop Word index (multi-entry) Yes Implicit Native lib download; README says run tests with -j 1 Fork "focusing primarily on bug fixes and small updates for version 3"; small (163 likes) realm 20.2.0 (2025-09-24) Apache-2.0 · realm.io Android, iOS, desktop Yes (RQL TEXT) Yes Schema version + callback Native Deprecated: README "We announced the deprecation of Atlas Device Sync + Realm SDKs in September 2024"; last commit 2025-10-23 sembast 3.10.1 (2026-11-09) BSD-3-Clause · tekartik.com all No Whole DB in memory, single isolate Manual Yes, pure Dart Yes hive / hive_ce hive 2.2.3 (2022-06-30); hive_ce 2.24.0 (2026-11-19) hive: unknown on pub.dev · hive_ce: Apache-2.0 / BSD-3 · iodesignteam.com all No Boxes in memory Manual adapters Yes hive: no; hive_ce: yes

drift. A typed layer over SQLite with reactive queries (watch()), which suits lists that update while a scan runs. Since sqlite3 3.x the SQLite library is supplied by a Dart build hook: prebuilt from upstream sources in the package's GitHub releases, checked by sha256, compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 among other options, and the same binary family on Android, iOS and Linux, so production and CI run the same engine. sqlite3_flutter_libs is now 0.6.0+eol ("Not used anymore, update to version 3.x of package:sqlite3"), and the drift docs say depending on it is no longer needed. FTS5 tables are declared in a .drift file with the fts5 module enabled in build.yaml. It needs build_runner codegen (drift_dev). We use that codegen because it gives compile-checked SQL and the migration tooling. Plain SQL is available when the query builder gets in the way. The maintainer is one very active person (Simon Binder), who also maintains sqlite3.

sqflite. Mature and simple, but it uses the operating system's SQLite. Android's framework SQLite does not enable FTS5 (Room users get no such module: FTS5 and are told to bundle SQLite). FTS4 would mean different SQL on each platform, and host tests would go through sqflite_common_ffi instead of the production path. It has no typed queries and no migration tooling.

ObjectBox, isar_community. Fast object stores, but neither has SQL-style joins and grouping for the artist/album/genre browse, nor a tested migration story for data the user cannot rebuild. ObjectBox has no full-text search, and its core is a binary download. isar is abandoned; isar_community is a small maintenance fork of v3 and too thin a base for a database we keep for years. Realm is deprecated. sembast and hive_ce keep data in memory and have no FTS or ordered secondary indexes, which rules them out at 20,000 tracks.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use drift 2.35 on sqlite3 3.9 (bundled SQLite through build hooks), with FTS5, opened in a background isolate. Do not depend on sqlite3_flutter_libs. Use drift_flutter only if its 0.3.x release has dropped the +eol dependencies by the time of the spike; otherwise open NativeDatabase.createInBackground(file) with path_provider for the path. It is the only option that meets every requirement: relational browse queries, FTS5 identical on both platforms, a background isolate, generated and tested migrations, and in-memory host tests running the production engine.

Shape of the schema (the library engineer owns the details):

  • sources(id, kind [local_folder | media_store | nas | device], uri_or_bookmark, display_name). R1 creates local_folder and, on Android, media_store (the shared music collection, decision 0012).
  • tracks(id, source_id, rel_path, size, mtime, track_key, title, title_sort_key BLOB, artist_id, album_id, genre_id, disc_no, track_no, year, duration_ms, codec, sample_rate, bit_depth, playable_code, art_ref), unique on (source_id, rel_path). Every track has a source and a location, so a NAS or device track is just another row.
  • artists, albums (with album artist, year, is_compilation), genres. Each has name, sort_name (the sort tag, if any) and sort_key BLOB (indexed).
  • track_stats(track_key PRIMARY KEY, rating, play_count, skip_count, last_played). Keyed by content, not by row or path, so it is never deleted when tracks are removed. "Reset ratings and play counts" is the only thing that clears it.
  • playlists(id, name, kind [otg | named], position) and playlist_entries(playlist_id, position, track_key, rel_path_hint).
  • search_fts as an FTS5 table (kind, name, ref_id, tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2', prefix='1 2 3'), rebuilt by the scanner. A query is prefix terms ("beat"*) grouped by kind.

Collation. Port lib_collate_key() byte for byte to a pure-Dart function in the domain layer (collateKey(name, sort) -> Uint8List, cut at 96 bytes), and store its output as an indexed BLOB. SQLite compares BLOBs with memcmp, and a shorter key that is a prefix sorts first, which is exactly lib_collate_cmp(). So ORDER BY sort_key gives the firmware's order with no custom collation registered per connection, and the fast-scroll letter is lib_collate_bucket() applied to the first byte. Unit tests reuse the firmware's cases in tests/test_library.c (collate_case_and_the, collate_diacritics, collate_classes, collate_sort_tag_wins). Ties break as the firmware does in app/library/lib_build.c (full key, then id).

Stable track key (track_key). A content fingerprint of the audio, not of the tags or the path, so it survives a retag, a rename and a move.

  • track_key = "a1:" + hex(SHA-256(codec ‖ audio_payload_length ‖ first 64 KiB of audio payload ‖ last 64 KiB of audio payload)). The audio payload is defined per container so that metadata never enters the hash. FLAC: the frames after the last metadata block. MP3: the frames between ID3v2 and any trailing ID3v1/APE/Lyrics3 tag. MP4/M4A/ALAC: the mdat contents. WAV: the data chunk. Ogg/Opus: the packet bodies of the audio pages, not page headers, because a longer comment header renumbers pages.
  • FLAC fast path: where STREAMINFO carries a non-zero MD5 of the decoded audio, use "f1:" + md5 + total_samples + sample_rate with no extra read. The firmware could compute this key cheaply too, which matters for R3 rating exchange.
  • Cost: about 128 KiB read per new or changed file, well inside the five-minute first-scan target. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are not read at all.
  • Move detection: a rescan diffs the walk against tracks by (source_id, rel_path). Paths that have disappeared are held as "missing" until the walk ends. Each new path gets a track_key. A new path whose key equals a missing row's key is a move, and that row's location is updated in place, keeping its id, queue references and playlist entries. Rows still missing at the end are deleted. Their track_stats stay, so a folder removed and added back gets its ratings back.
  • Rejected: path (breaks on a move); whole-file hash (breaks on a retag, and reading 150 GB is far too slow); tags plus duration (breaks on a retag, and collides for untagged files).
  • Known limits: byte-identical duplicates share one stats row (acceptable, and shown to be so in tests). A re-encode or re-rip is a new track. A one-to-one tag-plus-duration match within a single scan could carry stats over, but it is left out of R1 unless the owner asks for it.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• Build-time download. The sqlite3 hook downloads its prebuilt library from GitHub releases during flutter build and dart test. The app still makes no network connection at run time, but CI needs GitHub reachable, and builds depend on those release assets staying up. Fallbacks the hook supports: url_pattern to a mirror, or source: source to compile the SQLite amalgamation (public domain) ourselves. Escalate only if the owner objects to build-time downloads.
  • Codegen: build_runner for drift. Generated files are committed and CI checks they are current.
  • Single maintainer for drift and sqlite3. Both are very active, MIT, and SQL is portable, so a forced move to raw sqlite3 would be survivable.
  • Our own copy of SQLite adds about 1 to 2 MB per architecture to the app.
  • The key algorithm becomes a compatibility contract (it keys the user's ratings). It carries a version prefix (a1:, f1:), and changing it needs a migration that recomputes keys before stats are re-joined.
  • Writes from the scanner isolate must go through computeWithDatabase (or the same drift instance) so watch() streams in the UI see them.
  • Spec drift to raise with the lead: docs/ui.md says "A " and "An " are not ignored yet, but lib_collate.c already skips them. The app follows the code. The doc needs correcting by whoever owns firmware docs.

docs.title: To verify in the phase 1 spike
docs.text:
1. SELECT sqlite_version() and PRAGMA compile_options on an iOS simulator, an iOS device, an Android emulator (arm64 and x86_64) and Linux CI. CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fts5 succeeds on all of them.
  2. drift_flutter 0.3.1 with its +eol dependencies: does it pull a second SQLite or conflict with the hook? Decide between drift_flutter and plain NativeDatabase.createInBackground.
  3. App size delta and a clean release build on both platforms with no extra native configuration.
  4. dart test with NativeDatabase.memory() on GitHub's Linux runner. Measure the hook download time and whether it is cached.
  5. 20,000 generated tracks: bulk insert time through computeWithDatabase, Songs page query under 16 ms, FTS prefix query under 50 ms, and UI frame times during a scan.
  6. track_key stability: retag a FLAC, MP3, M4A and Ogg/Opus fixture (including growing the tag past its padding), rename and move them, and check the key is unchanged. Re-encode one and check the key changes.
  7. Are size and mtime reliable through Android SAF (DocumentFile.lastModified) and iOS security-scoped bookmarks? If not, choose another change signal.
  8. make-migrations round trip: v1 to v2 with a generated test, run in CI.

docs.title: Implementation (phase 1, 2026-11-22)
docs.text:
Built in mobile/lib/data/db/ (database), mobile/lib/data/scan/ (scanner, tag reader) and mobile/lib/domain/library/ (track model, collation, ports). Where it differs from the decision above, and why:

  • drift 2.35.4 and sqlite3 3.9.1 as decided, without drift_flutter and without path_provider. drift_flutter 0.3.1 still depends on the +eol sqlite3_flutter_libs and sqlcipher_flutter_libs, and path_provider 2.1 now pulls jni, jni_flutter, objective_c and ffi into the app for one directory name. The database is opened with NativeDatabase.createInBackground behind a LazyDatabase, in the directory that neupod_storage.appSupportPath() returns: Android noBackupFilesDir, iOS Application Support/library marked excluded from backup, never shown in Files or Finder. Excluded from backups because version 1 holds only what a rescan rebuilds; phase 3 revisits this when ratings and play counts arrive (they should survive a phone restore).
  • Phase 1 schema (version 1) is the subset the vertical slice needs: sources and tracks, with artist and album as text on the track, the title sort tag in title_sort, title_sort_key as an indexed BLOB (ORDER BY title_sort_key, id), reason_code (an UnreadableReason code, never English text) and scan_version per row (the tag reader and sort key the row was read with: a row from another version is read again on the next scan, once, whatever its size and mtime, and an unavailable folder or a partial walk does not keep re-reading the rest). The schema snapshot is committed in mobile/drift_schemas/library/drift_schema_v1.json. Migrations are stepwise from version 1, tested against the snapshots, and a downgrade is refused (decision 0008). The artists/albums/genres tables, track_key, track_stats, playlists and FTS5 come with their phase 3 and 6 items, as schema version 2 with a make-migrations test. Version 1 holds nothing the user cannot rebuild by rescanning.
  • Collation is ported exactly as decided (collateKey, compareKeys, collateBucket in domain/library/collation.dart). Besides the cases of tests/test_library.c, a golden table generated from the C source itself (scripts/app/gen-collate-golden.sh, 1,176 names: every Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A/B code point, articles, symbols, other scripts, long names) is checked byte for byte.
  • Tag reading (decision 0003), phase 1 subset: FLAC (STREAMINFO, Vorbis comments) and MP3 (ID3v2.2 to 2.4 text frames, Xing/Info with the LAME delay and padding, VBRI, else an estimate), title, artist, album, track number and duration, ported from app/audio/meta.c. Other formats are listed by file name until phase 3.
  • track_stats (phase 3, decision 0011, owner decision 20) is keyed by the firmware's path and size, not by track_key; a tag-free audio fingerprint (tracks.audio_fingerprint) carries it over a move or a retag. It is in its own database, stats.sqlite, which phone backups keep; the library database stays excluded from backups.

docs.title: 0006: State management and dependency wiring
docs.text: Status: Proposed (2026-11-21) · Owner: Architect

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Layers, each testable without the ones above it: pure-Dart domain, then data (database, scanner, tag reader, art cache), then audio (player, media session), then UI.
  • A long-running background scan with progress, cancel, and resume after the app is closed.
  • A player state stream (track, position, playing, queue, shuffle and repeat, output route) feeding Now Playing, the mini-player and the lock screen.
  • Reactive library lists (drift watch() streams, see 0005) that update while a scan runs.
  • Golden and widget tests for every screen in four style/mode combinations, at two sizes and the largest text size, using fakes and no platform plugins.
  • Built mostly by AI coding agents: we want a boring, well-documented approach with one idiomatic way to do each thing, and no heavy codegen unless it pays for itself.
  • MPL-2.0-compatible licence, actively maintained.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
Facts from pub.dev and GitHub, checked 2026-11-21. Toolchain: Flutter 3.50.1, Dart 3.14.0.

Package Version (date) Licence · publisher Last commit Layering Scan / player streams Test fakes Codegen Agent fit flutter_riverpod / riverpod 3.5.0 (2026-11-06) MIT · dash-overflow.net (riverpod is a Flutter Favorite) 2026-11-17 Providers wrap plain Dart services; lower layers never import it StreamProvider, AsyncNotifier ProviderScope(overrides:), ProviderContainer.test, overrideWithValue, overrideWithBuild Optional (riverpod_generator 4.0.10) Large docs. Risk: agents write 2.x idioms flutter_bloc / bloc flutter_bloc 9.1.1 (2025-05-02); bloc 9.2.1 (2026-05-12) MIT · bloclibrary.dev, Flutter Favorite 2026-11-19 Blocs and Cubits are plain Dart; DI through RepositoryProvider Cubit subscribes to the stream bloc_test 10.0.0, MockBloc None Very stable API since 8.x. More boilerplate (state classes, events) provider 6.1.5+1 (2025-08-19) MIT · dash-overflow.net, Flutter Favorite 2026-09-29 InheritedWidget sugar StreamProvider, ChangeNotifier Wrap in providers None Stable, but its author points new work to Riverpod. Weak async and disposal story signals / signals_flutter 7.1.0 (2026-05-29) Apache-2.0 · rodydavis.com 2026-11-06 Fine-grained reactive values Stream to signal adapters Manual None Small user base (26k downloads in 30 days), one maintainer, few examples ChangeNotifier / ValueNotifier + get_it (+ injectable, watch_it) get_it 9.3.0 (2026-09-19); injectable 3.0.0 (2026-04-20); watch_it 2.5.0 (2026-09-19) MIT · flutter-it.dev, codeness.ly 2026-09-29 Flutter SDK types; a global locator Hand-written StreamSubscription GetIt.I.reset() and re-register per test injectable is codegen Simple, but a global locator leaks state between parallel tests, and loading/error/dispose are hand-rolled each time

Riverpod 3. Major version 3.0 (2025) merged the AutoDispose and Family variants into a single Notifier and a single Ref. It added ProviderContainer.test, overrideWithBuild, WidgetTester.container and automatic retry of failed providers, and moved StateNotifierProvider, StateProvider and ChangeNotifierProvider to package:riverpod/legacy.dart. Every docs page shows a hand-written form next to the generator form, so codegen is not required. Overrides are the cleanest way to swap a fake LibraryRepository or Player into one golden test without a global locator. StreamProvider maps directly onto drift watch() and the player state stream. The main risk is that agents trained on Riverpod 2 will reach for StateNotifier, AutoDisposeNotifier or ref.watch inside callbacks.

bloc. The most explicit and stable option, with excellent docs and bloc_test. It costs one state class per screen, and usually an event class too. It also puts a second DI mechanism (RepositoryProvider, built on provider) next to the blocs. A good choice, but more ceremony than this app needs, and dependency overrides in widget tests are clumsier than Riverpod's.

ChangeNotifier + get_it. Least to learn, but every async load, error state and disposal is hand-written. The global locator has to be reset carefully for parallel widget tests, and injectable's codegen does not pay for itself in an app with about a dozen services.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use flutter_riverpod 3.5 without code generation, and only in the UI and the composition root. Domain, data and audio do not import Riverpod: they expose plain Dart classes, Streams and Futures behind interfaces declared in domain. Providers live in one place per feature on the UI side and do three jobs: build the real service (or a fake, via override), adapt streams (StreamProvider), and hold UI-facing state (Notifier / AsyncNotifier).

Rules for agents (to go into mobile/README.md for contributors and be enforced in review):

  • Use Provider, FutureProvider, StreamProvider, NotifierProvider and AsyncNotifierProvider, with .family and .autoDispose where needed. No package:riverpod/legacy.dart, no StateNotifier, StateProvider or ChangeNotifierProvider, no riverpod_generator, no hooks_riverpod.
  • ref.watch in build, ref.read in callbacks, ref.listen for one-shot effects (panels).
  • Business rules stay in domain or data, never in a Notifier. A Notifier forwards calls and maps state.
  • The scan is a data-layer LibraryScanner with Stream<ScanProgress> and cancel(). The UI reads it through a StreamProvider and calls cancel through ref.read. Running when the app is closed (WorkManager on Android; on iOS the scan resumes at next launch, owner decision 8) is a data/platform concern, not a Riverpod one.
  • The player is an audio-layer Player interface exposing Stream<PlayerState>. A single playerStateProvider (StreamProvider) feeds every screen.
  • Tests: ProviderContainer.test(overrides: [...]) for Notifiers. Widget and golden tests wrap screens in ProviderScope(overrides: [libraryRepositoryProvider.overrideWithValue(FakeLibraryRepository(...)), ...]), with retry disabled so failures surface at once.
  • Add riverpod_lint 3.2.0 (MIT) if it runs cleanly with the analyzer that Flutter 3.50 uses. Otherwise review enforces the rules above.

Why: it keeps the lower layers framework-free and so testable in plain dart test. Overrides make the golden matrix cheap. Drift and player streams plug in without glue code. There is no codegen beyond drift's.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• Agent drift to Riverpod 2 APIs is the main risk. Mitigations: the rule list above, the lint, and the reviewer checking imports. If it keeps happening after phase 1, fall back to flutter_bloc Cubits, which this layering allows without touching domain, data or audio.
  • Riverpod has had a breaking major (2 to 3) within the last two years, so pin ^3.5.0 and treat a 4.0 as a planned migration.
  • Automatic retry (on by default in 3.x) can hide a failing database open behind repeated retries. Set the ProviderScope retry to none for providers that open resources, and in all tests.
  • One maintainer (Remi Rousselet), very active. MIT licence.

docs.title: To verify in the phase 1 spike
docs.text:
1. ProviderScope overrides plus a golden test of a list screen fed by a FakeLibraryRepository, running headless on Linux CI.
  2. Scan progress through a StreamProvider while drift watch() lists update, with no dropped frames at 20,000 tracks.
  3. playerStateProvider driving Now Playing and surviving the app going to the background and back.
  4. riverpod_lint 3.2.0 works with Flutter 3.50.1's analyzer (dart analyze clean, no plugin errors).
  5. Retry disabled in tests: a provider that throws fails the test at once.

docs.text:
mobile/

    main.dart                 # runApp(ProviderScope(child: NeuPodApp()))

      providers.dart          # infrastructure providers: database, scanner, player, clock, file access
    domain/                   # pure Dart, no Flutter imports (enforced by a test that scans imports)

      collation/              # collateKey(), bucket() - port of lib_collate.c
      queue/                  # queue, shuffle, repeat, skip-back rule
      playlists/              # m3u8 parse and write
      ports/                  # interfaces: LibraryRepository, StatsRepository, Player, LibraryScanner, FolderAccess
    data/                     # implements domain ports; may import Flutter plugins, never UI
      db/                     # drift database, tables, .drift files (FTS5), migrations, generated code
      scan/                   # scanner isolate, tag reading and folder fallbacks, track_key
      art/                    # art cache
      platform/               # folder pickers, SAF and bookmarks
    audio/                    # implements Player; media session, interruptions, output route
    ui/
      style/                  # Classic/Modern tokens, skins, Montserrat, Lucide
      components/             # rows, headers, rail, panels
      features/
        home/  browse/  album/  now_playing/  queue/  search/  playlists/  settings/
          <feature>_screen.dart
          <feature>_providers.dart   # feature-level Notifiers and StreamProviders
  test/                       # mirrors lib/ one-to-one
    domain/ ...               # plain `dart test`-style unit tests
    data/ ...                 # drift NativeDatabase.memory(), scanner on generated fixture trees
    audio/ ...                # Player against fake platform channels
    ui/ ...                   # widget tests with ProviderScope overrides
    goldens/                  # per screen x {Classic, Modern} x {Light, Dark} x {small, large, max text}
    fakes/                    # FakeLibraryRepository, FakePlayer, FakeScanner, FakeFolderAccess (shared)
    drift/                    # migration tests generated by make-migrations
  integration_test/           # device/simulator flows: pick, scan, browse, play, background, resume

Dependency rule: domain imports nothing from this app. data and audio import domain only. ui imports domain, and app/providers.dart imports everything. Riverpod appears only under app/ and ui/. A unit test in test/architecture_test.dart reads the import lines and fails on a violation.

docs.title: 0007: Haptics and the system volume
docs.text: Status: Proposed (2026-11-22) · Owner: UI engineer 2

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Owner decision 9: wheel detents are light haptic ticks and button presses are firmer haptic clicks. Owner decision 10: on Now Playing the wheel sets the phone's system volume.
  • The device view design (docs/design/2026-11-21-app-device-view, section 5) names a platform API for each haptic event and asks for the names to be checked against current documentation. It also asks for one generator per kind, prepared in advance on iOS, at most 30 detent ticks a second, and respect for the system setting and an in-app Haptics setting.
  • Minimum OS (owner): iOS 18, Android 10 (API 29). Toolchain: Xcode with the iOS 27 SDK, Android compileSdk 36.

docs.title: What the documentation says
docs.text:
Checked 2026-11-22. Apple's pages were read through their documentation JSON, which the HTML pages load.

Event (design) iOS, as designed Checked Android, as designed Checked Detent UISelectionFeedbackGenerator.selectionChanged() iOS 10, current. The docs say: use it "only when the selection changes", which fits a detent CLOCK_TICK; SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK where available CLOCK_TICK is API 21. SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK is API 34: "very soft … if the device can't make a suitably soft vibration, then it may not make any vibration" Button or centre down UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .rigid), intensity 0.8 .rigid is iOS 13; impactOccurred(intensity:) is iOS 13, range 0 to 1 VIRTUAL_KEY API 5. Android's own key-press example uses it on down Button or centre up .light, intensity 0.5 iOS 10 VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE API 27, so it is available at our minimum. Used on up in the same example A hold takes effect .medium iOS 10 LONG_PRESS API 3 End of a list .soft, once iOS 13 REJECT, once API 30, which is above our minimum of 29

Two corrections to the design's table:

  1. iOS initialisers are deprecated in the iOS 27 SDK. UIImpactFeedbackGenerator.init(style:) and UIFeedbackGenerator.init() are marked deprecated in iOS 27.0. UISelectionFeedbackGenerator() uses the latter, so it is deprecated too. The replacements are init(style:view:) and init(view:), both iOS 17.5. Our minimum is iOS 18, so the plugin uses the view-attached forms directly, with no availability check. The generator classes and selectionChanged() / impactOccurred(intensity:) are not deprecated.
  2. REJECT needs a fallback on Android 10. On API 29 the end of a list uses LONG_PRESS, the same as a hold.

One clarification: the table's "API 34" applies only to SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK; CLOCK_TICK is API 21.

System setting. - iOS: the generators only ask. The system plays the haptic only on hardware that has it, with the app in the foreground, and with the system Haptics setting on. - Android: View.performHapticFeedback honours the user's touch-feedback setting by default and needs no VIBRATE permission. Since API 33 only privileged apps can override that setting (FLAG_IGNORE_GLOBAL_SETTING is deprecated); we never ask to.

So obeying the system setting needs no code. The in-app Haptics setting is applied in Dart, before any call.

Preparing (iOS). prepare() is optional but recommended. The Taptic Engine stays ready "for a short period of time (typically seconds)". Calling it immediately before a haptic does not help. Prepare again after each haptic when more are likely.

Volume. - Android: AudioManager.adjustStreamVolume(STREAM_MUSIC, ADJUST_RAISE | ADJUST_LOWER, 0) moves one step. Flags 0 omits FLAG_SHOW_UI, so the system volume panel is not asked for. It does nothing on fixed-volume devices (isVolumeFixed(), API 21). The step count is getStreamMaxVolume less getStreamMinVolume (API 28). - iOS: there is no public API to set the system volume. AVAudioSession.outputVolume is read-only. Apple DTS (2020) called digging into MPVolumeView's view hierarchy unreliable. Apple WWDR (August 2026) says a program cannot change the system volume without user interaction. Developers report the hidden-slider trick still in use, but I found no confirmation that setting the slider works on iOS 18, 26 or 27. "16 steps, 1/16 each" is community knowledge, not documented.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
An in-repo plugin, mobile/packages/neupod_device (Kotlin and Swift through Pigeon 30, as Flutter 3.50's plugin template does, at the version the other in-repo plugins use), covers both haptics and volume. It was named neupod_device, not neupod_haptics, because it carries both.

Event iOS Android Detent UISelectionFeedbackGenerator(view:), selectionChanged() SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK on API 34+, else CLOCK_TICK Down UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .rigid, view:), impactOccurred(intensity: 0.8) VIRTUAL_KEY Up UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light, view:), intensity 0.5 VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE Hold took effect .medium LONG_PRESS End of a list .soft REJECT on API 30+, else LONG_PRESS
  • iOS generators. One per kind, attached to the key window, made when the app's scene becomes active. All five are prepared when the wheel is touched. Each is prepared again after it is used, together with the ones likely to follow: light and medium after a press, soft after a detent.
  • Android. The plugin calls performHapticFeedback on the activity's decor view.
  • Rate limit and setting. In Dart (DeviceFeedback): detents at most 30 a second, the rest dropped; nothing at all when the in-app Haptics setting is off. A press cancelled by becoming a turn gets no release haptic.
  • Volume.
  • Android: adjustStreamVolume with flags 0, then the volume read back.
  • iOS: a hidden MPVolumeView, a 1x1 view at alpha 0.01 inside the key window. It is created as soon as the scene is active, because a freshly added view needs a moment before its slider works. Its UISlider is set to the next 1/16 step. It sits in the window because, by community knowledge rather than any Apple documentation, the slider only works there and the system HUD stays away only then. After 150 ms, AVAudioSession.outputVolume is read back.
  • Both return the volume read back from the system, never the target. They also return a status: ok, noSlider (iOS), noEffect (the volume did not move although it was not at its limit) or fixed (Android fixed-volume devices). The app sees it as SystemVolume.status / failed, so Now Playing knows when the workaround fails and the owner's fallback can apply (owner decision 10).
  • Click sound. A seam only (ClickSoundPort, silent). The setting exists (Off by default) and nothing plays yet.
  • Verifying. Emulators and simulators cannot vibrate, so every call is logged:
  • Android, in debuggable builds only, under the tag neupod_device (adb logcat -s neupod_device). Release builds log nothing.
  • iOS, at debug level, under subsystem net.stuartfraser.neupod, category device. The feel is for the owner's device check.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• The iOS volume workaround is unsupported by Apple and may not work on iOS 27. Owner decision 10 says: if Apple breaks it, the fallback is to be asked for, not guessed. This must be checked on the owner's iPhone (iOS 27) at the first device check. If it fails, the step comes back with status noSlider or noEffect and the level as read back, so the app can tell. Options for the owner then: a visible MPVolumeView on Now Playing, an app-level volume on the player, or no wheel volume on iOS.
  • It is also an App Review risk, which stays with the owner at submission, like Open question 1 of the spec.
  • SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK may be silent on phones whose motor cannot make a very soft tick. If the owner's Pixel feels nothing, switch the detent to CLOCK_TICK on all versions. That is a one-line change in NeupodDevicePlugin.kt.
  • Android's REJECT fallback on API 29 feels the same as a hold.
  • EU safe media volume. On phones sold in the EU (and others with the setting), Android refuses to raise the media volume past the safe-hearing limit on headphones until the user confirms in a system dialog. A raise from the wheel at that point does not move the volume. The plugin reports it as noEffect. The system may also show its own warning, which the app cannot suppress. Do Not Disturb can block changes the same way.

docs.title: 0008: Library database migrations
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-11-22) · Owner: Library engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Phase 1 shipped schema version 1 (sources, tracks) with an onUpgrade that dropped and recreated every table. That was fine for a cache a rescan rebuilds, but phase 3 and 6 add data the user cannot rebuild: ratings, play counts, last played, skip counts, playlists (decision 0005).
  • Version 1 was never released: no store or TestFlight build, only debug builds on the owner's and the CI's devices.
  • drift 2.35.4 / drift_dev 2.35.3 (pinned in mobile/pubspec.lock). The current drift docs (drift.simonbinder.eu/migrations, checked 2026-11-22) recommend dart run drift_dev make-migrations, configured in build.yaml: it writes a schema snapshot per version, a <database>.steps.dart file with a typed stepByStep helper, and a migration test on the generated SchemaVerifier.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
1. Reset the baseline: delete the v1 snapshot and start the migration history at the first schema with user-owned tables. Saves nothing (the v1 snapshot already exists and is exactly the schema in the code) and leaves every debug install of v1 with no path forward except a drop.
  2. Keep v1 as the baseline and migrate stepwise from it. A database at v1 upgrades like any other.
  3. Keep drop-and-recreate until the first user-owned table. Rejected: the step that adds that table is exactly when a drop would lose data, and the drop code would have to be removed in the same PR that first needs it gone.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Option 2. Version 1 stays the baseline, unchanged, and every later version is a drift step.

  • mobile/build.yaml names the database (library: lib/data/db/library_database.dart), the snapshot folder (drift_schemas/) and the test folder (test/drift/).
  • onUpgrade calls stepByStep() from the generated lib/data/db/library_database.steps.dart (through a getter, as drift advises), then PRAGMA foreign_key_check, which throws if a key is broken. With one version there are no steps yet, so any upgrade path throws; make-migrations regenerates the file with a from1To2 parameter when version 2 exists.
  • One transaction; a failure rolls back; user_version is unchanged. drift 2.35.4 does not wrap onUpgrade in a transaction, and writes user_version only after beforeOpen succeeds. So PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF runs first (the pragma does nothing inside a transaction), then all the steps and the foreign key check run in one transaction, as in drift's documented pattern (VersionedSchema.runMigrationSteps). If any step or the check throws, the whole upgrade rolls back, the database keeps its old schema, rows and user_version, and the next launch starts again from there. beforeOpen turns foreign keys back on. make-migrations itself writes nothing but the snapshot while there is only one version, so the steps file and the test helpers for v1 were generated with drift_dev schema steps and drift_dev schema generate --data-classes --companions, which make-migrations overwrites from then on.
  • Downgrades are refused. A database from a newer build (a newer user_version) makes drift's step runner throw a StateError, and nothing is changed or dropped. Stores do not downgrade apps; a developer who installs an older debug build over a newer one clears the app's data.
  • Tests (mobile/test/drift/library/migration_test.dart, written once by hand; make-migrations never overwrites an existing test file):
  • the current schemaVersion has a snapshot and it is the newest, and a fresh database matches it (a table changed without a new version fails);
  • every earlier version migrates to every later one and matches its snapshot (drift's generated pattern);
  • every earlier version migrates to the current one with every row kept: one row is written in each table of the old version (parents first, by foreign key, with valid references), and after the migration each table still has it, with the same value in each column still present. A step that drops a column on purpose lists it in _droppedOnPurpose;
  • a database from a newer version is refused and keeps its rows and its user_version;
  • a failed upgrade (a step that throws part-way, or one that breaks a foreign key), injected through LibraryDatabase.withStepsForTesting, leaves the schema, the rows and user_version exactly as they were.
  • Guard (mobile/test/data/db/library_tables_guard_test.dart): fails if any table other than sources and tracks exists. It is updated in the same PR that adds the first user-owned table, and that PR must bring its migration step. The first user-owned table, track_stats (decision 0011), went into its own database instead, stats.sqlite, so that phone backups keep it (owner decision 20); it follows this note's rules with its own snapshots (drift_schemas/stats/), tests (test/drift/stats/) and guard. make-migrations cannot read _testVersion ?? n from schemaVersion: write the bare number while it runs.

docs.title: Adding version 2
docs.text:
1. Change the tables in library_database.dart and bump schemaVersion to 2.
  2. dart run drift_dev make-migrations (from mobile/): writes drift_schemas/library/drift_schema_v2.json, regenerates library_database.steps.dart and test/drift/library/generated/.
  3. Add from1To2: (m, schema) async { ... } to stepByStep(...) in _upgrade, using schema (the v2 snapshot), not the live tables.
  4. dart run build_runner build; run flutter test test/drift test/data/db. If the step changes existing columns (not just adds tables or columns), add a data test with the generated v1/v2 classes as well.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every schema change costs a snapshot, a step and a passing migration test; the data test runs for each old version with no extra code.
  • The database stays excluded from backups for now (decision 0005); that is revisited with the first user-owned table.

docs.title: 0009: The Android scan survives the app being closed
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-11-23) · Owner: Android platform engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Spec, "The library" (owner decision 8): the scan runs in the background, shows progress, can be cancelled, and survives the app being closed on Android. On iOS it resumes at the next launch, which is already done.
  • Today the scan is Dart code in the app's Flutter engine: LibraryScanController (mobile/lib/app/library_scan_providers.dart) drives LocalLibraryScanner, which walks folders through neupod_storage (SAF) and writes through drift to the one database (decision 0005, single writer). When the user swipes the app away, FlutterActivity destroys its engine with it and the scan stops. The next launch starts it again, and unchanged files are skipped.
  • The controller's rules must hold: one scan at a time, a restart waits for the previous scan's last write, Cancel keeps what was written.
  • Minimum Android 10 (API 29); target and compile SDK 36; the owner's phone runs Android 17 (API 37). The CI emulator is API 29. The release manifest must not ask for INTERNET.

docs.title: What the documentation says
docs.text:
Checked 2026-11-23 (developer.android.com).

  • Foreground service types (Android 14+): each foreground service declares a type and its permission. dataSync ("import or export operations", "local file processing") needs FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC, an install-time permission, and has no runtime prerequisites. mediaProcessing (Android 15+) is for "operations on media assets, like converting media to different formats", which a tag scan is not. shortService is about 3 minutes.
  • Android 15 time limit: dataSync (and mediaProcessing) may run 6 hours in 24 while the app is in the background. Then the system calls Service.onTimeout(int, int) and the service has a few seconds to call stopSelf(), or the app gets a RemoteServiceException. The timer resets when the user brings the app to the front, and a service started while the app is in front gets the full 6 hours after it goes to the background. Once the time is used up, starting another throws ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException.
  • Starting from the background (Android 12+) throws ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException; a visible app may start one.
  • Notifications (Android 13+): POST_NOTIFICATIONS is a runtime permission. "Apps don't need to request the POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission in order to launch a foreground service." Without it the service runs, and its notice is shown in the Task Manager, not the drawer. Media-session notifications are exempt, which is why playback (decision 0002) never asked for it. The documentation advises asking in context, after a user action.
  • Android 16 applies the job runtime quota to jobs that start while the app is visible and to jobs that run beside a foreground service. That covers WorkManager's expedited and ordinary work.
  • Android 17: its behaviour changes cover none of foreground services, dataSync or task removal. Its background audio hardening applies only to apps that target API 37.
  • Swiping from Recents: AOSP does not kill a process that has a foreground service when its task is removed. The activity is destroyed; the service, with stopWithTask false (the default), keeps running.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
1. Foreground service (dataSync) that keeps the app's own engine. The service holds the process at foreground priority. When the activity goes away mid-scan, it hands its engine to a keeper instead of destroying it. The scan carries on in the engine it started in. The next activity takes the engine back.
  2. Foreground service that runs the scan in a second, headless engine (a Dart entry point started by the service). It survives as well, but there are then two Dart isolates with two drift connections to one SQLite file. The single writer rule and the controller's "a restart waits for the previous write" would need cross-engine locking. The app's UI would have to learn the progress from the other engine over a channel. And neupod_storage and drift would have to start in an engine without an activity. That is a second app inside the app.
  3. WorkManager, expedited or long-running. An expedited job is short, and Android 16 puts jobs started while the app is visible under the runtime quota. A long-running worker is a foreground service anyway (setForeground with a dataSync type), plus a new AndroidX dependency, and it still needs a Dart engine to run the scan: option 2's problems, with WorkManager on top.
  4. The PlaybackService (Media3) hosts it. Its type is mediaPlayback, which is for playing media; holding it in the foreground to scan with nothing playing misuses the type (and the store's declaration). It would also tie the scan to the media session's lifecycle. Rejected.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Option 1. It is the only one that keeps today's scan as it is: one engine, one controller, one database connection, and the progress row in Settings > Library unchanged. Android only gains a service that keeps the process and the engine alive.

  • Service. ScanService (app module, foregroundServiceType="dataSync", not exported). It does no work: the scan runs in Dart. It starts when the controller starts a scan (always while the app is in front: launch, return to front, Update Library, a folder added). It stops when the scan has stopped writing (done, failed or cancelled). START_NOT_STICKY: if the process dies anyway, the next launch scans again as it does today.
  • Keeping the engine. MainActivity.onDestroy asks whether a scan is running. If one is, shouldDestroyEngineWithHost() returns false and the engine goes to EngineKeeper. provideFlutterEngine() hands it to the next activity, so reopening the app shows the same scan with the same progress. If the scan ends with no activity, the kept engine is destroyed: its plugins detach (the audio plugin's controller releases the playback service), and the process is left with nothing running. When no scan runs, the engine lives and dies with the activity, exactly as before.
  • Never a second engine while a scan runs. On Android 10 and 11, Back finishes the root activity, and its onDestroy can come after the user has launched the app again. A new activity therefore takes the scan's engine whether it is kept or still attached to the finishing activity (ScanRuntime.engineForNewActivity). Flutter then detaches the old activity, which must not destroy the engine, because shouldDestroyEngineWithHost() is false for the scan's engine. So no second Dart app starts a second scan (a second writer on the database), and the first scan's end cannot stop the service under another.
  • Activity state in plugins. A plugin that waits for an activity result must not keep waiting once the activity is gone for good, since the engine may live on. neupod_storage now ends a pending folder pick as cancelled in onDetachedFromActivity (not on a configuration change, whose new activity gets the result). Without that, a swipe-away with the picker open would leave Dart's pickFolder hanging and every later Add Folder refused as "busy" for the life of the process. neupod_device keeps only the activity, which it clears; the audio plugin is not activity-aware.
  • Notification. Channel "Library scan", low importance (no sound). It shows the firmware's words: title "Building library", text "N found · N read" (scanProgressLabel, the same text as Settings > Library), an indeterminate bar (the total is unknown until the walk ends, as on the firmware's sweeping bar), and a Cancel action. Tapping it opens the app. Dart sends the text, so the wording lives in one place. Updates are posted at most every 500 ms (Android drops a package's notification updates past a few a second), always with the newest text. Android 12+ defers a foreground service's notification by up to 10 seconds, so a scan of unchanged files (well under a second) never shows one.
  • Cancel. The action starts the service with a cancel intent. The plugin asks Dart to cancel, and Dart runs the controller's own cancel() (the same path as the Select key in Settings > Library). Once the cancelled scan's last write has finished, Dart stops the service. If the same scan is still running 10 seconds after Cancel (Dart did not answer), the service stops anyway and a kept engine is released, with a log line.
  • One scan at a time. Unchanged: the controller still owns the scan. It tells the service (through ScanKeepAlive, a domain port; no-op on iOS and in tests): started when a scan starts, progress as it goes, and stopped only once the scan has stopped writing. A restart sends a second started (the service is already up) and no stopped in between. A cancel followed at once by a start leaves the service up for the new scan. Every stopped first waits for any scan still stopping (a cancel, a restart, a failure) to finish its last write.
  • POST_NOTIFICATIONS. Declared, and asked for on Android 13+ only when the user started the scan (Update Library or a folder added). It is never asked at launch or on return to the front. Android stops showing the prompt after two refusals. Without the permission the scan still survives; its notice is in the Task Manager only. This is the one runtime permission added. The others (FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC) are install-time, and the release manifest still has no INTERNET.
  • Limits. If the service cannot start (the app was not visible, or the 6-hour budget is spent), the scan runs in the app as before. On Android 15+, onTimeout stops the service and destroys a kept engine. An open app keeps scanning, and the next launch picks up from the database. A scan the user starts with the app in front resets the budget.
  • iOS is unchanged. scanServiceOverrides() installs the service on Android only; everywhere else the port does nothing.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• JVM (android/app/src/test/.../ScanSessionTest.kt, ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest, now run in CI's android job): the session (start once, stop once, update throttling with the newest text, nothing after stop) and the engine keeper (hand-over, destroy at scan end with no activity, the test hook).
  • Dart (test/app/scan_keep_alive_test.dart): the controller's calls in order for done, failure, restart, cancel then start, the notification's Cancel, and app close. The service stops only after the cancelled scan's write has ended. Also covered: the channel messages and their firmware words, a failing channel, and Android-only installation.
  • Instrumentation on the CI emulator (integration_test/scan_service_test.dart):
  • First test: a scan starts through the controller with the real service, and Add Folder's picker is opened. The test calls finishAndRemoveTask() on the activity, as swiping it away does. It then checks that the engine was kept, the service is running and the open pick ended as cancelled. The scan then completes (its marker file, done with no error, progress after the activity went), and the service stops.
  • Second test: the app is launched again, and the new activity takes the kept engine. A new scan starts and the app is swiped away and launched again mid-scan; the scan's progress goes on in the same engine. Add Folder's picker opens again (not "busy"). Swiped away again with the picker open, the pick ends as cancelled. The notification's Cancel (the same intent as its action) then cancels the scan, and the service stops. The app is closed while the scan runs: closed after it ended, the engine is rightly destroyed, and the Dart test in it could not report.
  • CI's manifest check also requires FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC and the service's dataSync type. The scanner there is a stand-in: an emulator under instrumentation cannot grant a SAF folder. Debug builds only expose debugFinishActivity, debugRelaunch, debugNotificationCancel, debugState and debugKeepEngineAfterScan; the last keeps the engine after the scan so the test can report. Its limit: the system never kills an instrumented process, so it proves the engine and the scan outlive the activity, not that the foreground service keeps the process from being killed. That part is AOSP's documented behaviour, and it is checked on the owner's phone. If the engine were not kept, the test could not report, and the run would show up as the script's per-file timeout, not as a failed assertion.

docs.title: Consequences and risks
docs.text:
• A swiped-away app whose scan is still running keeps its whole engine in memory (tens of MB) until the scan ends. That is the cost of one engine, and it ends with the scan.
  • OEM task killers that ignore foreground services (some vendors) still stop the scan; it resumes at the next launch.
  • dataSync may be narrowed in a future Android. Google's migration guide points data transfers to user-initiated data transfer jobs, which need a network constraint and so do not fit a local scan. Revisit when a new target SDK changes the type.
  • Owner check: the notification and the swipe-away on the Pixel 7 (Android 17) at the next device check.

docs.title: 0010: Album art and the art cache
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-11-23) · Owner: Library engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Gate 1 (owner, 2026-11-23): no album art anywhere, on iOS or Android, in the screens or on the lock screen. The screens and the player could show art; the library supplied none.
  • Firmware behaviour is the rule. The device picks art in app/audio/meta.c (meta_art_offer), app/audio/art.c (art_sources, art_folder_rank, art_folder_pick, art_decode over TJpgDec) and app/runtime/art_service.c (find_and_decode); the library's album header and Cover Flow ask by the album's first song (ui_library.c).
  • The spec puts an art cache in the data layer and asks for work off the UI isolate and for bounded memory.
  • The scan stays header-only (decision 0003): it records where a picture is, never its bytes.

docs.title: The firmware's rules, ported exactly (mobile/lib/domain/library/art_rules.dart)
docs.text:
1. Embedded picture: every FLAC PICTURE block and ID3v2 APIC/PIC frame is offered; a JPEG beats a PNG beats anything else, a front cover (type 3) adds one, the first wins a tie. The kind comes from the first bytes, not the mime. ID3 frames that are compressed, encrypted or unsynchronised (frame or tag), and descriptions past the first 160 bytes, are skipped. MP4 covr items (covr_item, app/audio/mp4.c): every data box is offered as a front cover, whatever its type code says.
  2. Sources in order: the embedded picture if it is a JPEG, then a cover file in the track's own folder. One that does not decode gives way to the next.
  3. Cover file names: cover.jpg, then folder.jpg, then front.jpg, ASCII case folded. No .jpeg, no PNG.
  4. Decodable means TJpgDec would decode it (mobile/lib/data/art/firmware_jpeg.dart ports jd_prepare and art_decode's checks): baseline (SOF0) only, 8-bit tables, 1 or 3 components, Y sampling 1x1, 2x2 or 2x1, tables within its 4096-byte pool (each definition takes pool, so repeated tables overflow it), at most 5120 px a side, no side that scales to nothing at the decoder's scale (the 160 px builds, NEUPOD_ART_HIRES), and compressed data that runs to a marker before the picture ends: TJpgDec reads 16 bits ahead, so a cut anywhere in the scan, even only the end marker missing, fails there. Progressive JPEGs and PNGs are not shown, as on the device.
  5. TJpgDec ignores EXIF orientation (APP1) and the Adobe colour transform (APP14): the app blanks both segments before decoding, so a cover is the same way up and the same colours as on the device.
  6. An album's art is its first song's in album order; Now Playing and the lock screen show the playing track's own.

Checked against the C compiled for the host: scripts/app/gen_art_vectors.py (with scripts/app/art_vectors.c) writes mobile/test/fixtures/art/expected.tsv, which test/data/scan/art_vectors_test.dart reads. For each cover file the C also gives the thumbnail's shape and its colour at the centres of its quarters, which the app's decode must match (so a rotation or a colour transform shows).

Where the app cannot see what the device sees, a lead decision as for walk order (drift_library_view.dart): names of one rank in one folder (Folder.jpg and folder.jpg on a case-sensitive disk) are taken in byte order, since the card's directory order is not visible; a cover file not downloaded from iCloud is not read (owner decision 7), so the folder has none, which is what the device shows for a cover file it cannot decode.

Known differences:

  • The device skips a cover file with the FAT hidden or system attribute (art_service.c scan_next, line 380: nfs_dirent_hidden); Windows Media Player writes Folder.jpg that way. Neither Android's folder access nor iOS shows FAT attributes, so the app uses such a file (it skips only names starting with a dot, as the device does).
  • The app reads at most 32 MB of a picture (maxArtBytes); the firmware has no byte limit, only its 5120 px one.

docs.title: Options considered for decoding
docs.text:
Option Off the UI isolate Tests Cost image 4.13.1 (pure Dart, MIT, Brendan Duncan; released 2026-11-14) in Isolate.run Yes, all of it Plain flutter test, same code on both platforms A package (with archive 4.7.1 MIT, posix 6.5.4 MIT); slower than native decoders dart:ui instantiateImageCodec + toByteData Decodes on engine threads, but the work is driven from the UI isolate and encoding a file needs the raster thread Needs the engine (runAsync, real codecs) None Native (UIImage / BitmapFactory) through a plugin Yes Device only Two implementations to keep equal

Decision: image, in a background isolate, one picture at a time, decoded at the largest reduced scale (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) that keeps the long side at 600 px or more, as art_decode picks its own (a 5120 px cover would be about 79 MB of pixels at full scale).
