Every picture the device accepts is a baseline JPEG at most 5120 px a side, so the pure-Dart decoder's speed is acceptable for a one-off per album.

docs.title: The cache (mobile/lib/data/art/art_cache.dart)
docs.text:
• In art/ under the plugin's private support directory (excluded from backups, like the library database).
  • Two JPEGs per picture: 192 px (rows, album header, Music menu: drawn up to 96 design px, decoded at twice that) and 600 px (Home, Now Playing and Cover Flow up to 220 design px; the lock screen). Shrunk to fit, never enlarged, never the original.
  • Keyed by a hash of every source's URI, size, modification time and place in its file: a changed file or a cover file added or removed is a new key.
  • At most 64 MB, least recently used out first (a hit refreshes the file's time); the lock screen's song and the next four are pinned.
  • One render at a time: the lock screen's first, then the newest request (what is on screen now). A cover that leaves the screen before its render starts withdraws it, and a render nobody waits for is dropped.
  • The lock screen: each queue item's artUri is the file:// path of its 600 px file; the first song's is made before the queue is set (waiting at most 2 s), the next four as the queue plays, found through the library by the queue items' ids (so a queue restored after a restart is served too).

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: Schema version 4 (step from3To4, after #147's library tags in 3) adds six nullable columns to tracks (no new table: art is rebuilt by a rescan, so the guard test stays at sources and tracks): art_offset, art_length, art_kind, folder_art_uri, folder_art_size, folder_art_mtime. Scan version 5 (4 is #149's M4A and WAV tags) reads every file again for its picture; every scan notes each folder's cover file on its tracks without reading them.

docs.title: 0011: Ratings, play counts and last played
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-11-25) · Owner: Library engineer · Owner decision 20 (spec, 25 November 2026) settled the three open questions

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The spec (README.md, The library) asked for ratings, play counts, last played and skip counts per track in the app's own database, "keyed so that they survive a rescan and a file move within the library". Decision 0005 planned a track_stats table keyed by a content fingerprint for that.
  • The firmware is the reference (constitution II). It keeps ratings in app/settings/ratings_store.c and plays in app/settings/plays_store.c, both keyed by the file's path and size: ratings_key(path, size), an FNV-1a hash of the path mixed with the size (ratings_store.c:26; plays_store.h, "An entry is keyed like a rating"). A rebuilt library keeps them; a moved file, or a retag that changes the size, starts again at nothing.
  • So the spec and the device disagreed on a move. The firmware has no skip count at all. Decision 0005 excluded the database from phone backups until ratings arrived. All three went to the owner (questions below, answered).

docs.title: Owner decision 20 (25 November 2026)
docs.text:
1. Identity: the device's key, plus a carry-over. Ratings and play counts are keyed by path and size, as on the device. When a rescan sees a file move (its old path gone, one new file with the same audio fingerprint), they are carried to the new key. (Options were: A, the device's key only; B, a content fingerprint as the key; C, the device's key with a carry-over. C was recommended and chosen.)
  2. Skip counts are dropped for now, on the app and the device.
  3. Backups: ratings and play counts get their own small database, included in iCloud and Google backups; the library database stays excluded. (Options were: keep everything excluded; back up the library database; a separate stats database. The last was recommended and chosen.)

docs.title: The firmware rules, ported
docs.text:
All in mobile/lib/domain/library/play_stats.dart, checked against the compiled C by test/domain/library/play_stats_vectors_test.dart with test/fixtures/plays/firmware_vectors.json, which scripts/app/gen-plays-vectors.sh prints from the firmware's own play_tracker.c, ratings_store.c and plays_store.c (scripts/app/plays_vectors.c). CI regenerates the file and fails on a difference.

Rule Firmware App A track start counts as a play once, when half its length has been heard, or 30 s when the length is unknown, or when it ended by itself after 3 s heard ptrk_update, app/runtime/play_tracker.c:12; constants app/include/play_tracker.h:23-25 PlayTracker.update Only time spent playing counts (a seek or scan does not move it); a held-up pass adds at most 1 s; a new track start begins again; times are uint32_t and wrap same same (masked to 32 bits) A pass every 100 ms on the monitor task, whatever screen is up; playing = PLAYER_PLAYING and not held for a Bluetooth headset; ended = PLAYER_ENDED; a new track_id on every start, a skip and a gapless handoff, not on a seek count_plays, app/runtime/player.c:441; app/runtime/runtime.c:328; player.h:59 PlayCounter (domain/library/play_counter.dart): a 100 ms timer while a track is current; playing = PlayerState.isPlaying; ended = PlaybackStatus.ended; a start = a new queue or another index A rating is 0 to 5; 0 clears it; anything above 5 is ignored ratings_set, ratings_store.c:45 PlayStats.rated A counted play adds one (saturating at 65535, uint16_t) and stamps "last played" with the serial; any touch (a play, a note) counts the serial up and stamps the entry apply, plays_store.c:50-91 (saturation :84) PlayStats.touched; the serial is the largest stamp, so it lives in the table "Last played" is a serial, not a time: "the player has no real clock on every board" plays_store.h kept as a serial, so the order matches the device's The wheel sets the stars one per turn whatever the turn's size, clockwise more, 0 to 5; a haptic step only when they change; saved at once p2_scroll, app/ui/ui_nowplaying.c:788-802 starsAfterTurn; NowPlayingScreen page 2 A rating of 4 stars or more notes the track (zero plays) so Top rated can open it ui_nowplaying.c:795 TrackStatsStore.rate

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Its own database: stats.sqlite (lib/data/db/stats_database.dart, StatsDatabase), schema version 1, one table track_stats(path, size, rating, plays, last_played, stamp), primary key (path, size), CHECK rating 0 to 5 and plays 0 to 65535. Migrations follow decision 0008 (snapshots in drift_schemas/stats/, one transaction, a downgrade refused; with one version any upgrade throws and changes nothing). Tests: test/drift/stats/. The guard test allows exactly sources and tracks in the library database and exactly track_stats in the stats database.
  • Where it lives (owner decision 20, backups): neupod_storage backedUpDataPath().
  • iOS: Application Support/stats, created if needed, with isExcludedFromBackup set to false and read back (the call fails if it is still excluded); the flag on a folder covers its contents. The library stays in Application Support/library, flag true (decision 0005).
  • Android: filesDir/stats. The manifest now names explicit rules: res/xml/backup_rules.xml (android:fullBackupContent, Android 11 and earlier) and res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml (android:dataExtractionRules, Android 12 and later, cloud backup and device transfer), each with the one rule <include domain="file" path="stats/"/>. With an include rule nothing else is backed up; the library database and the art cache are in noBackupFilesDir, which Android never backs up anyway.
  • Checked by test/app/backup_rules_test.dart (the Android rules and manifest) and, on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator in CI, by integration_test/backup_paths_test.dart (iOS: the real flags of both folders and of stats.sqlite; Android: the paths).
  • The library database, schema version 5, adds one column, tracks.audio_fingerprint (null until a rescan reads the file again: scan version 6). The never-merged first draft of this PR put track_stats in the library database as version 5; it was restructured before merge, so the chain on main goes 4 to 5 with only the new column.
  • Key: the device's identity. path is the device's form of the track's path, '/' + tracks.rel_path, as a card's root gives it; size is the file's size. The app stores the two themselves, not the firmware's 32-bit hash, so two tracks never share numbers through a hash collision. The hash can be computed from them when R3 exchanges ratings with a device.
  • Nothing ties the table to tracks; it is another database. A rescan, a re-read file, a new scan version, a removed folder or a deleted file never touches a row; a folder added back finds its numbers again.
  • One table for the firmware's two stores. A row with stamp 0 is a rating the plays store would not know; a row with no rating and stamp 0 is deleted.
  • The app keeps every track; the device keeps 128 (24 ratings on the Pico 2 W) and evicts. Memory lets a device do less, never differently (constitution IV), so the app does not port the eviction, the 96-byte path limit (plays_store.c:101) or the copy of title and artist (the app has the library).

docs.title: The carry-over on a move or a retag
docs.text:
• The fingerprint (lib/data/scan/audio_fingerprint.dart): a1: and the hex SHA-256 of the container family (flac, mp3, mp4, wav), the audio payload's length in bytes and the first 64 KiB of the payload. The payload is where the container keeps the audio, and nothing else:
  • FLAC: everything after the metadata block flagged last (an ID3v2 tag in front is skipped). Comments, pictures and padding are metadata blocks.
  • MP3: from the first frame header after any ID3v2 tags (and padding) to the end, less APEv2, Lyrics3v2 and ID3v1 at the end.
  • MP4/M4A: the body of the first top-level mdat box. Taggers rewrite moov/udta and may move mdat, never its body.
  • WAV: the body of the data chunk (LIST and id3 chunks are tags).
  • Why this one. Cheap: only new or changed files, from the handle already open for their tags, in the scan's isolate; unchanged files are never opened. It reads the payload's first 64 KiB plus the container's headers (a few hundred bytes); an MP3 also reads up to 64 KiB to find its first frame header, so up to about 128 KiB in all. Robust: no tag byte is hashed, so a retag, a rename and a move leave it unchanged. The payload length stands in for the owner's "plus the duration": it is exact and needs no parse, while a duration can be an estimate (an MP3 with no Xing header) and comes out the same for different encodings; two recordings that share their first 64 KiB (a silent intro) still differ unless they are also exactly as long to the byte. A re-encode or a re-rip is new audio and starts again, as on the device.
  • A size-changing retag carries over: yes, for FLAC, MP3, MP4/M4A and WAV, since the fingerprint has no tag bytes. Ogg, Opus and raw AAC files are listed by name and never opened by the scanner (the device does not parse them), so they have no fingerprint and no carry-over; their numbers stay under the old key.
  • The rule (LocalLibraryScanner, _Moves): across every folder of one scan, a key that left (a file gone from a complete walk, a folder removed, or a file whose size changed) and a key that arrived (a new file, or the new size) with the same fingerprint, exactly one of each, is a move. At the end of the scan the store carries the numbers (TrackStatsStore.carry), in one transaction. Copies of the same audio on either side are not a move (which one would it be?). A new key that already has numbers keeps them; the old ones stay under the old key. A scan cancelled before the end carries nothing; the numbers stay under the old key, not lost.
  • The key is shared across library folders. It is the path relative to the folder, as on a card, so two folders holding the same relative path at the same size share one row (as the device has one card). A move whose old key is still held by a file in another folder is therefore not carried: the numbers stay with the file still there.
  • Damaged files never hang the scan. Every walk stops at the end of the file and steps strictly forward; a size that runs past the end, a 64-bit MP4 size at or above 2^63, an APEv2 or Lyrics3v2 size that does not move the end back (a Lyrics3v2 size must be six ASCII digits), and more than 1,024 FLAC metadata blocks all give no fingerprint, or stop taking trailing tags off.
  • Tests: test/data/scan/audio_fingerprint_test.dart (each container, retagged and not, other audio, and damaged input: negative and non-digit Lyrics3v2 sizes, huge APEv2 sizes, 64-bit MP4 sizes, boxes and chunks past the end, a FLAC block overrun, 8 MB of zeros after fLaC, WAV chunk stepping) and the "ratings and play counts" group of test/data/scan/local_library_scanner_test.dart (a move in a folder, a move to another library folder, a size-changing retag, copies, no overwrite, an old key still held in another folder).

docs.title: Known gaps (logged in PROGRESS)
docs.text:
• A restart of the same queue entry is not a new start yet. The engine does not report one: Previous after 3 s and (phase 4) repeat one restart the same index, so a second play in a row of the same entry is not counted. On the device they are new starts (begin_track, player.c). Needs a start counter from neupod_audio (audio engineer).
  • Plays are counted by Dart. Where Android keeps playing after the Flutter engine has gone (the media service alone), nothing counts them until the app is back.
  • The device's page 2 puts the stars above the rows, lit stars in the accent colour and the rest in the line grey. The app keeps owner decision 13's Rating row and its existing star skin (filled and outlined stars in the secondary and tertiary inks): a UI styles question for the owner.
  • Most played, Top rated and Unplayed (Music > Playlists on the device) and Settings > Reset ratings and play counts belong to phase 6; the numbers they need are stored now.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• Firmware: app/runtime/play_tracker.c, app/include/play_tracker.h, app/settings/ratings_store.c, app/include/ratings_store.h, app/settings/plays_store.c, app/include/plays_store.h, app/runtime/player.c (count_plays, begin_track, apply_next), app/ui/ui_nowplaying.c (page 2), docs/ui.md (Now Playing, page 2), docs/storage.md (Playlists, play counts and On-The-Go).
  • App: docs/app/README.md (The library; owner decisions 13 and 20), decisions 0005 and 0008.
  • Platforms: Apple's URLResourceValues.isExcludedFromBackup; Android Auto Backup (fullBackupContent, dataExtractionRules, noBackupFilesDir). The behaviour is checked by the tests named above, on the CI simulator and emulator, not taken from the documentation alone.

docs.title: 0012: Android's shared music collection
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-11-26) · Owner: Library engineer · Owner decision 21 (spec, 26 November 2026) settled the duplicate rule, music only and the row's words

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The spec (Getting music onto the phone): on Android the user picks folders, and the app "also offers the device's shared music collection". Owner decision 8: its tracks get embedded art only, because folder art would need a restricted image permission.
  • Decision 0004 planned it: MediaStore audio, READ_MEDIA_AUDIO on Android 13 and later and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (with maxSdkVersion="32") before, asked for only when the user turns the collection on; items opened by their content://media/... URI on every version (Android 10 cannot read the DATA path without legacy storage).
  • The app's minimum is Android 10 (API 29), so MediaStore's RELATIVE_PATH and VOLUME_NAME columns are always there.
  • The firmware is the reference (constitution II): the device reads its tags from the file. MediaStore's own tag columns (TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, ...) come from Android's scanner and differ from the device's (other fallbacks, other text handling, a title made from the file name without its extension), so they are not used.
  • Ratings and play counts are keyed by the device's path and size, '/' + rel_path (decision 0011).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The collection is one more root of the folder access plugin, not a second scanner. neupod_storage gets one call, addSharedCollection(), and a root kind, sharedCollection, with the fixed id mediastore:audio (sharedCollectionRootId). Everything else is the folder path unchanged:

Picked folder (SAF) Shared collection (MediaStore) Turned on pickFolder(): the system picker, a persisted read-only tree grant addSharedCollection(): the read permission if not held (the system's question), then the plugin's own "on" flag (SharedPreferences) Listed by listRoots(), in grant order listRoots(), after the folders, while on; available is false when the permission was taken away in the phone's Settings Walked by startWalk / nextWalkBatch: one DocumentsContract query per directory the same calls: one MediaStore query (Audio.Media, VOLUME_EXTERNAL, IS_MUSIC != 0), served a page at a time; always complete relPath path below the picked folder RELATIVE_PATH + DISPLAY_NAME: the path from the top of the storage volume (Music/Album/01 Song.flac) uri the document URI in the tree content://media/<volume>/audio/media/<id> size, modifiedMs the document's SIZE, DATE_MODIFIED (seconds) x 1000 Opened by openFd: ContentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r"), read with pread the same Turned off removeRoot(id): the grant released removeRoot('mediastore:audio'): the flag cleared (Android lets an app give up a runtime permission only from 13, and only at the next process end; the permission is left to the user) sources.kind local_folder media_store (no schema change: kind is text, decision 0005)
  • Tags are read from the file's bytes by the app's firmware-ported readers, exactly as for a folder's files. The scanner never sees MediaStore's tag columns (the projection does not ask for them).
  • The device-style key works unchanged: a collection track's key is '/' + RELATIVE_PATH + DISPLAY_NAME and its size, so ratings, play counts and the carry-over by audio fingerprint (decision 0011) apply as they do to folders.
  • Incremental rescan by DATE_MODIFIED and size. The scanner's existing check (same size, mtime, URI and scan version: not reopened) needs nothing new. The whole collection is listed on every scan (one query; 20,000 rows is a few hundred milliseconds), which is also what tells the scanner a song has gone. GENERATION_MODIFIED (API 30+) would save no query, since deletions are only seen by listing.
  • Music only: IS_MUSIC != 0, as Android's own music players do, so ringtones, notification and alarm sounds, recordings and podcasts are left out (owner decision 21).
  • Hidden names (a name or a folder starting with .) are skipped, as in a folder walk.
  • Two volumes, one path. A track's path is unique in its source (tracks(source_id, rel_path)). If the phone's storage and an SD card both hold Music/a.flac, the phone's own is listed and the card's left out. Rare; noted.
  • Art: embedded only (owner decision 8). The collection's walk lists only audio, so no cover file is ever found.
  • Turning it off is the folder's Remove: the next scan deletes the source's tracks, and track_stats (another database) keeps their numbers, which come back when it is turned on again.
  • Background scan: the scan is the same LocalLibraryScanner run, so the Android foreground service (decision 0009) covers it with no change.
  • Read only: the plugin adds no write call (the static guard, test/read_only_guard_test.dart, passes unchanged).

docs.title: The same file through a picked folder and the collection
docs.text:
A file in Music/Library/A/01 x.flac reaches the app as A/01 x.flac through a picked Music/Library and as Music/Library/A/01 x.flac through the collection: two keys, two rows, two sets of numbers unless something chooses.

Owner decision 21: the picked folder lists it; the collection leaves it out. The scanner knows where each picked folder is from its tree URI (content://com.android.externalstorage.documents/tree/primary%3AMusic%2FLibrary is volume external_primary, path Music/Library; an SD card's volume id is MediaStore's volume name in lower case) and where each collection item is from its URI's volume and its relative path. An item inside a picked folder on the same volume is skipped by the collection's walk (case ignored, as Android's shared storage ignores it). Folders from other providers have no location and hide nothing. lib/data/scan/shared_collection.dart.

When the owner adds or removes a folder over songs already in the library, the keys change in one scan: one gone, one arrived, the same audio fingerprint. That is decision 0011's move, so the numbers are carried to the new key (tested: test/data/scan/shared_collection_test.dart, "picking a folder over collection songs carries their numbers").

docs.title: The options the owner chose from (B chosen, owner decision 21)
docs.text:
Rule For Against A No rule: both list it Nothing to explain The song is twice in Songs, its album, Shuffle; plays and ratings split over two keys B (built, recommended) The picked folder wins Once in the library; it keeps the folder's cover art (decision 8 denies the collection that); the path is the one the user chose, which is likely nearer a card's layout (Album/...); the user's explicit pick beats the general switch A rule to explain if anyone wonders why the collection's count is lower C The collection wins Once in the library Those songs lose folder art; their paths become storage paths (Music/Library/...); picking a folder inside the collection does nothing visible D One or the other: picking a folder turns the collection off, or the reverse No overlap ever Takes away a reasonable set-up (a folder on the SD card plus the phone's music)

Changing B to A or C is a few lines in LocalLibraryScanner (the insidePickedFolder skip).

docs.title: Owner decision 21 (26 November 2026)
docs.text:
1. Duplicates: B, the picked folder wins (as built).
  2. Music only (IS_MUSIC), although the device lists every audio file on its card.
  3. The row's words stay: Add Music on This Phone while off; listed as Music on This Phone as a folder is while on, with Turn Off (the firmware's question, as Remove: Turn off Music on This Phone?, n songs come off the list., Select = Turn Off · Menu = Keep) where a folder has Remove.

docs.title: Note for R3
docs.text: A collection track's key runs from the top of the phone's storage (/Music/Album/...); a card's paths run from the card's root. Matching the two for a ratings exchange is R3's to design; nothing is needed now.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• test/data/scan/shared_collection_test.dart, over a fake MediaStore (a host folder served as the collection, with content://media URIs, MediaStore ids and DATE_MODIFIED in seconds, and SAF tree URIs for picked folders): tags from the bytes and the device's fallbacks, paths from the top of the storage, the media_store source, no folder art; a rescan that opens only new or changed items and drops what left; the duplicate rule; turning it off with the numbers kept and found again; the carry-over when a folder is picked over collection songs; the tree URI and volume parsing.
  • test/ui/screens/library_screen_test.dart ("the shared music collection"), test/data/platform/storage_folder_access_test.dart.
  • integration_test/media_store_test.dart on the CI emulator (API 29), through the real plugin: the instrumentation rule (MainActivityTest.java, only with neupodSeedMediaStore=true, which tool/android_integration_tests.sh passes for this file) grants the permission and inserts a WAV into MediaStore through ContentResolver; the test turns the collection on, finds it listed and the file in its walk, opens it, scans it with the app's scanner (duration read from the WAV header), turns it off and sees the song go. The permission dialog itself is not driven (it is the system's); with the permission held, turning on asks nothing. On iOS the same file checks that the call is refused as unsupported.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• Android, media store (collections, RELATIVE_PATH, VOLUME_NAME, IS_PENDING, permissions by version): https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/shared/media
  • MediaStore.Audio.AudioColumns.IS_MUSIC, MediaStore.VOLUME_EXTERNAL: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/MediaStore.Audio.AudioColumns
  • Granular media permissions (Android 13): https://developer.android.com/about/versions/13/behavior-changes-13#granular-media-permissions
  • ExternalStorageProvider document ids (primary:Music, <uuid>:Music): AOSP packages/providers/MediaProvider and frameworks/base/packages/ExternalStorageProvider.

docs.title: 0013: The scale test and its targets
docs.text: Status: Accepted (2026-11-26) · Owner: Test engineer · The targets marked "lead call" are proposals for the lead and the owner; the spec's own are marked "spec"

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• The spec (The library): "Sizing target: 20,000 tracks. First scan of 5,000 FLAC files in under five minutes on a mid-range phone; a rescan with no changes in under ten seconds. (Targets are proposals; measure and report.)" Its test table: "A generated 20,000-track library: scan time, memory, scroll smoothness", at the end of the library phase. It sets no target for list reads, the database or memory.
  • The last handoff asked for "real queries" before the scale test: DriftLibraryView reads the whole tracks table and folds it into the firmware's entities in Dart.
  • mobile/tool/gen_test_library already wrote a scale library, but not a real library's shape (200 artists of 10 albums of 10 tracks, FLAC and MP3 only, no compilations).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The scale library (scaleCases, --scale N) is shaped like a real one: about 13 tracks an album and 2.5 albums an artist, so 20,000 tracks are 1,500 album folders by 563 album artists; FLAC, MP3 and M4A (ALAC) in turn, one format an album, with real tags written into the repository's small fixtures, so the real tag readers run; a compilation every 15th album (by "Various Artists" or by the flag alone, its tracks by other artists); two discs every 8th other album (disc tags, (Disc n) folders); "The" artists, some in ", The" folders; accented, Nordic, Cyrillic and Japanese names; every 50th track untagged (owner decision 15, so each makes its folder an album: 1,901 albums in the Albums list). 20,000 tracks are 314 MB. The generator gained an M4A tag writer (m4aWithTags), which also fixed the curated library's "untagged" ALAC file: it was the fixture byte for byte, and the fixture has tags.

The test is mobile/test/scale/library_scale_test.dart (tag scale). It generates the library in a temporary folder, scans it with the app's LocalLibraryScanner (through a dart:io storage root, test/support/host_library.dart) into a database file opened as the app opens it (SQLite in a background isolate), and deletes it all afterwards.

  • Every PR runs it at 2,000 tracks inside flutter test, against tight limits of its own (the last column below): about 5 to 10 times what the slower of the M1 host and the CI runner takes, so a regression of that size fails and CI's own variation does not.
  • The full run is NEUPOD_SCALE_TRACKS=20000 flutter test test/scale from mobile/, or the app workflow's scale_tracks input (gh workflow run app.yml --ref <branch> -f scale_tracks=20000), which uploads the numbers as the scale-report artifact. NEUPOD_SCALE_REPORT=<file> writes them as JSON locally.

docs.title: Targets and limits
docs.text: What Target Source Limit at 20,000 (the full run) Limit at 2,000 (every PR) First scan 5,000 FLAC files in 5 minutes on a mid-range phone (60 ms a file) spec 60 ms × tracks 15 s (CI 2.7 s) Rescan, nothing changed under 10 s at 20,000 spec 10 s 2 s (CI 0.16 s) Rescan, 100 changes (60 retagged, 20 removed, 20 added) under 16 s at 20,000 (the unchanged rescan plus 100 files at the first scan's rate) lead call 16 s 3 s First list after a launch or a scan (the table read and folded) under 1 s at 20,000 lead call 1 s 500 ms (CI 124 ms) Any list once loaded: Artists, Albums, Cover Flow, Songs, an artist's albums, an album's tracks under 100 ms at 20,000 lead call 100 ms 20 ms A Search keystroke (the prefix match over every name) under 50 ms at 20,000 lead call 50 ms 20 ms Database under 2 KB a track (40 MB at 20,000) lead call 2 KB × tracks 2 KB × tracks Memory the library view's lists under 50 MB at 20,000 lead call reported, not enforced (RSS is noisy across runners) reported Scroll smoothness no dropped frames scrolling Songs at 20,000 spec (test table) the device check: the host cannot measure frames

docs.title: Numbers (2026-11-26)
docs.text:
M1 is the build Mac (Apple M1, 8 GB, macOS 27.2.1, Flutter 3.50.1); CI is the app workflow's check job on GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 runner (run 45841467685, scale_tracks=20000). Both are flutter test, debug (JIT): the code's cost on a desktop CPU and SSD, which says little about a phone's storage. M1 ranges are over three runs; CI is one run.

M1, 2,000 CI, 2,000 M1, 20,000 CI, 20,000 Library generated 31 MB 31 MB 314 MB, 1,500 album folders 314 MB in 1.0 s First scan 1.9 s 2.7 s 17.6 to 18.5 s (0.9 ms a file) 9.9 s (0.5 ms a file) Rescan, nothing changed 0.1 s 0.11 s 0.8 to 1.1 s 0.86 s Rescan, 100 changes 0.16 s 0.14 s 0.8 to 0.9 s 0.92 s Database (after a checkpoint) 1.7 MB 1.5 MB 17.2 MB (860 bytes a track) 15.4 MB Table read alone (all rows, from the database isolate) 12 ms 188 to 193 ms 227 ms First list after a scan (read and fold) 54 ms 70 ms 424 to 428 ms 544 ms Artists / Albums / Cover Flow, loaded 0.05 / 0.04 / 0.02 ms 0.07 / 0.15 / 0.16 ms 0.07 / 0.18 / 0.05 ms Songs, loaded 0.09 ms 0.33 ms 1.2 to 5.2 ms 1.8 ms An artist's albums / an album's tracks 0.18 / 1.1 ms 0.17 / 0.9 ms 0.16 / 0.9 ms Search: building its index / one keystroke 16 / 0.6 ms 0.7 ms a key 29 to 37 / 3.3 ms 43 / 3.4 ms Lists counted 59 artists, 191 albums, 10 compilations the same 563 artists, 1,901 albums, 100 compilations the same Process memory (max RSS) 259 MB 387 to 408 MB (231 MB at the start; the lists add 5 MB) 438 MB (212 MB at the start; the lists add 4 MB)

Every target is met on both. The 20,000-track step took 17 s of CI time and the whole check job 2.5 minutes, well inside its 15-minute timeout (a requested scale run gets 30). The phone numbers come from the device check (PROGRESS, phase 3).

docs.title: "Real queries": not now (lead call)
docs.text:
DriftLibraryView does not query each list. It reads the tracks table once (one SELECT joined to its source) and folds it into the firmware's artists, albums and genres in Dart (lib_build.c's index_file, stage_entity, ent_cmp, the walk order), then keeps that until the tracks or sources change. Measured at 20,000:

  • every list once loaded takes 0.02 to 5 ms, 20 to 5,000 times under the 100 ms bar, and no index would help it (no list is a query);
  • the one slow step is the first list after a launch or a scan: 0.43 s, of which 0.19 s is the table read and the rest the fold. It happens once, and in practice before the user opens a list: Home counts the songs at launch and again when a scan ends, which loads the view.

Per-list SQL would need the firmware's entity keys stored at scan time (the collation keys of the album artist and the album, folded as ent_cmp folds them, and the walk order), a schema version 6 with a scan version bump, so every owner's library is read again once, and SQL that reproduces the firmware's fold exactly. That is the bigger, riskier change, for a cost the user should not see. So the fold stays, and the stored-keys design is the plan if the device check shows the first list over 1 s on the iPhone or the Pixel. No schema change was made, so decision 0008's migration rules and the guard tests are untouched.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Measure on a device only. It is the real number, but cannot run on every PR; the host run catches regressions and the device check gives the phone's number.
  • A fixed set of committed scale files. 314 MB in a public repository, and no way to change the shape; generated at test time instead, never committed.
  • Every limit scaled with the size. A list read must stay quick at any size, so only the first scan's limit grows with the track count.

docs.title: UI design review, 12 November 2026
docs.text:
An owner-commissioned design review of the firmware UI (164 simulator screenshots reviewed). This folder holds the review as delivered:

  • REPORT.md: findings, the design system (colour tokens, type scale, layout metrics, icons, motion), a proposal per screen and the backlog (DS-*, NP-*, LB-*, BT-*, ST-*, IN-*, HL-*, FL-*, SP-*).
  • mockups/: every proposed screen at 320x240 and 480x360 (<area>-<screen>-<WxH>.png).
  • render.py: regenerates the mock-ups; every length comes from the metric table, so it doubles as a layout reference.

The backlog is tracked in Backlog; the implemented design system is described in UI mock-ups.

The mock-ups are drawn with Inter as a stand-in. Implementations use Montserrat Medium (the fonts the firmware already builds), which runs about 4 % wider; the review left that margin.

docs.title: Owner decisions (12 November 2026)
docs.text:
Where the review conflicts with earlier decisions, these win, in every phase:

  1. Now Playing. Select opens page 2; hold Select enters seek (the wheel seeks, Select commits, Menu cancels). This supersedes the earlier "Select toggles volume / seek". Built in phase 2.
  2. Bluetooth link lost. ADR-0019 stands: playback pauses and stays on Bluetooth; the firmware never switches the output by itself. The review's "Couldn't reconnect, playing on wired" toast becomes "Couldn't reconnect — paused".
  3. Theme. Light by default. Settings > Display > Theme is Light / Dark / Auto; Auto means dark once the backlight dims.
  4. Order. Phase 1 foundation (DS-*, HL-1), phase 2 Now Playing and library rows / fast scroll, phase 3 Bluetooth screens, phase 4 the rest.
  5. Platform. The Pico 2 W is frozen (ADR-0001 amendment). Design for the RP2350B with PSRAM and the Y2; ignore the review's "Pico 2 W" fallbacks, but keep that build compiling.
  6. Licences. Standing rule: every third-party asset added (Lucide icons, ISC; new font sizes, OFL) goes into LICENSE.md and the on-device Licences screen (app/ui/ui_licence_data.c); the licences ctest checks they agree.
  7. Dark accent. The dark theme's accent is #2868D8 (RGB565-safe, about 5:1 with white text); the review's #3078E8 gave 4.2:1. The contrast test asserts at least 4.5 in both themes.
  8. Toast height. The toast strip covers exactly one list row (30 px at 320x240, 45 px at 480x360), not 22 / 33 px.
  9. Auto theme stays as built. Auto is dark while the backlight is dimmed or off and light otherwise. With Auto-dim turned off the backlight never dims, so Auto behaves like Light (until the screen goes off).
  10. Text that does not fit scrolls (supersedes the review's "always an ellipsis"). One-line text wider than its box runs as a ticker: it waits 1 s, then scrolls round at about 35 px/s (52 px/s on 480x360) with a small gap between repeats, and only while it overflows. Where it applies: the Home track title and artist, the focused list row's main text (unfocused rows keep the ellipsis, like classic wheel players), the status-bar title; and, as a standing rule, Now Playing title / artist / album in phase 2 and any later one-line text. It stops and rewinds when focus leaves the row, and stands still while the screen is off. Tours snapshot every ticker at its start position.

docs.title: neuPod UI/UX review and proposal
docs.text:
Reviewed: 164 simulator screenshots (320x240/, 480x360/, two contact sheets), firmware v0.1.0-dev. Target: LVGL 9, RGB565, partial redraws, Montserrat Medium 14/20/48 (320×240) and 20/28/48 (480×360), click wheel + Select + 4 buttons + Hold.

Mock-ups are in mockups/, named <area>-<screen>-<WxH>.png, rendered at native resolution for both profiles. They use Inter Medium/SemiBold as a stand-in for Montserrat Medium (same x-height class; expect Montserrat to run ~4% wider — all widths below leave that margin). Fixture names (Aurora Lane, Harbour Lights, Beacon) are kept so the engineer can compare like for like.

docs.title: 1. Summary — highest-impact changes, ranked
docs.text:
1. Now Playing hierarchy — title/artist/album stack, format and output as pills, progress with remaining time, volume as a quiet bottom strip; one layout for wired and Bluetooth (np-nowplaying, np-nowplaying-bt). Today the title is a file name, "Playing – 1 of 3" competes with the format, and the volume bar is as heavy as the progress bar.
  2. Two-line list rows with secondary text for Songs and search results (lib-songs) — today artist is right-aligned on the same line and collides with long titles (lib-songs.png, text-nowplaying.png).
  3. Fast-scroll letter overlay + index rail (lib-songs-fastscroll) — the wheel accelerates but gives no position feedback; the overlay already exists in Files (files-many.png, the "F" tile) and should be generalised and moved off the content.
  4. Consistent status bar: left context slot (clock / track position / count / path), centre title, right Bluetooth + battery with a percentage when < 20 % (home-home). Today the left slot is always empty and the battery reads "--".
  5. Selection bar as the one accent: 4 px radius, 3 px inset from the edges, only the focused row coloured; chevrons and secondary text drop to grey — the bar then "moves" between rows with an 80 ms slide instead of repainting two rows.
  6. State feedback without modal screens: top toast strip for link-lost / can't-play / library busy (bt-dropped), bottom HUD strip for volume from any screen (np-volume-hud), and busy dots replaced by a determinate progress bar where a count is known (lib-building).
  7. Hold / Power feedback (hold-locked, hold-power-progress) — a pill at the bottom and a 3 px progress line under the status bar; no full-screen dim.
  8. Text entry on the wheel (in-text) — a horizontal letter ring with the current glyph at 48 px, mode chips (abc / ABC / 123 / #!? / space / ⌫) on Left/Right, field at the top. Today letters are evenly spaced small glyphs and there is no visible mode switch (in-text.png, wifi-kb.png).
  9. Dark theme via tokens (home-home-dark, np-nowplaying-dark) — one token table, Auto switches to dark when the backlight dims; the product board's LCD benefits less than an OLED would, but night use and battery on a future panel both improve.
  10. Missing screens: Cover-Flow-style album browser without 3D (lib-coverflow), Now Playing page 2 (np-page2), Playlists (lib-playlists), Licences (settings-licences), real empty states (lib-empty).

docs.title: 2.1 Colour tokens (RGB565-safe: R and B multiples of 8, G multiples of 4)
docs.text:
Token Light Dark Use bg #F8F8F8 #101010 screen background surface #FFFFFF #181818 cards, input fields, right pane bar #E8E8E8 #202020 status bar fill line #E0E0E0 #303030 hairlines, progress track, scrollbar track ink #181818 #F0F0F0 primary text, battery fill ink2 #606060 #A0A0A0 secondary text, chevrons, volume fill ink3 #A0A0A0 #686868 tertiary text, disabled rows, hints accent #1858C8 #2868D8 selection bar, progress fill, focused value on_accent #FFFFFF #FFFFFF text on the selection bar accent_soft #D8E4F8 #203050 pills, info toast amber #D08018 #E89828 seek mode, warnings amber_soft #F8E8C8 #483818 warning toast background green #209858 #30B870 charging, streaming OK, signal full red #D03028 #E84840 battery < 15 %, errors

Contrast: ink2 on surface 5.9:1 light / 7.1:1 dark; ink3 on surface 2.6:1 — use ink3 only for text ≥ 14 px that is not the sole carrier of meaning (hints, disabled rows). on_accent on accent 7.3:1.

Theme switch: a theme_t struct of these 14 colours; every style reads from it; lv_obj_report_style_change() after swap. Auto = light while the backlight is at full, dark once it dims (and remembers the user's last manual choice).

docs.title: 2.2 Type scale (existing fonts only)
docs.text:
Role 320×240 480×360 Weight Where Title 20 28 Medium Now Playing title, album header, empty-state heading Body 14 20 Medium list rows, status-bar title, settings values Small 12 (new) 16 (new) Medium secondary list line, times, pills, hints, status-bar left slot Big 48 48 Medium seek time, letter overlay, clock, text-entry current glyph

The only addition is Small (12 / 16 px). It is the single biggest readability gain in the proposal (secondary lines, times). Cost: one Montserrat Medium size per profile, ASCII + Latin-1 + punctuation ≈ 9–12 KB each. If flash is tight, ship 12 px only and let 480×360 use 14 px Body for secondary text with ink2 (works, looser).

Truncation: always LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT with a single ellipsis; never clip glyphs (text-nowplaying.png currently clips "Have You Fed t…" at the title size but wraps nothing). Title in Now Playing may wrap to two lines on 480×360 only.

docs.title: 2.3 Layout metrics
docs.text:
Metric 320×240 480×360 Status bar height 24 36 Single-line row 30 45 Two-line row 40 60 Horizontal padding 10 15 Selection bar inset / radius 3 / 4 4 / 6 Split-pane divider (Home, Settings) 56 % / 44 % same Art: Now Playing 112 168 Art: Home panel panel width − 24 same Art: album header, NP page 2 64 96 Art: Cover Flow centre / neighbours / outer 96 / 64 / 48 144 / 96 / 72 Progress bar height (normal / seek) 4 / 6 6 / 9 Toast strip height 22 33 HUD strip height 26 39 Pill height 18 27 Scrollbar width / margin 2 / 1 3 / 2

Visible rows: 320×240 gives 7 single-line rows or 5 two-line rows; 480×360 gives the same counts (everything scales ×1.5). Keep row counts identical across profiles so wheel acceleration feels the same.

docs.title: 2.4 Album-art sizes to decode
docs.text: Decode once per album to a 160×160 RGB565 thumbnail (51 KB) on the PSRAM board and keep an LRU of ~24 (1.2 MB). Draw it scaled down for every slot above; nothing is scaled up, which is what makes today's 64 px → 2.6× art look soft (art-cover.png). On the Pico 2 W target keep 96×96 (18 KB) and an LRU of 6; Now Playing then shows art at 1:1 on 320×240 and 1.17× on 480×360 — acceptable.

docs.title: 2.5 Icon set
docs.text:
Use Lucide (ISC licence, https://lucide.dev) rendered to 1-bit-alpha bitmaps at 16 and 24 px (320) / 24 and 36 px (480). Lucide is stroke-based, consistent at small sizes, and its licence permits embedding without attribution in the UI (keep the licence text in the Licences screen). Required glyphs, 14 in total:

chevron-right, play, pause, skip-back, skip-forward, shuffle, repeat, repeat-1, volume-2, bluetooth, wifi, lock, folder, file. Battery, signal bars and the three busy dots are drawn primitives (rectangles), not glyphs.

Drop FontAwesome where these cover it; keep it only for glyphs you already ship and still need.

docs.title: 2.6 Motion (all small-area, no full-screen redraw)
docs.text:
Motion Duration Easing What moves Selection bar to adjacent row 80 ms ease-out only the bar (lv_anim on y); text repaints two rows Selection bar jump > 3 rows / fast spin 0 ms — no anim; letter overlay shows instead Push screen (deeper) 120 ms ease-out-cubic list area slides in 24 px from the right, fades from 0; status bar title swaps instantly Pop screen (Menu) 100 ms ease-out-cubic list slides 24 px to the right and fades out Toast in / out 150 / 200 ms ease-out / ease-in one-row (30 / 45 px) strip slides down from under the status bar Volume HUD 120 ms in, hold 1200 ms, 200 ms out ease-out 26 px bottom strip; bar fill animates 60 ms Seek mode enter / leave 0 ms — colour swap only; haptic tick Progress bar 1 Hz step — invalidate only the bar rectangle Letter overlay appears instantly, fades 250 ms after the wheel stops ease-in 44 px tile + rail Cover Flow step 90 ms ease-out five tiles re-blit at new x/size; no rotation Power-hold progress linear over 2 s — 3 px line under the status bar grows left to right

Cap LVGL at 30 fps on the MCU (LV_DEF_REFR_PERIOD 33); 60 fps on the Y2 if the kernel gives a vsync'd fb.

docs.title: 3. Per-screen review and proposal
docs.text: Button conventions used throughout: Wheel scroll/adjust · Select open/choose · Menu back · Play/Pause global · ◁ ▷ prev/next (hold = seek) · Power hold 2 s lock, 10 s off.

docs.title: 3.1 Home
docs.text:
Current (home.png, home-clock.png, art-home.png): split list + right panel; the panel shows a generic disc glyph, "Nothing playing", "--:--" and a debug line "image 2.0 MB". When playing it shows art, file name and "⏸ Paused" but no progress. Status bar left slot is empty; battery reads "--".

Proposed (home-home, home-idle, home-home-dark):

  • Left 56 %: the seven items, chevrons on items that open a list, none on "Shuffle Songs". "Now Playing" greys out when nothing is queued instead of opening an empty screen.
  • Right panel, playing: art at panel width, title (Body, semibold) and artist (Small) centred, a 3 px progress bar, elapsed/remaining in Small. Paused shows the pause glyph in front of the elapsed time.
  • Right panel, idle: 48 px clock, date, one Small line "1,204 songs · 72 %". Remove "image 2.0 MB" from release builds (keep it behind a debug flag).
  • Status bar: clock in the left slot on Home only.

States: idle / playing / paused / library-not-built (panel shows "Update Library" prompt, Select on Music still works). Transitions: push on Select; the panel does not animate. Wheel: scroll items; Select opens; Play/Pause toggles playback without leaving Home.

docs.title: 3.2 Now Playing
docs.text:
Current (np-bt-badge.png, seek-scrub.png, np-bt-volume.png, art-cover.png, text-nowplaying.png): file name as title; format badge in blue sits where the artist should; "Playing – 1 of 3" is body-weight; the volume slider is as prominent as progress; seek mode recolours progress amber and adds a third "Seek 0:08" line with yet another bar; on BT the label changes to "Headset 47 %". Long titles clip (text-nowplaying.png).

Proposed (np-nowplaying, np-nowplaying-bt, np-seek, np-page2, np-volume-hud):

  • Status bar: left slot "3 of 12", centre "Now Playing", Bluetooth glyph in blue when streaming.
  • Art 112 / 168 px at the left; to its right the stack Title (Title size) → Artist (Body, ink2) → Album · Year (Small, ink3). Fall back to the file name only when there is no title tag, and then show the folder name as the "artist".
  • Pill row under the stack: format pill (accent_soft, e.g. "FLAC 16/44.1" or "AAC 44.1" when the BT codec is what's leaving the box) and output pill (outline: "Wired" or the headset's name). The output pill is where "Headset" belonged.
  • Progress: 4 px, elapsed left, remaining right, a quiet ink3 "repeat 1 / shuffle" word in the centre only when either is on.
  • Volume: bottom strip, label "Volume −18 dB" or "Headset 62 %" in Small, bar in ink2, 45 % of the width. On a volume change from any other screen the same strip appears as a HUD for 1.2 s (np-volume-hud).
  • Seek mode: the pill row is replaced by the seek time in Big amber; the progress bar grows to 6 px with a knob; hint line "Scroll: seek · Select: go · Menu: cancel". Leaving seek restores the pills. No third bar.
  • Page 2 (Select on Now Playing when not seeking): small art + title, star rating under it (wheel adjusts when focused), then Shuffle / Repeat / Gapless / Add to playlist / Go to album / Go to artist.

States: playing / paused (pause glyph before elapsed time, art unchanged) / seeking / BT link lost (toast, progress bar goes ink3, "Paused" under the title — see bt-dropped) / no art (placeholder tile with a ring, not a music-note glyph) / unsupported codec (toast "Can't play: AAC — skipped", auto-skip after 1.5 s). Transitions: push from a list = 120 ms slide; Menu returns to the list that queued the track. Wheel: volume; Select → page 2; hold Select → seek mode (wheel seeks, Select commits, Menu cancels); ◁ ▷ tracks, hold to scan at 4× with the seek bar shown.

docs.title: 3.3 Library (Artists, Albums, Songs, Genres, Compilations, Playlists, Album, Update Library)
docs.text:
Current (lib-songs.png, lib-album.png, lib-album-greyed.png, lib-artists.png, lib-building.png, lib-needs-writable.png, lib-cant-play.png, lib-update-done.png, music-empty.png): single-line rows with artist right-aligned (collides with long titles); album screen is a bare track list with no header; greyed unplayable rows give no reason until you press Select, then a yellow bar appears bottom-left; busy and error states are rendered as fake list rows ("Building library…" with dots as the first row, "Select to cancel" as the third); "No artists" is a selected blue row.

Proposed:

  • Songs / search results (lib-songs): two-line rows, title in Body and "Artist · Album" in Small ink2; 2 px scrollbar at the right edge; status-bar left slot shows the count.
  • Fast scroll (lib-songs-fastscroll): when wheel velocity passes the acceleration threshold, show a 44 px dark tile with the first letter of the focused row at the top-right and a 26-letter rail along the right edge with the current letter in ink at Small size, the rest at 8 px ink3 (every second letter on 320×240). The tile never covers the selection bar. Fade out 250 ms after the wheel stops. Sort keys ignore "The ", "A " and diacritics so the rail is useful.
  • Album (lib-album): header with 64 px art, album title (Title), "Artist · Year" (Body ink2), "3 songs · 9:41 · FLAC" (Small ink3); hairline; tracks as "n Title" with duration right. Unplayable tracks greyed with the codec in brackets ("Carrier Wave (AAC)") so the reason is visible before pressing.
  • Artists / Albums / Genres / Compilations: single-line rows with chevrons; show counts on the right ("4 albums") only on 480×360 where there is room.
  • Albums as Cover Flow (lib-coverflow): optional view toggled with ▷ on the Albums list. Five flat tiles: centre 96 px, neighbours 64 px, outer 48 px, no rotation or reflection; title and "Artist · Year · n songs" under the centre; status-bar left slot "7 of 31". Wheel moves one album per step; Play plays the album; Select opens it.
  • Playlists (lib-playlists): smart lists first (On-The-Go, Recently added, Most played, Unplayed) then .m3u files from the card, counts on the right.
  • Update Library / busy (lib-building): centred heading, determinate bar (songs found / total files from a first directory count), current folder in Small, hints "Menu: run in background · Select: cancel". While running in the background the status bar shows three busy dots in the left slot of every screen.
  • Empty and error states (lib-empty): heading in Title, one or two Small lines that say what to do, a single accent button. "Library needs a writable card" becomes a toast on the library root plus this empty state, never a selected list row.
  • Can't play: toast at the top in amber_soft with the codec and "skipped"; the track is skipped automatically after 1.5 s in a queue, or the row stays focused in a list.

Transitions: push/pop slides; Cover Flow step 90 ms. Wheel: as lists; in Cover Flow one album per detent with acceleration to 3 per detent.

docs.title: 3.4 Bluetooth
docs.text:
Current (bt-found.png, bt-pairing.png, bt-dropped.png, bt-forget-asks.png, settings-bt-streaming.png, bt-key-next.png): the settings page mixes status rows (Status, Address) with actions (Scan, Connect, Forget) in one list; the scan list shows a "Cancel pairing" row at the top and three-colour signal bars; "Headset disconnected" is a yellow band with "Reconnecting…" dots inline; "Forget" turns into "Select again" as a confirmation, which is easy to trigger by accident; the right pane in Settings dumps "SBC bitpool 53 · 328 kbit/s · 0 underruns" (fine for a dev build, not for users).

Proposed (bt-devices, bt-dropped):

  • One Devices screen: known devices first with their state on the right ("Connected" in on_accent on the selection bar, "Saved" in ink2), then found devices with signal bars (three bars, monochrome ink/line, no traffic-light colours), phones greyed and labelled "(phone)" because they cannot be sinks, then "Scan again". Scanning progress as four dots at the bottom in ink3.
  • Select on a saved device: Connect / Forget / Rename in a small list pushed from the right; Forget asks "Forget AirPods Pro?" with Select = yes, Menu = no — never a self-mutating row.
  • Pairing: the row's right text becomes "Pairing…" with three dots; Menu cancels (no "Cancel pairing" row).
  • Link lost: bt-dropped — toast "AirPods Pro disconnected · reconnecting…", playback paused, progress bar goes ink3, status-bar glyph grey. On success the toast becomes "AirPods Pro connected" in accent_soft for 1.2 s; on give-up, "Couldn't reconnect — playing on wired" or "— paused" if nothing is plugged in.
  • Codec detail stays in About › Diagnostics, not in the Settings right pane.
  • Status, Address and Audio output move to a short Bluetooth settings page: Bluetooth On/Off, Audio output Auto/Wired/Bluetooth, Devices ›, Absolute volume On/Off.

States: off / idle / scanning / pairing / connected / streaming / reconnecting / failed. Wheel: list; Select on a device = connect (found) or options (saved).

docs.title: 3.5 Settings
docs.text:
Current (settings.png, settings-bt.png, haptics, display): two-pane with values on the left rows and a centred prose summary on the right ("Resume playing / At power-up / On / Plays on power-up if it was playing") that reads as a paragraph; About shows "6 of 8 checks ok" and "nogit".

Proposed (settings-display):

  • Left list: Display, Click, Haptics, Gapless, Shuffle, Repeat, Resume, Bluetooth, About — values on the row where the value is a word, chevrons where it opens a page. Rows that toggle (Gapless, Resume) toggle on Select without leaving the list; a 60 ms value flip, haptic tick.
  • Right pane: a key/value summary left-aligned (Small), heading in Body semibold, one line of help in ink3. No centred prose.
  • Display page: Theme Light/Dark/Auto, Brightness, Dim after, Off after.
  • About: version, build, storage used/free, battery health, then Diagnostics › (checks, codec detail, underruns) and Licences › (settings-licences).

docs.title: 3.6 Files (Extras › Files)
docs.text:
Current (files.png, files-many.png, files-many-end.png, text-folder.png): fine functionally; the "… more (first 256 shown)" row is a blue selected row; the "F" letter tile sits over the list centre.

Proposed (files-browser): path in the status-bar left slot, folder/file glyphs from the icon set, size right-aligned in ink2, scrollbar. Folders with more than 256 entries show "256+" on the folder row and page in the list with "Load more" as the last row (not selected by default). Letter overlay as in the library (top-right tile).

docs.title: 3.7 Input widgets (text, password, number, slider, choice, date/time, search)
docs.text:
Current (in-text.png, wifi-kb.png, in-slider.png, in-choice.png, in-datetime.png): letters in an even row of five with the current one blue; hints as a sentence; no visible way to switch case/digits/symbols; slider is a bare bar; date/time fields underline the active field.

Proposed (in-text): field at the top in a surface box with a caret; a horizontal ring of nine glyphs with the current one in Big accent and widths proportional to glyph size; mode chips below (abc / ABC / 123 / #!? / space / ⌫) switched with ◁ ▷; hint line at the bottom. Password shows the typed glyph for 800 ms then a dot. Number/slider: value in Big centred, bar below, min/max in Small at the ends. Choice: plain list. Date/time: keep the field underline but make the active field accent and add the field name under it in Small.

Wheel: letters (acceleration jumps 3); Select types; Menu deletes (hold = clear); Play = done; ◁ ▷ = mode (text) or field (date/time).

docs.title: 3.8 Hold, lock and power
docs.text:
Current: nothing visible in the tours beyond the brief's description.

Proposed (hold-locked, hold-power-progress): while locked, any key press wakes the screen for 3 s and shows a dark pill at the bottom "Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock"; the content behind is unchanged (no dim, so no full-screen blend). While Power is held, a 3 px accent line grows under the status bar over 2 s with a pill "Keep holding to lock · 10 s = off"; past 2 s the pill reads "Locked", the line resets and refills to 10 s in red with "Release to cancel · shutting down in 6"; haptic tick at 2 s and each second after 7 s.

On the product board the physical Hold switch drives the same pill without the progress line.

docs.title: 3.9 Splash and About
docs.text:
Current (splash.png): wordmark, a thin progress line, a row of eight boxed status glyphs with red crosses, a red "[1/2] battery: gauge: no response" line and the version.

Proposed: keep the wordmark and the progress line; move the self-test row to a debug splash (shown only when a check fails or when Menu is held at boot) and show it as a short list ("Battery gauge — no response") rather than crossed-out icons. Release splash: wordmark, progress line, version in ink3, 600 ms minimum.

Owner amendment, 2026-11-13: after testing on the Y2 the owner asked for the icon row back ("the device check screen has lost the icons and replaced with text - I want the icons back, that loading screen was good"). The release splash is now wordmark, progress line, icon row (Lucide icons, pulse / solid / red cross), version; the text list stays on the debug splash only.

docs.title: 3.10 Status bar (global)
docs.text: Left slot by screen: Home = clock · Now Playing = "n of m" · lists = count · Files = path · Album = album/artist name · Cover Flow = "n of m". Centre: screen title. Right: Bluetooth glyph (ink3 saved, ink connected, accent streaming), battery outline with fill (green while charging, red below 15 %) and the percentage as text only below 20 % or while charging. Three busy dots replace the left slot when the library is building in the background.

docs.title: 4. Mock-ups
docs.text:
All in mockups/, light theme unless named -dark, both 320x240 and 480x360:

File Section home-home, home-idle, home-home-dark 3.1 np-nowplaying, np-nowplaying-bt, np-nowplaying-dark, np-seek, np-page2, np-volume-hud 3.2 lib-songs, lib-songs-fastscroll, lib-album, lib-coverflow, lib-playlists, lib-building, lib-empty 3.3 bt-devices, bt-dropped 3.4 settings-display, settings-licences 3.5 files-browser 3.6 in-text 3.7 hold-locked, hold-power-progress 3.8

render.py regenerates them; every length comes from the metric table in §2.3, so it doubles as a layout reference.

docs.title: 5. Implementation notes (cost and cheaper alternatives)
docs.text:
Item Cost Cheaper alternative New Small font size (12 / 16 px) ~10 KB flash per profile Ship 12 px only; 480×360 uses 14 px Body in ink2 for secondary text Lucide icons, 14 glyphs × 2 sizes × 2 profiles, 1-bit alpha ~6 KB Render at 16 px only and let LVGL scale ×1.5 on 480×360 (slightly soft) 160×160 art thumbnails, LRU 24 1.2 MB PSRAM 96×96, LRU 6 (18 KB each) on the Pico 2 W; Now Playing at 1:1 Selection-bar slide (80 ms) invalidates two rows per frame Disable below 30 fps; the bar simply jumps Push/pop slide + fade list area redrawn ~4 frames Slide only (no alpha); or title-swap only on the Pico 2 W Toast / HUD strips one 22–26 px strip none needed — already minimal Letter overlay + rail 44 px tile + 26 small labels, drawn ~once per 100 ms Rail every second letter on 320×240 (as mocked) Cover Flow, five flat tiles five lv_image re-blits per step; no rotation Three tiles on the Pico 2 W Dark theme zero runtime cost; one token struct — Power-hold progress line 3 px × width invalidate at 10 Hz — Determinate library progress needs a first pass to count files (fast: directory entries only) Indeterminate bar that sweeps, still better than row-dots

Avoid: full-screen dim behind the lock pill (alpha blend of the whole frame), blur, gradients on backgrounds, animating the progress bar more often than 1 Hz, and per-frame redraw of the right pane on Home.
