docs.title: App device view, 21 November 2026
docs.text:
The layout framework for the phone app: how the neuPod's 4:3 screen and click wheel sit on a phone, and how the wheel behaves, in numbers. It answers the design request and follows the owner's decision that the app is the device (app specification, owner decisions 9 to 11).

Owner decision, 22 November 2026: Search is typed with the wheel, as text is on the device, not with the phone's keyboard. This overrides the design request and the app specification, which both say Search opens the keyboard.

This folder holds:

  • this README: decisions, rules and exact values;
  • mockups/: 43 drawings as PNG and as the standalone HTML they were rendered from;
  • render.py: the generator. Every position in the mock-ups is computed from the ratios below, so it doubles as a reference implementation of the layout.

The screens inside the device are the UI styles design, unchanged. Nothing here redesigns a screen; it only places them. The mock-ups are design intent drawn in HTML, not app output. A blue circle marks a finger and is not part of the UI. Album art squares are placeholders.

Drawn fresh. The body, the wheel and the glyphs are this project's own geometry and rendering. No Apple logo, no "iPod", nothing traced from Apple's products. The proportions below are deliberately our own (a wider screen and a thinner frame than the donor shell), chosen for legibility on a phone. Type is Montserrat (SIL OFL); the previous and next glyphs are Lucide's skip-back and skip-forward shapes (ISC); the play/pause glyph and the wordmark are drawn for this design.

docs.title: Recommendations at a glance
docs.text:
Question Recommendation Alternative drawn How the device fits the phone A: the body fills the phone, edge to edge B: the body at fixed proportions on a dark surround Body finish Follows the mode: silver in Light, black in Dark, with a setting to pin one Either finish with either style Touching the screen Wheel plus taps and drags on the screen Wheel only The phone's status bar Shown, above the device Hidden Large text Fewer, larger rows: 7, 6 or 5

The owner chooses between the candidates at the app's design gate, on real screens.

docs.title: 1. Device geometry
docs.text:
Everything is a ratio of W, the phone's width in points. The app lays the device out from these at any size.

Part Value Screen 0.88 W wide, 0.66 W high (4:3), centred horizontally Screen frame (black glass) 0.012 W on every side of the screen; outer corner radius 0.02 W; screen corner radius 0.008 W Side margin, body edge to screen 0.06 W (frame included) Wheel diameter D 0.64 W, centred horizontally Centre button 0.36 D across; a groove 0.04 R wide round it (R = D / 2) Button glyphs on a circle of radius 0.70 R: MENU at the top, next at the right, play/pause at the bottom, previous at the left Wordmark neuPod, 0.036 W high, centred between the frame and the wheel; omitted when that gap is under 44 pt

Scale. The screens are designed at 600x450. The app lays them out at 600x450 and scales the whole screen uniformly by s = 0.88 W / 600. It does not pick a different layout per phone.

Phone Screen (pt) s Small / Body / Title (pt) Row, one / two lines (pt) Wheel D (pt) Centre (pt) 375x667 330 x 247.5 0.550 12.1 / 14.3 / 20.9 30.8 / 41.2 240 86 393x852 345.8 x 259.4 0.576 12.7 / 15.0 / 21.9 32.3 / 43.2 251.5 90.5 440x956 387.2 x 290.4 0.645 14.2 / 16.8 / 24.5 36.1 / 48.4 281.6 101

Minimum. The screen is never narrower than 320 pt (s = 0.533, where Small is 11.7 pt). On a phone narrower than 364 pt the screen stays 320 pt and the side margin shrinks instead, down to 12 pt, so the narrowest supported phone is 344 pt wide. Portrait only. Tablets and landscape are out of scope for R1.

docs.title: 2. Fitting the phone
docs.text:
Two candidates, drawn at all three sizes in Classic and at 393x852 in Modern.

A: fills the phone (recommended) B: fixed proportions 375x667 393x852 440x956 Modern

A: the body fills the phone. The body finish is the app's background, under the status bar, the notch or Dynamic Island, the home indicator and the Android gesture bar. There is no outline and no surround.

  • Frame top = top safe-area inset + max(8 pt, 0.03 W).
  • Floor = phone height less max(bottom safe-area inset, 0.03 W).
  • Wheel centre = midway between the frame's bottom edge and the floor. A taller phone therefore gets more body above and below the wheel; the screen and wheel do not grow.
  • If the space between the frame and the floor is less than D + 24 pt, shrink D until it fits, to no less than 0.56 W.

B: fixed proportions. The body is W wide and 1.675 W high with corner radius 0.08 W, sitting on a surround.

  • Body bottom = the bottom safe-area inset (the phone's bottom edge where there is none). The surplus height shows as surround above the body, which keeps the wheel within reach of the thumb.
  • Frame top = body top + 0.075 W. The wheel is centred between the frame and the body's bottom edge less 0.03 W.
  • The surround is #0b0c0e in every style and mode. The silver body gets a drop shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6)); the black body also gets a 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.14) edge so it separates from it.
  • If the body is taller than the safe height, fall back to A.

Why A: on a tall phone B leaves a dark band of 100 pt or more above the body that does nothing, and the body's corners compete with the phone's own. A looks like the object in your hand and is simpler to build. B's advantage is that it reads as a device with an outline, and it looks the same on every phone.

docs.title: 3. Body finishes
docs.text:
Two finishes. Colours run top to bottom.

Part Silver Black Body #eceef1, #d9dce1 at 45 %, #c3c7ce #1b1c20, #101114 at 50 %, #08090a Wheel ring #fbfbfc to #e1e4e8, 1 px #a9aeb6 edge #2b2d32 to #1d1f23, 1 px #3a3c42 edge Groove round the centre #b4b9c0 #050506 Centre button #e6e9ed to #c9cdd4 #15161a to #0b0c0e Glyphs and MENU #5a5f67 (5.0:1 or better on the ring) #cfcfcf (8.8:1 or better on the ring) Wordmark #8d929a #5c5f66 Phone status bar text (fit A) dark light Screen frame #050608 with a 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.08) inner edge, both finishes

Rule. The finish follows the mode, not the style: silver in Light, black in Dark. Classic Light is therefore silver and Modern Dark is black, as drawn. This also covers Classic Dark (black) and Modern Light (silver), which the UI styles design has not drawn yet; their screens are still blocked on that design's Open question 1, but the body is not. Recommended on top: a Body setting (Automatic, Silver, Black), so an owner of a black neuPod can keep a black body with a light screen. Both cross-combinations are drawn:

docs.title: 4. The click wheel
docs.text: State Drawing Idle as the finish table Finger on the ring a 50 degree wedge of the ring under the finger, tinted rgba(0,0,0,.07) (silver) or rgba(255,255,255,.08) (black); it follows the finger Button pressed that button's 90 degree sector tinted rgba(0,0,0,.13) or rgba(255,255,255,.14), from touch-down until release Centre pressed the centre button tinted the same Disabled glyphs and MENU at 35 % opacity; ring and centre unchanged. For any moment the wheel cannot act; no screen drawn here uses it

docs.title: Hit zones
docs.text:
With R = D / 2, measured from the wheel's centre:

Zone Radius Acts as Centre 0 to 0.36 R Select Dead band 0.36 R to 0.44 R nothing; a touch that starts here is ignored Ring 0.44 R to 1.06 R (6 % beyond the drawn edge) turning, and the four buttons

The four buttons are 90 degree sectors of the ring centred on up (Menu), right (Next), down (Play/Pause) and left (Previous). Every zone is at least 44 pt in its smaller dimension at the minimum screen size.

Press or turn. A touch that starts on the ring is undecided until it moves.

  • Turn: the finger's angle about the centre has moved 7.5 degrees or more from where it touched down. From then on it is a turn until the finger lifts, and no button fires on release.
  • Press: the finger lifts, or is held, without reaching 7.5 degrees. The button is the sector under the touch-down point. The press shows and clicks at touch-down; if the touch then becomes a turn, the press is cancelled without acting.
  • Once turning, track the angle wherever the finger goes, including over the centre and outside the ring. Ignore samples closer than 0.2 R to the centre, where the angle is unstable.
  • A touch that starts on the centre is a Select press for as long as it stays within 0.44 R; sliding out cancels it.

docs.title: 5. Wheel behaviour, in numbers
docs.text:
The app ports the firmware's logic rather than imitating it. The constants are the firmware's (app/include/runtime_config.h, hal/include/hal_input.h, app/ui/ui_logic.[ch]).

Detents. The device's wheel reports 96 positions a turn and 4 positions make a list step.

Value One position 3.75 degrees of finger travel One list step (one detent) 15 degrees; 24 steps a turn Direction clockwise moves down a list, raises volume, seeks forward

Convert the finger's angle change to positions (keep the fraction), counted from the touch-down angle so the 7.5 degree threshold swallows nothing, and feed them to a port of ui_accel_feed().

Acceleration, exactly as the firmware: an energy value gains the positions received and decays linearly to zero over 150 ms; the step multiplier comes from the energy.

Energy (positions within the window) Multiplier Roughly, at a steady speed under 12 1x under 300 degrees a second 12 or more 2x from 300 degrees a second 24 or more 4x from 600 degrees a second 40 or more 8x from 1,000 degrees a second

A reversal drops the leftover positions of the old direction. The selection bar slides to an adjacent row in 80 ms; a move of more than three rows jumps.

Fast-scroll letter tile. On an indexed list (Artists, Albums, Songs and the like), the letter tile and the index rail appear while the multiplier is 2x or more, stay while the wheel moves, and fade over 150 ms once it has rested for 250 ms. (Trigger and timings as the UI document describes them; confirm against ui_list.c and ui_rail.c when porting.)

Press and hold.

Control Short press Held Previous, Next previous or next track (Previous restarts the track after 3 s of play) after 600 ms: scan at 10 times speed while held; applied 350 ms after release; ends itself after 30 s Centre, on Now Playing page 2 after 500 ms: seek mode. The wheel then moves the target by about 1/60 of the track a step (1 to 30 s); Select applies, Menu cancels, 10 s without input cancels Centre, elsewhere Select nothing in R1 Menu back one level nothing in R1 Play/Pause play or pause nothing in R1 (Open question 4)

On Now Playing the wheel sets the phone's system volume (owner decision 10). One step is one of the platform's volume steps. While it turns, the device's volume bar replaces the progress bar, and returns to progress 1.2 s after the wheel rests.

Haptics. One generator per kind, prepared in advance so the first tick is not late. Names are the platform APIs to use; check them against current documentation.

Event iOS Android Detent (each list step, volume step or seek step) UISelectionFeedbackGenerator.selectionChanged() HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK; SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK where available (API 34) Button or centre down UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .rigid), intensity 0.8 HapticFeedbackConstants.VIRTUAL_KEY Button or centre up UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .light), intensity 0.5 HapticFeedbackConstants.VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE (API 27) A hold takes effect (scan starts, seek mode entered) UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .medium) HapticFeedbackConstants.LONG_PRESS End of a list reached UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .soft), once HapticFeedbackConstants.REJECT (API 30), once
  • When accelerated steps arrive faster than 30 a second, fire at most 30 ticks a second and drop the rest.
  • No haptic on a press that is cancelled by becoming a turn, beyond the touch-down click already given.
  • Haptics obey the system setting and a Haptics setting in the app (On by default).

Click sound. Off by default (Click sound: Off, On). When on: a tick of about 8 ms per detent and a lower click per press, synthesised for this project (not a sample of any product), played as a system sound so it follows the ringer switch and silent mode, never mixed into the music stream, and limited to 30 a second like the haptics.

Other touches.

  • The first touch that lands on the wheel owns it until it lifts. Further touches on the wheel are ignored.
  • The wheel's edge is 0.18 W from each side of the phone, clear of the system edge gestures.
  • The system back gesture is Menu: Android's back gesture or button, and a swipe from the left edge on iOS. At Home, Android's back leaves the app as usual; on iOS it does nothing.
  • The home-indicator swipe and the notification shade are the system's and are never intercepted.

docs.title: 6. Direct touch on the screen
docs.text:
1: the wheel only 2: the wheel plus the screen (recommended)

Candidate 1. The screen is display only. Everything goes through the wheel, as on the device.

Candidate 2. The wheel works exactly as in candidate 1, and the screen also takes touches:

  • Tap a row: the selection bar jumps to it and it is activated, as wheel-to-it then Select. The row shows a pressed tint (rgba(24,88,200,.18) in Classic, rgba(255,255,255,.12) in Modern) from touch-down.
  • Drag a list: it scrolls with the finger; the selection bar stays on the row nearest its place on screen, so it never leaves the view.
  • Cover Flow: a horizontal drag moves the covers; a tap on the centre cover opens it.
  • Now Playing: a tap on the art opens page 2. The progress bar is not draggable (seek mode is the way to seek).
  • The status bar, the right-hand pane and panels' backgrounds take no touches. A panel's OK can be tapped.

Why 2: on a touch screen people tap what they see, and a row that ignores a tap feels broken. The cost: one-line rows are 31 to 36 pt high at the default text size, under the 44 pt guideline. The wheel with Select is the path that meets the guideline; taps are a convenience on top of it, and at the largest text tier the rows reach 44 pt.

docs.title: 7. Screens in the device
docs.text:
All at 393x852, fit A. Classic Light on the silver body, Modern Dark on the black body.

Screen Classic Modern Home Songs, wheel spinning, letter tile and rail Album with a disc heading Cover Flow Now Playing, at rest Now Playing, wheel setting the volume Now Playing, seek mode Centred panel, centre pressed Search, typing with the wheel Search, in the results

Notes on the screens the UI styles design had not drawn:

  • Letter tile and rail: 82 px tile, radius 15, 52 px from the right edge and 21 px below the status bar, the letter at 48 px; the rail is 26 px wide at the right edge, every second letter at 17 px with the current one at 22 px. Classic: tile rgba(24,24,24,.86) with a white letter. Modern: tile rgba(240,240,240,.92) with a #101010 letter.
  • Disc heading: a 34 px band, Small text. Classic: #e9ebee with #606060 text. Modern: rgba(255,255,255,.07) with #c4c4c4. Every disc gets one; track numbers restart under each. The album drawn is the owner's In Sides, whose first disc's track names are real.
  • Seek mode: the seek time at 72 px in the style's amber (#d08018 Classic, #e89828 Modern), a 6 px amber bar with a 26 px knob on a soft amber track, the times, and the hint Scroll: seek · Select: go · Menu: cancel. The format line and the album line give way to it. Classic's amber on white is 3.1:1; it is used only at this large size, and is flagged in the UI styles design.
  • Search: see below.

Search, by the wheel. Search is an item in the Music menu. It never raises the phone's keyboard, and tapping the field does nothing. It reuses the device's text entry (docs/ui-input.md: the letter ring and mode chips, in search mode, where every edit calls back so the list can filter live). The firmware has that widget but no Search screen yet, so the screen below is new for both.

Typing (first drawing). From the top of the 405 px content area:

Part Size (design px) Content Field 44 high in a 60 band magnifier, the text typed so far, a caret in the accent Live results three rows of 50 the best three matches, with what each is at the right in Small (Artist, Album · 1991) Letter ring 64 band, hairline above nine glyphs; the current one at 56 px in the accent, its neighbours at 30, 26, 22 and 18 px fading from ink to tertiary Mode chips 36 high, radius 18, in a 40 band abc, ABC, 123, space, del; the active one filled (Classic #d8e4f8 with #1858c8 text; Modern the accent with white text), the others outlined Hint Small, tertiary Select: type · Menu: delete · Play: results

The count of matches follows the play glyph in the status bar (4 found).

Control While typing Wheel turns the letter ring, one glyph a detent; the firmware's acceleration jumps three Centre types the current glyph (on space a space, on del deletes one) Previous, Next move along the mode chips Menu deletes one character; held, clears the field; on an empty field, leaves Search Play/Pause goes to the results

In the results (second drawing). The field stays at the top without its caret, and the full results follow under 30 px headings Artists, Albums, Songs, as an ordinary list: the wheel scrolls it, the centre opens a row, and Menu returns to typing with the text kept. Play/Pause is play or pause again.

With direct touch (candidate 2), a live result or a mode chip can also be tapped.

docs.title: 8. Largest text size
docs.text:
The 4:3 screen cannot reflow, so it honours the phone's text size by showing fewer, larger rows. The whole screen stays 600x450; type and bars are multiplied by k and the row count drops.

Tier k iOS text size Android font scale Rows, one line Rows, two lines Status bar Row height (design px) Standard 1 up to Large (the default) under 1.15 7 5 45 56 / 75 (as built) Large 7/6 Extra Large, Extra Extra Large 1.15 to under 1.3 6 4 52 66 / 99 Largest 7/5 Extra Extra Extra Large and the accessibility sizes 1.3 and above 5 3 63 77 / 129

On-phone sizes: Body is 15.0, 17.5 and 21.0 pt at 393 pt wide across the three tiers, and a one-line row is 32, 38 and 44 pt. The same tiers apply at every phone size, since the screen scales with the phone.

7 rows 6 rows 5 rows Home Songs

Rules:

  • Lists simply show fewer rows; they already scroll. Text that no longer fits ends in an ellipsis, and the focused row's text scrolls as a ticker, as on the device.
  • Fixed layouts scale their type by k and keep their structure: on Home the art shrinks to 200 px at the largest tier; on Now Playing the art shrinks to make room and the album line is dropped first, then the format line.
  • Nothing may clip. The app's golden tests cover every screen at all three tiers.
  • The accessibility sizes beyond the largest standard setting are capped at the largest tier (Open question 3).

docs.title: 9. Accessibility
docs.text:
With VoiceOver or TalkBack running, the picture of the device is not the interface; the semantics below are.

The screen. Each row is one element, in order, so swiping moves row by row.

Element Label Action A row its text, then its second line or value, then position: Albums, 4 of 7 activate opens it (always, whichever touch candidate is chosen) A greyed row its text, then the reason: Carrier Wave, AAC, can't play none; announced as dimmed Status bar one element: Playing, shuffle on, track 3 of 12, headphones, battery 78 percent none Screen title announced when the screen changes A panel focus moves to it; its title, then its text OK

The wheel is one adjustable element.

Lists and menus Now Playing Seek mode Label Click wheel Volume Seek Value the focused row, as above 62 percent 2 minutes 14 seconds of 4 minutes 1 Increment next row volume up one step forward one step Decrement previous row volume down one step back one step

It carries five named actions, in this order: Select, Menu, Previous track, Next track, and Play or Pause according to the state. The four buttons and the centre are not separate elements, so the screen reader does not stop on them twice.

  • A change made by the wheel is announced through the element's value, not as a separate announcement.
  • Haptics still fire. With Reduce Motion on, the selection bar and screen changes do not animate.
  • Switch control and external keyboards: arrow up and down move the selection, Return is Select, Escape is Menu, Space is Play/Pause, left and right arrows are Previous and Next.
  • Contrast and "nothing by colour alone" are inherited from the screens; the wheel's glyphs meet 4.5:1 in both finishes.

docs.title: 10. The phone's status bar
docs.text:
Recommended: shown, above the device. The phone's status bar stays visible, drawn over the body finish (fit A) or the surround (fit B), with dark text on silver and light text on black.

  • The device has no clock, by the owner's decision; on a phone the system clock is right there and people rely on it.
  • On a phone with a notch or Dynamic Island the space is reserved whether the bar is shown or not, so hiding it gains nothing. On a home-button phone it would gain 20 pt.
  • Hidden makes a purer picture and is what a game would do; it is the alternative, not drawn separately because it differs only by the missing text.
  • Merged (the phone's time or signal inside the device's bar) is not recommended: it changes the device's screen, which the UI styles design fixes.

In the device's own status bar the battery shows the phone's battery, the output icon follows the phone's route (headphones for wired, the Bluetooth glyph in blue for Bluetooth), and Wi-Fi is not shown in R1 because the app makes no network connection.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
For the owner. Nothing here is settled by the drawings.

Answered at gate 2 (22 November 2026), see the app spec's owner decision 13: 1, 3 to 11 and 13 are decided; 2 (direct touch) is judged by feel at gate 1; 12 stays open. Route icons (7): the speaker shows none, USB and wired outputs the jack plug, AirPlay and other wireless outputs a new generic external-speaker icon in the device's style.

# Question What was drawn meanwhile 1 Fit A or B Both, at three sizes; the screens use A 2 Direct touch: wheel only, or wheel plus the screen. Candidate 2's one-line rows are under 44 pt at the default text size Both; candidate 2 recommended 3 Text beyond the largest tier. The accessibility sizes are capped at 5 rows. Is that acceptable, or should those sizes switch to a plain, reflowing list view outside the device picture? Capped 4 Holding Play/Pause. The device has a separate Hold; the phone has its own lock. Should a hold do anything (stop and clear the queue, for example)? Nothing 5 Body setting. Follow the mode automatically only, or also offer Silver and Black as a choice Automatic, with both cross-combinations drawn 6 Proportions. The screen is wider and the frame thinner than the donor shell, for legibility. Closer to the real device would mean a screen of about 0.82 W (Body 14 pt at 393) Our own proportions 7 AirPlay and other routes. The device's icon set has headphones, a jack plug and Bluetooth. What shows for AirPlay, the phone's speaker and USB audio? Not drawn; speaker shows no icon 8 The wordmark on the body. Keep neuPod between the screen and the wheel, or leave the body plain Drawn, small and low-contrast 9 Left-edge swipe as Menu on iOS Specified as Menu 10 Click sound. Whether it plays through headphones or only the phone's speaker System sound, follows the ringer switch 11 Search placement. An item in the Music menu, or on Home Music menu 13 Search, three live results. Three rows fit above the letter ring. Fewer and larger, or none until Play/Pause? At the larger text tiers only two, then one, will fit Three 12 Classic Dark and Modern Light screens are still undrawn (UI styles Open question 1); only their bodies are covered here Bodies only

docs.title: UI styles: Classic and Modern, 21 November 2026
docs.text:
A design session with the owner on how the firmware UI should look and behave. It builds on the 12 November design review and overrides it where the two disagree.

The brief (owner): the interface should look and feel like the original click-wheel player's. New components and some animation will be added, but as much of the original as possible is kept, for familiarity.

This folder holds:

  • this README: the decisions, the rules and the exact values;
  • mockups/: every screen that was drawn, as a PNG and as the standalone HTML it was rendered from (the HTML is the reference for exact colours, gradients and sizes);
  • IMPLEMENTATION-BRIEF.md: the working instructions for building it;
  • PROGRESS.md: the checklist of work, ticked off as it merges.

The mock-ups are design intent drawn in HTML, not firmware output. They are drawn at 600x450, the touch AMOLED boards' profile, in Montserrat Medium (22 / 26 / 38 px) with Lucide icons. Album art squares are placeholders. Track names on the first screens are the test fixtures; the Music screens use real names from the owner's library.

docs.title: Owner decisions (21 November 2026)
docs.text:
1. Two styles, two modes each. A theme is a style (Classic or Modern) and a mode (Light or Dark). Auto still switches the mode when the backlight dims.
  2. Classic is the 6G look as shipped: gradient selection bar, glossy status bar, green shaded battery. It is drawn fresh, not copied from the original's artwork.
  3. Modern goes beyond it: "art-led glass". True black, a backdrop and accent taken from the album art, translucent tinted chrome. It borrows the layering idea from current phone design but not live blur or refraction.
  4. A monochrome style is parked. When it returns it may bring its own fonts, provided they go through the same rendering rules (display-text filter, glyph coverage, licences screen).
  5. The AMOLED leads. Design at 600x450 first; 480x360 and 320x240 are scale-downs that must pass the layout audit.
  6. Status bar is the same on every screen: play state at the left, title in the middle, hardware icons at the right.
  7. Play state is one of three glyph groups: play; play then the two-arrow loop (repeat); play then the crossing arrows (shuffle). Merged single icons were looked for in five open icon sets and none works at status-bar size.
  8. Track position stays (3 of 12) after the play glyph.
  9. No clock. There is no RTC, so the time is unknown after every cold start. The clock is dropped everywhere.
  10. Headphones icon only while a 3.5 mm plug is in the jack. A jack-plug icon in its place when the output is set to Line. Bluetooth icon is blue when a headset is connected or in use.
  11. Volume on Now Playing is not permanent. Turning the wheel swaps the progress bar for a volume bar with a quiet speaker at one end and a loud one at the other; it reverts when the wheel rests. No dB figure.
  12. Volume on any other screen swaps the status-bar title for a small volume bar for about a second. The bottom HUD strip goes away.
  13. The format is less prominent: one small grey line (FLAC 16/44.1), no pill. The output is not written on Now Playing at all; the status-bar icon says it.
  14. The toast strip goes away. Messages go to one of three places (below).

docs.title: What a style owns
docs.text:
Today a theme is a table of 14 colours (app/ui/ui_theme.[ch]) and components such as the battery are fixed drawings. From now on:

A style owns Shared by every style Its colour table, one per mode, with the same 14 token names Layout: every position and size in ui_metrics_t A small set of skins: status bar fill, battery, selection bar, scroll bar, progress and volume bars, panel, art frame, list ground Row counts (7 single-line, 5 two-line) Whether it draws an art backdrop Fonts, glyph coverage, the display-text filter Wheel and button behaviour, copy, screen structure

Both styles therefore run the same screens and the same snapshot tours.

docs.title: Status bar
docs.text:
Three zones, in this order, on every screen:

Left: play state, then context.

State Glyphs Stopped nothing Playing play triangle Paused pause bars Shuffle on transport glyph, then crossing arrows (Lucide shuffle) Repeat all transport glyph, then two-arrow loop (Lucide repeat) Repeat one transport glyph, then loop with a 1 (Lucide repeat-1) Shuffle and repeat transport glyph, crossing arrows, loop

The mode glyphs stay while paused. After the glyphs comes the screen's context text where it has one: 3 of 12 on Now Playing, the count on a list (1,204, 9 albums). Home and menus show the glyphs only.

Centre: the screen title. It gives way, for one to two seconds, to a message or to the volume bar (see Feedback).

Right: hardware, right-aligned, always in this order: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, output (headphones or jack plug), lock, battery. A member that does not apply is not drawn and the others close up toward the battery.

Icon Shown Colour Wi-Fi station joined ink Bluetooth a headset is saved dim when not connected; blue when connected or in use Headphones a plug is in the 3.5 mm jack and the output is wired ink Jack plug Audio output is set to Line ink Battery always style skin; rules as built (green charging, red below 15 %)

The jack-plug glyph is not in Lucide and was drawn for this design: see mockups/classic-status-states.html.

Not yet drawn, listed so they are not forgotten: fast-forward and rewind while scanning, opening (matters for network streaming), can't-play, recording, and the three busy dots for a background library update.

docs.title: Now Playing
docs.text:
• At rest: art, title, artist, Album . Year, the small format line, the progress bar with elapsed and remaining and the repeat / shuffle word between them.
  • Wheel moves: the progress bar and the times are replaced in place by the volume bar with a speaker glyph at each end. It returns to progress when the wheel has rested (use the existing 1.2 s hold).
  • The permanent volume strip, the dB figure, the format pill and the output pill are removed.
  • Seek mode and page 2 are unchanged in behaviour and take the style's skins.

docs.title: Feedback: three places
docs.text:
The sliding toast strip and the bottom volume HUD are removed in both styles. A message goes to exactly one of:

Place Use it when It must not Messages that move here Status bar title (swaps for about 2 s) Something changed by itself and the user only needs to know Need an answer; exceed about 24 characters Headphones unplugged, Couldn't reconnect - paused, Line out off, No audio output, headset connected / disconnected, Library updated, and the transient refusals Busy, Can't pair now, Not now, Bluetooth is starting The row The feedback is about the row under the selection bar Say anything unrelated to that row Success as a flash of the bar with a tick: Added to On-The-Go, Removed from On-The-Go. A reason on a greyed row, visible before the press: Not in the library, Not an audio device, Plug into the jack first, No speaker in this device, Nothing playing, unplayable codecs (AAC, can't play) Centred panel (Select or Menu dismisses) Something was lost or is about to be Be used for routine confirmations Battery empty, Can't save: settings full, Paired, but not saved (read-only card), Card is full, Card read error, Library update stopped

Rules:

  • Volume and a message share the status-bar title. Volume wins; the message shows after it.
  • Can't open: too many screens is an internal limit and should not reach the user: fix the cause or log it.
  • The firmware raises about 50 toasts today (grep ui_toast_show app/ui). Every one must be assigned to a place; none may be silently dropped.

docs.title: Music screens
docs.text:
• Music menu: split like Home. Cover Flow, Playlists, Artists, Albums, Songs, Genres, Compilations, Update Library; the right pane previews the highlighted item (four covers for Albums).
  • An artist's albums: All Songs first, then a two-line row per album with a cover thumbnail, the year and the song count. Drawn in year order (designer's call, see Open questions).
  • Cover Flow: Classic is the angled version with reflections on black. Modern is five flat rounded covers (220 / 150 / 100 px) over a backdrop washed in the centre album's colours.
  • Album: the status-bar title is the album; a header shows the cover, the artist, the year and the song count; then numbered tracks.

docs.title: Classic, Light: the values
docs.text:
All at 600x450. A | B in a gradient means a hard step at the midpoint (the gloss line).

Part Value Ground / text #ffffff; ink #181818, secondary #606060, tertiary #767676, disabled #a0a0a0 Status bar 45 px; top to bottom #fdfdfd, #dcdfe3 at 50 % | #c6cad0 at 51 %, #b6bbc2; 1 px #8c9199 under it; glyphs #3a3d42, dim #9a9ea5, Bluetooth active #1858c8 Battery body 44x22, 2 px #5d626a outline, radius 4, inside #f4f5f6; fill top to bottom #c9f5a3, #63c62f at 45 % | #3f9c1c at 55 %, #58b82a; terminal 4x10 Selection bar full width, square; #6db3f5, #2f80e0 at 50 % | #1b62cf at 51 %, #1858c8; white text with a 1 px dark shadow Selection flash #d6eafd, #a9d0f8 | #93c3f5, #8abdf3; text and tick #10233f Right pane (Home, Music) #f3f4f6 to #dde0e4, 1 px #b9bdc4 at its left; art with a soft drop shadow Scroll bar 14 px gutter #d5d8dc to #f1f2f4; thumb left to right #8fc3f6, #2f80e0, #1858c8, radius 4 Progress / volume bar 12 px, radius 6; track #c9ccd1 to #eceef0 with 1 px #9da2a9; fill as the selection bar, starting #8fc3f6 Art square corners; on Now Playing a 56 px reflection at 30 % fading to nothing Album header 121 px, #f3f4f6 to #e3e6e9, 1 px #b9bdc4 under it, 96 px art Panel 452 px wide, white, 1 px #6f757d, radius 10; title strip in the status-bar gradient; the OK row is a 52 px selection bar; scrim rgba(40,44,52,.45) Cover Flow black to #1a1c20; centre 200 px, sides 156 px turned 58 degrees, reflections

docs.text:
Part Value Ground #050608, effectively black Backdrop two soft washes in the art's two main colours (one near a top corner at about 45 to 55 % strength, one near the opposite bottom corner at about 75 to 85 %), under a darkening scrim of 30 % at the top to 50 to 55 % at the bottom. Made once per track from the art (a small blurred, darkened copy), never blurred live. No art: the ground alone Accent the art's dominant colour with its lightness clamped until white text on it is at least 4.5:1. In the mock-ups #d9734e becomes #b8502c (7:1) and #e9c46a becomes #8a5a12 (5.9:1) Text ink #f0f0f0, secondary #b0b0b0 to #c8c8c8, disabled #7c7c7c Status bar rgba(10,10,12,.5) over the backdrop, 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.10) under it; dim glyphs #7a7a7a; Bluetooth active #5aa2ff (fixed, not the accent) Battery capsule 44x22, 2 px rgba(255,255,255,.6), radius 8; fill #8cecb4 to #30b870, radius 4; terminal 3x9 List ground rgba(0,0,0,.38) to .42 over the backdrop; dividers rgba(255,255,255,.08) Selection bar inset 6 px, radius 14 (one line) or 16 (two lines); the accent, with a highlight of rgba(255,255,255,.16) fading out by 55 % of its height, a 1 px light top edge rgba(255,255,255,.28) and a shadow 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.45); white text Selection flash the bar keeps its colour and gains a 3 px ring rgba(255,255,255,.6) and a tick Scroll bar 4 px, rgba(255,255,255,.45), no track Progress bar 6 px, radius 3; track rgba(255,255,255,.2); fill a light tint of the art colour (#f2a586 in the mock-up) Volume (Now Playing) a floating capsule 44 px high, radius 22, rgba(0,0,0,.4), 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.14); bar 8 px, fill #f0f0f0 Art radius 16, shadow 0 12px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.6), 1 px light top edge Panel 452 px wide, rgba(28,28,32,.92), 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.16), radius 22; OK is a 50 px accent button, radius 14; scrim rgba(0,0,0,.6) Cover Flow flat covers 220 / 150 / 100 px, radii 20 / 16 / 12, opacity 1 / .85 / .6

The existing rule that every colour is RGB565-exact was written for the LCD. Keep it for flat fills; gradient stops and alpha blends on the AMOLED are exempt.

docs.title: Other resolutions
docs.text: Lengths scale through the existing metrics profiles: 600x450 values times 4/5 for 480x360 and 8/15 for 320x240, rounded as ui_metrics.c already does. Row counts do not change. On 320x240 the left of the status bar is tight when shuffle and repeat are both on; the track position may drop out in that one state.

docs.text:
Not decided. Do not settle these by guessing; ask the owner.

Gate 2 (22 November 2026), app spec owner decision 13: 9 is decided (placeholder cover, "Nothing playing" and the song count). Classic Light is adjusted to 4.5:1 contrast where the values below fall short, and Bluetooth saved versus connected gets a cue besides colour (bears on 4).

# Question What was drawn meanwhile 1 Classic Dark and Modern Light have not been designed Only Classic Light and Modern Dark exist 2 Typeface. The 6G used a Helvetica-like face; both styles use Montserrat for now Montserrat 3 Row "done" feedback in Classic: the pale flash drawn, or the original's quick blink Pale flash with a tick 4 Saved but unconnected Bluetooth: dimmed icon (as built) or hidden Dimmed 5 Modern recolouring: in Cover Flow and Album the backdrop and accent follow the album on screen; elsewhere the playing track. Or always the playing track? Follows the album on screen in those two views 6 Album order under an artist: by year or by name By year 7 Thumbnails on album rows cost a decode per row Drawn with thumbnails 8 Classic Cover Flow angled needs the performance test first; the firmware has only the flat one Angled 9 Home right-hand pane when nothing is playing, now that the clock is gone Not drawn 10 Performance. Modern depends on alpha blending and a full-screen backdrop at speed on a microcontroller. docs.title: What this overrides
docs.text:
• 12 November review: the toast strip (DS-5, owner decision 8), the volume HUD (NP-4), the Now Playing pills and volume strip (NP-1), the clock in the status bar's left slot (DS-3), the rounded inset selection bar as the only look (DS-4; it becomes Modern's).
  • docs/ui.md describes the UI as built. It stays correct until each piece of this design merges, and is updated in the same PR as the code.

docs.title: Implementation brief: UI styles (Classic and Modern)
docs.text:
You are implementing the design in README.md in this folder. Read it in full first, and look at every PNG in mockups/; open the matching .html when you need an exact colour, gradient or size.

This is a long job. You work through PROGRESS.md one item at a time, in a loop, until every item is ticked or a stop condition is met. PROGRESS.md is the only record of where you are: a new session, or one whose context was compacted, starts by reading it and carries on from the first unticked item.

docs.title: Before the first item
docs.text:
1. Load the repo's neupod skill (.claude/skills/neupod/SKILL.md) and follow its rules for every target. They are not repeated here and they win over this brief. Read CONTRIBUTING.md.
  2. Read docs/ui.md, docs/adr/0018-ui-resolution-profiles.md, app/ui/ui_theme.[ch], app/ui/ui_metrics*.h, app/ui/ui_frame.c, app/ui/ui_strips.c and tests/CMakeLists.txt (the tours).
  3. Build host and run ctest. Everything must pass before you change anything. If it does not, stop and report.
  4. Reconcile the checklist. Walk app/ui/*.c and the tours and compare every screen and state you find with PROGRESS.md. Add what is missing, in the right phase, in a docs-only PR. Do not remove items.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
Repeat until done:

  1. Pick the first unticked item in PROGRESS.md whose phase is open (a phase opens when the one before it is complete, unless the file says otherwise). Skip an item marked BLOCKED and note why it still is.
  2. Plan it briefly: what the README says, which files change, which tours cover it, what could regress.
  3. Implement on a branch named per CONTRIBUTING.md. Keep app/ portable. Reuse ui_metrics_t; add fields to it for new lengths, never literal pixel values in screen code. Name colours by token; add skin functions to the style, never an if (style == ...) inside a screen.
  4. Verify, all of:
  5. host unit tests and every UI tour pass at 320x240, 480x360 and 600x450, with the layout audit on;
  6. the item is covered by a tour snapshot in each style it applies to, at each of the three sizes; add tour steps where there are none;
  7. you have looked at the new snapshots next to the mock-up PNGs. They need not match pixel for pixel (LVGL is not a browser), but structure, colours, proportions and text must agree. Describe any difference you leave;
  8. text contrast: at least 4.5:1 for anything that must be read; extend the existing contrast test to the new tables;
  9. builds for every platform CI builds: host, rp2350, rp2350-amoled241, esp32s3, y2;
  10. the frozen Pico 2 W image: report flash and static RAM deltas. It has about 100 bytes of static RAM spare. New style code must cost it nothing: gate it at compile time the way NEUPOD_UI_HIRES does. If an item cannot be done without growing that image, stop and ask.
  11. Review: have a fresh reviewer (a subagent that has not seen the work) read the diff against the README.
  12. Document in the same PR: docs/ui.md (it describes the UI as built), CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased), and any ADR the change touches. A new third-party asset goes into LICENSE.md and the Licences screen; the licences test must pass.
  13. PR, per the repo's rules; squash-merge once CI is green.
  14. Tick the item in PROGRESS.md with the PR number and the date, in that same PR or the next one. Add one line under "Notes" for anything the next session must know.
  15. Go to 1.

Keep PRs small: one item, or a few that cannot be separated.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Host tours are the main check. On top of them:

  • Phase 0 runs on the two Waveshare AMOLED boards; it exists to measure them.
  • At the end of each phase, deploy to whichever of the AMOLED boards and the Y2 are attached (bench-status.sh) and check that phase's screens by eye and by screenshot where the target supports it. Record what was verified, on which board, with the date, in the PR and in PROGRESS.md. If no board is attached, write "not hardware-tested" and carry on.
  • Every device rule in the neupod skill applies, including the Y2's.

docs.title: Stop and ask the owner
docs.text:
Stop the loop, summarise, and wait, when:

  • an item depends on one of the README's Open questions; do not decide them. You may prepare options (for example snapshots of two variants) to make the answer quick;
  • the README and the code or an ADR conflict in a way the README does not address;
  • phase 0's numbers say an effect cannot be drawn at an acceptable frame rate, and the fallback changes the look;
  • a change would grow the frozen Pico 2 W image, change an owner decision, or is one the neupod skill says to ask about;
  • the same item has failed verification three times.

When you stop, leave the tree clean, PROGRESS.md current, and say exactly what you need.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
The checklist in PROGRESS.md follows these.

Phase 0: measure (throwaway). On each AMOLED board, time these at 600x450 and report frame time and CPU load: a vertical gradient bar one row high sliding one row; a full-width alpha-blended panel over an image; a full-screen backdrop image with a list scrolling over it; five album tiles moving one Cover Flow step, flat, and with the two-plane angle of the Classic mock-up; a 3 px ring appearing round a row. Also measure making the backdrop (a small blurred, darkened copy of a decoded cover) once per track: time and memory. This code is not merged; the report is (docs/design/2026-11-21-ui-styles/PHASE0-RESULTS.md). Stop after phase 0 and show the owner the numbers.

Phase 1: the style layer. A theme becomes style x mode. Each style supplies its colour tables and its skin functions. Today's look is kept as the build default until both new styles are complete, so nothing changes for a user yet. Settings > Display gains Style (Classic, Modern) next to Theme; stored like the other settings. Tours can select a style. Classic Dark and Modern Light are BLOCKED on Open question 1.

Phase 2: status bar. The three zones, the play-state glyphs, the hardware icons and their rules, the clock removed (including the Home pane; Open question 9 covers what replaces it), title swap for a message and for volume.

Phase 3: feedback. Assign every ui_toast_show() call to one of the three places per the README table, build the row flash, the greyed-row reason and the centred panel, then remove the toast strip and the bottom HUD.

Phase 4: Now Playing. Volume swaps with the progress bar; the format line; pills and volume strip removed; seek mode and page 2 in both styles; Modern's backdrop and accent from the art.

Phase 5: lists and menus. Selection bar, scroll bar and list ground skins; Home; the Music menu with its preview pane; every library list; fast-scroll tile and rail.

Phase 6: albums. An artist's albums with thumbnails; the album header; Cover Flow in both styles.

Phase 7: everything else, in both styles: Settings and its pages, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, Files, Playlists, the wheel input widgets, library building / empty / error states, Hold and lock, the power-hold line, the boot splash, Licences, Diagnostics.

Phase 8: finish. Make the new styles the default (Classic Light) where the build carries them; a full pass of every screen in every style at every size, on host and on each attached board; docs/ui.md rewritten to match; this folder's README updated where the build ended up different, with the reason.

docs.title: Done
docs.text: Every item in PROGRESS.md is ticked or marked BLOCKED with an owner question attached, CI is green on main, and the final report lists: what shipped, what is blocked and on what, the Pico 2 W size deltas, and what was and was not verified on hardware.

docs.title: Phase 0 results: effect timings on the AMOLED boards
docs.text:
Measured 21 November 2026 for IMPLEMENTATION-BRIEF.md, phase 0. The bench code is throwaway and is not merged: branch chore/phase0-bench (app/ui/ui_bench.c, CMake option NEUPOD_UI_BENCH).

Board Status ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.41 (ESP32-S3R8, 240 MHz, 8 MB octal PSRAM) Measured (below) RP2350-Touch-AMOLED-2.41 (RP2350B, 8 MB QSPI PSRAM at 62.5 MHz SCK) Measured (below). Single UI core: the UI task's core shows almost no idle time

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• The 600x450 profile, the product's LVGL configuration (software renderer, one draw unit, partial mode with two 600 x 30 render buffers in internal RAM, RGB565), the real flush path. Only LV_GRADIENT_MAX_STOPS is raised to 4 for the Classic bar.
  • Each test changes the scene once per UI pass, as fast as it will go, for 5 s after a 300 ms warm-up. fps is therefore capacity, not a capped rate. frame is one lv_timer_handler pass that rendered, flush included. flush is the part of it spent in the flush (copy into the panel shadow in PSRAM, then QSPI to the panel). Render = frame - flush.
  • ui core is the UI task's share of its core (os_task_stats); the other core stays about 95 % idle in every test.
  • All pictures are synthesised (a 600x450 RGB565 backdrop, a 160x160 cover), held in PSRAM. No JPEG decode.
  • Numbers are stable: two full rounds agree within 1 %.

docs.title: ESP32-S3: frame tests
docs.text:
Test What changes each frame fps frame ms avg / p95 flush ms render ms ui core grad_bar Classic 4-stop gradient bar moves one row (7-row list) 35.7 27.0 / 27.8 13.5 13.5 64 % ring 3 px ring on the Modern bar appears / disappears 55.5 17.1 / 18.1 8.3 8.8 64 % alpha_panel 452 px panel at 50 % and a 45 px 50 % status strip over a full-screen image 13.2 74.5 / 75.4 27.0 47.5 68-74 % backdrop_list list ground at 40 % over a full-screen backdrop, list scrolls one row 6.0 163 / 164 52.9 110 75 % backdrop_list_smooth same, LVGL animated scroll 5.8 163 / 164 52.8 110 67-70 % flow_flat Modern Cover Flow: rounded tiles 220/150/100, opacity 1/.85/.6, one step over 250 ms 5.3 185 / 189 52.8 132 78 % flow_angled Classic Cover Flow: side tiles turned (6 px slices), 30 % reflections, gradient ground 2.6-2.8 349-376 / 361-388 49.7 ~310 86 % backdrop_draw_scaled 75x56 or 150x112 backdrop stretched to full screen by LVGL, every frame 4.4 226 / 227 54-55 171 80 % backdrop_draw_full pre-scaled 600x450 backdrop drawn 1:1, every frame 9.6 103 / 103 60 43 63 %

A full-screen flush costs about 53 ms (540 KB at QSPI 40 MHz is 27 ms on the wire; the rest is the byte-swapped copy into the PSRAM shadow and back out through the bounce buffers). Small changes are fine: the Classic bar moving and the Modern ring both stay above 30 fps. Anything that repaints the whole screen over a picture runs at 3 to 13 fps.

docs.title: ESP32-S3: making the backdrop (once per track)
docs.text:
From a 160x160 RGB565 cover: downscale, 3-pass box blur, scrim (30 % top to 55 % bottom). Average of 8 runs.

Small buffer Bytes Blur radius Scale Blur Scrim Total PSRAM vs internal 75x56 16,800 2 2.4 ms 5.7 ms 0.4 ms 8.4 ms same 150x112 67,200 5 6.0 ms 23.3 ms 1.5 ms 30.8 ms same

Upscaling either one into a 600x450 buffer (bilinear, 540,000 bytes of PSRAM) takes another 119 ms. Per track this is cheap either way. Drawing the result is what costs (above): a pre-scaled full-size backdrop draws in 43 ms of render, LVGL scaling the small one on every frame in 171 ms.

docs.title: RP2350: frame tests
docs.text:
Same tests, same method. Two rounds agree within 1 %.

Test fps frame ms avg / p95 flush ms render ms vs ESP32-S3 grad_bar 44.0 21.9 / 22.2 4.9 17.0 faster (flush) ring 62.5 15.1 / 16.8 2.7 12.4 faster (flush) alpha_panel 13.1 75.2 / 75.7 9.2 66.0 same backdrop_list 5.5 178 / 186 17.6 160 slower backdrop_list_smooth 5.4 177 / 179 17.6 160 slower flow_flat 4.4 218 / 232 19.0 199 slower flow_angled 1.9 505 / 533 17.5 488 slower backdrop_draw_scaled 4.0-4.2 235-244 / 243-253 19.1 216-225 same backdrop_draw_full 11.9 82.7 / 88 19.4 63 faster

The flush is about three times cheaper than the ESP32's: 18 ms for a full frame. Rendering is slower, about 1.2 to 1.6 times, wherever pictures are read from PSRAM. The result is the same picture as the ESP32: small changes are fine, and full-screen repaints over a picture run at 2 to 13 fps.

docs.title: RP2350: making the backdrop
docs.text:
Small buffer Where Bytes Scale Blur Scrim Total 75x56 internal 16,800 8.1 ms 10.1 ms 0.6 ms 18.8 ms 75x56 PSRAM 16,800 9.8 ms 17.3 ms 0.8 ms 28.0 ms 150x112 PSRAM 67,200 20.6 ms 89.7 ms 6.9 ms 117 ms 150x112 internal does not fit (2 x 33,600 B from an 80 KB RTOS heap)

Upscaling to a 600x450 PSRAM buffer: 294-301 ms, once per track. All of this is still cheap next to a track change.

docs.title: What this means for the design
docs.text:
At 30 fps the budget is 33 ms a frame. On both boards as configured today:

  • Classic Light is affordable for lists, the selection bar and the status bar. Its Cover Flow is not: the angled version draws at 2 to 3 fps, the flat one at 4 to 5.
  • Modern Dark is not affordable as drawn. Every scroll over the backdrop repaints the screen (5 to 6 fps). Panels and translucent chrome over a picture are around 13 fps.

Most of the cost is software rendering on one core, plus a flush that blocks it. Engineering options exist that do not change the look; none has been tried yet:

  1. Overlap the flush with rendering (asynchronous DMA flush, both render buffers in use). Saves up to the flush per frame: 53 ms on the ESP32-S3, 18 ms on the RP2350.
  2. A second LVGL draw unit on the other core (LV_DRAW_SW_DRAW_UNIT_CNT 2 with an RTOS LV_USE_OS). Up to about half the render time. Free on the ESP32-S3 (its second core is 95 % idle); on the RP2350 core 1 runs audio, so only partly.
  3. QSPI to the ESP32's panel at 80 MHz, if the RM690B0 and the board allow it (not checked).
  4. Always pre-scale the backdrop to 600x450 per track (119 ms once), never let LVGL scale it per frame.
  5. Bigger render buffers in internal RAM, and composing the static backdrop once with the list ground baked in, so a scroll blends rows over a flat picture instead of picture plus a 40 % layer.

Even all five together are unlikely to bring a full-screen repaint over a picture under 33 ms on either chip: the best render alone is 43 ms (ESP32-S3) and 63 ms (RP2350) for a pre-scaled backdrop with nothing on it. Fallbacks that do change the look (the owner's call, brief "Stop and ask"):

  • Modern without the backdrop under lists (art wash only on Now Playing, where nothing scrolls), or the backdrop dimmed to a flat colour taken from the art.
  • Cover Flow: flat in both styles; or the angled Classic version drawn only at rest, flat while moving.
  • Fewer animated frames: jump a row instead of sliding, at both styles' cost.

docs.title: Not yet done
docs.text:
• Nothing was checked by eye on the panel (the bench prints numbers only).
  • A real JPEG decode at 160x160 (the backdrop numbers start from an already-decoded cover).

docs.title: App Custom mode, 25 November 2026
docs.text:
A fourth mode for the phone app's device view. Light, Dark and Auto stay as they are: the body finish follows the mode. Custom lets the user choose the colour and the transparency of three parts (the body, the wheel, the centre button), and where a part is see-through a picture of a neuPod board shows from underneath, the "clear case" look.

It answers the owner's request of 25 November 2026 (backlog AP-1) and extends the device view design. It changes paint, not layout: every position, hit zone and wheel number in that design stands.

This folder holds:

  • this README: decisions, rules and exact values;
  • mockups/: 20 drawings as PNG and as the standalone HTML they were rendered from;
  • render.py: the generator. It imports the device view's render.py for the geometry and the screens, and its hsv, paint and increase_contrast functions are the reference implementation of the rules in section 4;
  • IMPLEMENTATION-BRIEF.md: the working instructions for building it;
  • PROGRESS.md: the checklist of work.

The mock-ups are design intent drawn in HTML, not app output. A blue circle marks a finger and is not part of the UI. The Home screen inside the device is the UI styles mock-up reused unchanged, so it shows items and a Wi-Fi icon the app does not have; only the body, the wheel and the new screens are this design.

Drawn fresh. Nothing here copies Apple's artwork, and no colour or look is named after an Apple product colour. The board pictures are placeholders drawn by render.py and labelled as such in every drawing. They are not neuPod boards and must not ship.

docs.title: Owner decisions (25 November 2026)
docs.text:
1. Mode is Light, Dark, Auto, Custom. Custom sets the colour and transparency of the body, the wheel and the centre button separately, with a colour wheel as the picker. A custom look carries its own screen choice (Light, Dark or Auto) and its board picture. Style (Classic or Modern) stays a separate setting.
  2. The app never scrolls and never shows scroll bars, vertical or horizontal: the device always fits the phone. Inside the 4:3 screen, Custom's screens avoid scrolling too where they can.
  3. Three starter looks ship with the app: Harbour, Sea glass and Clear case.

Everything else below is the designer's proposal until the owner confirms it.

docs.title: Recommendations at a glance
docs.text: # Question Recommendation Alternatives 1 Where it lives Mode cycles in place through four values; a Custom look row under it opens the list of looks Mode opens a page of four choices; the row hidden unless Mode is Custom 2 The editor In the 4:3 screen, with the real body and wheel round it as the live preview A full-phone editor with a small picture of the device 3 Input Both. The wheel does everything; touching the colour wheel on the screen is a shortcut Wheel only; touch only 4 Readability Legends are pure black or pure white, chosen by the luminance under them, switching at 0.179; a part that still falls short is painted flat Legends on backing plates; clamping the colour 5 Transparency Body sharp, up to 85 %; wheel and centre over a pre-blurred copy, up to 60 %; a solid cap under the phone's status bar One picture, sharp everywhere, with plates under the legends 6 Board pictures 1200 x 3120 px, anchored on the wheel's centre, three in the set A picture fitted to each phone 7 Presets Six looks, listed in Settings > Custom look; saved as they are edited Eight, in a scrolling list; an explicit Save 8 Accessibility Reduce Transparency paints every part solid; Increase Contrast also moves brightness until legends reach 7:1 Ignoring the settings in Custom 9 Classic and Modern Both work unchanged; the black screen frame keeps any body off the screen A neutral band round the screen 10 Data model Each part stores hue, saturation, brightness, transparency as whole numbers; RGB is computed Storing RGB and alpha

docs.title: 1. Where it lives
docs.text:
• Mode cycles in place on Select, in the owner's order: Light, Dark, Auto, Custom. It has no chevron, because it changes a value and does not open a list. (The build cycles Auto, Light, Dark today; the order changes.)
  • Custom look sits directly under Mode and is always shown. Its value is the name of the look in use; its chevron opens the list of looks. Opening a look from that list sets Mode to Custom, so there is one way in and no greyed row.
  • When Mode is not Custom the row still shows the last look's name. Nothing about the look is lost by leaving Custom.

Why: the design system's rules are that a row which toggles has no chevron and a row which opens a list has one, and that the five controls do the same thing everywhere. Two rows keep both rules. Settings stays within seven rows at the standard text size as drawn (Style, Mode, Custom look, Library, Click sound, Haptics, Licences); the specification's other Settings items need a home that keeps to owner decision 2 (Open question 6).

Alternatives. Mode opens a page of four radio rows with Custom leading on to the looks: one more press for the common change between Light and Dark. The row hidden unless Mode is Custom: the list changes length under the selection bar, and the design system says empty is stated, not hidden.

docs.title: 2. The editor
docs.text:
The editor is three screens deep, each an ordinary device screen. The body, the wheel and the centre button round the screen are the live preview: every change repaints them at once, at full size, on the real thing.

Custom look A look A part

Custom look (the list). One row per look, then New look. The look in use carries a tick. Moving the selection bar onto a look previews it on the body after the wheel has rested for 250 ms; Menu leaves with the look in use unchanged. Select opens the look and makes it the look in use.

A look. Seven rows, no scrolling:

Row Value Select Body swatch, then Solid or 55 % clear opens the part editor on Body Wheel the same opens the part editor on Wheel Centre the same opens the part editor on Centre Board the board's name opens the board picker Screen Light, Dark or Auto cycles in place Name the look's name opens the device's text entry (the letter ring), 16 characters at most Reset or delete opens two rows: Reset to default, Delete look

A part (the colour wheel). At 600x450, under the 45 px status bar, whose title is the part and whose left slot is the look's name:

Part Size (design px) Content Part tabs 36 high, radius 18, in a 52 band Body, Wheel, Centre; the one being edited filled (Classic #d8e4f8 with #1858c8 text; Modern the accent with white text), the others outlined Colour wheel 250 across, 19 from the left hue round the circle, red at the top, clockwise; saturation from the centre (none) to the rim (full); the whole disc darkened by the brightness. A 26 px ring marks the colour Swatch and hex 40 band, right column a 30 px swatch and the colour as #rrggbb. Read only Four fields 60 each, right column Hue 0 to 359 degrees, Saturation, Brightness and Transparency in per cent; each a name, a value and a 10 px bar with an 18 px knob. The focused field is the screen's one selection bar Legend note Small, secondary, 30 band what the rule in section 4 did: Legends: white ink, 6.3:1, with painted flat or Held at 50 % so MENU stays readable when it applies Hint Small, tertiary, 36 band Scroll: change · Prev/Next: field · Select: next part Wheel, see-through Centre, pressed

Which part is being edited is said three ways, none by colour alone: the status-bar title, the filled tab, and a single pulse of that part's edge on the body (the edge goes from 30 % to 100 % ink and back over 400 ms; skipped with Reduce Motion on).

The board picker. A split screen like Home: the three boards at the left, a thumbnail of the highlighted one at the right. Moving the bar previews the board on the body after 250 ms; Select chooses it.

Alternative considered: a full-phone editor with sliders under a small picture of the device. It has more room, but the preview shrinks to a thumbnail, the wheel stops being the input, and it is the "generic app with a neuPod logo" the specification rules out.

docs.title: 3. Input
docs.text:
Recommendation: both, with the wheel as the complete path.

Control In the part editor Wheel changes the focused field, one step a detent, with the firmware's acceleration Previous, Next move the focus along the four fields, as they move along the mode chips in Search Centre the next part: Body, Wheel, Centre, Body Menu back to the look. Every change is already saved Play/Pause play or pause, as everywhere Field Step a detent A full range at rest speed Hue 5 degrees three turns of the wheel (72 detents); under half a turn at 8x Saturation, Brightness 4 % about one turn (25 detents) Transparency 5 % 12 detents for the wheel and centre, 17 for the body

Hue wraps round; the other three stop at their ends with the end-of-list haptic.

Does a colour wheel turned by the click wheel hold up? For hue, yes, and it is the natural pairing: both are circles and clockwise means onward in both. On its own, no. A colour has three dimensions and a part has a fourth, and the wheel moves one value at a time, so it needs the four fields and a way to step between them. With them, a whole look can be made by the wheel alone. The wheel's angle is never mapped straight onto the hue (touch at three o'clock, get that hue): the wheel is relative everywhere else, its four compass points are buttons, and the first 7.5 degrees decide press or turn.

Direct touch, when the device view's candidate 2 is in force:

  • touching or dragging on the colour wheel sets hue and saturation together, and moves the focus to Hue;
  • dragging along a field's bar sets that field; tapping a field focuses it;
  • tapping a part tab changes the part.

Touch is the quick way to a rough colour; the wheel then refines it a step at a time. The colour wheel is 144 pt across on a 393 pt phone, so a fingertip covers some 15 degrees of hue: good for getting near, not for finishing.

Why not wheel only: the first colour is three turns away. Why not touch only: the device view may yet be wheel only (gate 1), the screen reader's adjustable wheel must be able to do all of it, and a finger hides the colour it is choosing. With a screen reader the wheel's label is the field (Hue) and its value 205 degrees, body; increment and decrement step it; the part tabs and fields are also reachable as elements.

docs.title: 4. Readability on any colour
docs.text:
The legends are MENU, play/pause, previous and next on the wheel, the neuPod wordmark on the body, and the phone's own status bar. All must reach 4.5:1 on whatever is chosen.

The rule. Legend ink is pure black #000000 or pure white #ffffff, nothing between.

  1. Work out the colours under the legend: the part's colour at both ends of its gradient (section 5 gives the gradients), each composited over the darkest and the lightest of what shows through if the part is see-through.
  2. For each ink take its worst contrast over those colours (WCAG 2 relative luminance). Use the ink whose worst case is higher; black on a tie. For one flat colour this is black at luminance 0.179 or more, white below.
  3. If that worst case is under 4.5:1, paint the part flat: its one colour, no gradient. Go to 1.
  4. If it is still under 4.5:1 (only possible when the part is see-through), give back transparency in steps of 5 % and go to 1 each time. At 0 % a flat colour always passes.

Why it always ends: against one opaque colour, the better of pure black and pure white is never under 4.58:1 (the worst case is at luminance 0.179). Greys for ink would not have that property, which is why the device view's #5a5f67 and #cfcfcf glyphs are not used in Custom.

Numbers:

Value Ink #000000 or #ffffff Switch, one flat colour luminance 0.179 (black at or above) Target 4.5:1; 7:1 with Increase Contrast (section 8) Guaranteed for any opaque flat colour 4.58:1 Step when giving back transparency 5 %

Which legend uses what:

Legend Measured against Notes The wheel's four legends the wheel's gradient ends, over the blurred board's darkest and lightest colour when see-through one ink for all four, and for the ring's edge and groove Wordmark the body's gradient ends when the body is see-through the wordmark sits on a badge (section 5), a flat patch of the body's colour, so it is measured against that one colour Phone status bar the body's top colour alone (the solid cap, section 5) black ink maps to the dark status bar style, white to the light one Centre button nothing it carries no legend; its ink is used only for its edge and pressed tint

The stored look is never changed by the rule. The editor's legend note says what was done, and the Transparency field keeps showing what was asked.

Alternatives. Backing plates under every legend: provable, but four stickers on a clear wheel. Clamping the colour until grey ink passes, as Modern clamps its accent: the user then cannot have the colour they chose, on an opaque part where nothing is forcing it. Giving up the gradient costs far less than either.

docs.title: 5. Transparency
docs.text:
Part see-through Clear case

Layers, bottom to top.

  1. The board's ground colour, over the whole phone.
  2. The board picture, sharp, with its anchor on the wheel's centre (section 6).
  3. The body's colour at the body's opacity.
  4. The cap: the body's top colour, solid, from the phone's top edge to the screen frame's top edge, then fading to nothing over 0.06 W. The phone's status bar is always on a known colour.
  5. The screen frame and screen, unchanged, plus a 1 px outer edge in the body's ink at 16 % so the frame reads on a dark or see-through body.
  6. The wordmark; on its badge when the body is see-through. The badge is the body's colour, flat and solid, radius 0.036 W, with 0.012 W of padding above and below and 0.03 W each side.
  7. Inside the wheel's circle: the blurred copy of the board picture (same anchor and scale), then the wheel's colour at the wheel's opacity. The body's colour is not under the wheel.
  8. Inside the centre button: the blurred copy again, then the centre's colour at its opacity.
  9. Edges, legends, touch and press tints.

Layers 1, 2, 7 and 8 are drawn only when something needs them. A look with every part solid draws no picture and costs what a finish costs today.

What shows behind what. Behind the body, the board sharp: this is the clear case. Behind the wheel and the centre button, the board blurred, like frosted plastic: shapes and colour come through, detail does not. That keeps the legends on a calm ground, makes the wheel read as a separate part even when it is the body's colour, and is why the wheel can be see-through at all. The blur is made when the asset is built, never live.

Most transparency. Body 85 %; wheel and centre 60 %. Nothing reaches 100 %: a part with no colour of its own has no edge to find and no tint to press, and "clear" plastic is never invisible. The wheel's lower limit keeps the rule in section 4 from having to give much back.

Gradients. A part's one colour makes its gradient by mixing toward white (+) or black (-):

Part Top Middle Bottom Body +10 % at 0 the colour at 45 % -10 % at 100 % Wheel ring +6 % -6 % Centre button +6 % -6 %

Edges and states, in the part's ink (black or white):

Solid part See-through part Ring edge and centre edge, 1 px ink at 30 % the same Groove round the centre, 0.04 R ink at 22 % the same Finger on the ring, 50 degree wedge black at 7 % or white at 8 % plus 6 % x transparency: up to 10.6 % or 11.6 % Button or centre pressed black at 13 % or white at 14 % plus 10 % x transparency: up to 19 % or 20 % Disabled legends at 35 % the same

A tint over a busy ground reads weaker than the same tint over a flat one, so it strengthens with transparency. Idle, the edge and the groove carry the wheel's shape; they are ink, not a shade of the part, so they survive any colour and any transparency.

docs.title: 6. Board pictures
docs.text:
Value Size 1200 x 3120 px, portrait, opaque, sRGB Format WebP, lossy at quality 85 or lossless if smaller; about 300 KB a picture is the aim Scale 1200 px is W, the phone's width. Drawn at phone width / 1200, never stretched and never cropped to fit Anchor pixel (600, 2040) sits on the wheel's centre. 1.70 W of picture above it, 0.90 W below Beyond the edges the board's ground colour, stored with the asset Blurred copy the same picture, Gaussian blur of radius 36 px (0.03 W), saved at 300 x 780 px and scaled up Per board, stored id, name, ground, and frostDark and frostLight: the darkest and lightest pixel of the blurred copy inside the largest wheel circle (radius 384 px about the anchor), measured when the asset is built

Alignment. The picture hangs from the wheel, not from the top of the phone, because the wheel's centre is the one point that moves with the phone's height. The board sits behind the wheel in the real device, so the picture should have the wheel's connector, or whatever is truly there, at the anchor. A taller phone shows more picture above and below; the screen covers most of what is above.

Composing a picture. Fill the whole canvas: the board at its true scale relative to the body where that is known, on a plain backing in the board's ground colour. Keep the area inside radius 384 px of the anchor free of large white silkscreen or bare bright metal, so the blurred copy stays within about 40 levels from darkest to lightest; the app's asset test fails a picture whose spread makes a white, 60 % see-through wheel give back more than 10 %.

The set. Three, as drawn: Main board, top, Main board, bottom, Copper only (the copper layers alone). Only neuPod's own boards may be used: KiCad renders or the owner's photographs of them. No picture of any Apple board, and none of the donor's. boards/ in this repository is empty today, so there is nothing to render from yet: the three pictures in the mock-ups are placeholders made by render.py, each lettered PLACEHOLDER · NOT A NEUPOD BOARD across its face. The feature can be built and tested with them but must not be released with them (Open question 2).

docs.title: 7. Presets
docs.text:
• Six looks at most. With New look that is seven rows, the screen's worth at the standard text size, so the list never scrolls (owner decision 2). Each is a few dozen bytes; the limit is the screen, not storage.
  • Where: Settings > Custom look.
  • Save: there is no Save. A look is stored as each change is made.
  • New look makes a copy of the look in use (of the default finish when there is none), named Look n with the lowest unused number, opens it and makes it the look in use. That is also "save as". At six it is greyed with its reason at the right: 6 of 6.
  • Name: the Name row, typed with the device's text entry. Sixteen characters, the firmware's glyph set. An empty name is not accepted: Menu on an empty field leaves the old name.
  • Switch: Select on a look in the list.
  • Delete: Reset or delete > Delete look, then a centred panel Delete Harbour? with Delete and Menu to cancel, because something is about to be lost. Deleting the look in use makes the one above it the look in use. Deleting the last look leaves the list with only New look, and Mode falls back to Auto.
  • Reset to default: Reset or delete > Reset to default, with the same kind of panel. It sets the look's three parts to the default finish for the look's screen as it stands (Light, or Auto on a light phone: the silver values below; otherwise the black ones), all solid. The name, the board and the screen choice are kept.
Default Body Wheel Centre Light 218, 4, 88 (#d7dbe0) 220, 2, 95 (#edeff2) 220, 4, 87 (#d5d8de) Dark 225, 20, 8 (#101114) 223, 12, 14 (#1f2124) 228, 19, 6 (#0c0d0f) Default, Light Default, Dark

These are close to the silver and black finishes but are not them: Custom makes its gradients and its ink by its own rules. Light and Dark modes keep the finish table exactly.

The starter looks (owner decision 3) are in the list on first use and are ordinary looks: they can be edited, renamed and deleted, and are not restored.

Look Body Wheel Centre Board Screen Harbour 205, 62, 44, solid 40, 8, 94, solid 205, 62, 36, solid Main board, top Auto Sea glass 165, 35, 70, 55 % 165, 10, 96, solid 165, 40, 60, solid Main board, top Auto Clear case 200, 6, 92, 85 % 200, 4, 96, 60 % 200, 6, 90, 60 % Copper only Auto

docs.title: 8. Accessibility
docs.text:
Setting What Custom does Reduce Transparency (iOS; Android where the system offers one) Every part paints solid; no board picture is loaded. The look is not changed. In the editor the Transparency field is greyed, with Reduce Transparency is on as the legend note while it has the focus Increase Contrast (iOS; Android's high-contrast setting) As Reduce Transparency, and: the legend target is 7:1. A part whose legend falls short has its brightness moved the least distance, darker or lighter, that reaches it (luminance at most 0.100 or at least 0.300 for a flat colour). Edges go from 30 % to 60 % ink. The look is not changed Reduce Motion No pulse when the part changes; previews in the lists swap without a fade Largest text The lists show fewer, larger rows, as every list does. The part editor keeps its structure and drops what it can say elsewhere (below) Reduce Transparency, Clear case Increase Contrast, Sea glass

The part editor at the text tiers.

Tier k Layout Standard 1 as section 2 Large 7/6 the hint line goes; fields 66 high; colour wheel 230 Largest 7/5 the part tabs go (the status-bar title already names the part, and Select still steps it); the right column shows the focused field only: its name at 31 px, its value at 53 px, its bar, and 1 of 4; colour wheel 230; the legend note stays

At the Large and Largest tiers the list of looks and a look's seven rows no longer fit and move with the wheel, as all lists do there; no scroll bar is drawn on Custom's screens (Open question 5).

Screen reader: a look's row reads Harbour, in use, 1 of 4; a part row Body, solid, 1 of 7; the colour wheel is one element, Colour, hue 205 degrees, saturation 62 percent, not adjustable (the click wheel is the adjustable element). Nothing in the editor is told by colour alone: values are written beside every bar, and the swatch has its hex beside it.

docs.title: 9. Classic and Modern
docs.text:
Custom changes the body, never the screen. The screen's style comes from the Style setting and its mode from the look's Screen choice, so all four modes work with both styles. The screen always sits in its black glass frame, which is what keeps a loud body off it.

A pale body with Classic Light A saturated body with Modern Dark
  • Pale body, Classic Light (Chalk: 48, 10, 98). The white screen and the cream body are close in tone; the frame separates them as it does on silver. Ink is black at 15:1 or more on all three parts. The wheel differs from the body by a few levels only, so its shape rests on the 30 % edge and the drop shadow, as silver's does.
  • Saturated body, Modern Dark (Flare: body 338, 88, 86; wheel 338, 70, 30; centre 20, 90, 95). Modern takes its accent and backdrop from the album art, so the body may clash with it; that is the user's choice and is left alone. The body's luminance is 0.167, just under the switch: ink is white, the gradient fails by a hair and the body is painted flat, for 4.85:1. The phone's status bar is light. This is the case the flat rule exists for.

Classic Dark and Modern Light are still not designed (UI styles Open question 1). Until they are, a look whose Screen is Dark in Classic, or Light in Modern, shows the style's designed mode, exactly as Light and Dark modes do today.

docs.title: 10. The data model
docs.text:
In plain terms; names are suggestions.

A part's paint: four whole numbers.

Field Range Meaning hue 0 to 359 degrees round the colour wheel, red at 0 saturation 0 to 100 per cent, from the wheel's centre to its rim brightness 0 to 100 per cent (the V of HSV) transparency 0 to 85 for the body, 0 to 60 for the wheel and centre per cent see-through. Opacity is 100 less this

The RGB colour is computed from the first three by the usual HSV conversion (hsv() in render.py) and never stored. Storing what the user set means a grey keeps its hue and a black keeps its saturation when the editor is opened again.

A look.

Field Type Notes id string made once, never reused; the list's order is the stored order name string 1 to 16 characters body, wheel, centre part paint board main-top, main-bottom or copper an unknown id falls back to main-top screen light, dark or auto

The setting.

Field Type Notes mode light, dark, auto or custom replaces today's pinned-or-not mode looks list of looks, 0 to 6 the three starters until the user changes them lookInUse a look's id, or none kept when Mode leaves Custom

Not stored: the ink, the flat flag, the transparency kept, the gradients. They are worked out from the look, the board and the accessibility settings each time, so a changed rule or a new board picture never needs a migration.

{
  "mode": "custom",
  "lookInUse": "look-2",
  "looks": [
    {
      "id": "look-2",
      "name": "Sea glass",
      "body": { "hue": 165, "saturation": 35, "brightness": 70, "transparency": 55 },
      "wheel": { "hue": 165, "saturation": 10, "brightness": 96, "transparency": 0 },
      "centre": { "hue": 165, "saturation": 40, "brightness": 60, "transparency": 0 },
      "board": "main-top",
      "screen": "auto"
    }
  ]
}
