docs.title: Implementation brief: Custom mode for the device view (AP-1)
docs.text:
You are building the design in README.md in this folder, in the Flutter app under mobile/. This brief stands alone: everything you need to build is here or in the mock-ups. Read the README for the reasons, look at every PNG in mockups/, and open the matching .html when you need an exact size or colour. render.py in this folder is the reference for the colour arithmetic; where this brief and render.py disagree, stop and ask.

You work through PROGRESS.md one item at a time and tick each item when its PR merges. It is the only record of where you are.

Not yours to decide: anything under the README's Open questions. Build what was drawn and leave the question open.

docs.title: Before the first step
docs.text:
1. Read docs/app/TEAM-BRIEF.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; their rules win over this brief.
  2. Read mobile/lib/ui/device/README.md, device_finish.dart, wheel_painter.dart, device_view.dart, mobile/lib/ui/screens/shell/shell_style.dart, mobile/lib/ui/screens/browse/settings_screen.dart and mobile/lib/domain/style/colour_math.dart.
  3. Run the app's tests. Everything passes before you change anything; if not, stop and report.
  4. This feature changes paint, not layout. device_geometry.dart, the hit zones and the wheel's numbers are not touched. A golden of Light or Dark mode that changes is a bug.

docs.title: The data model
docs.text:
Pure Dart, in mobile/lib/domain/style/. No Flutter imports.

enum LookPart { body, wheel, centre }
enum LookScreen { light, dark, auto }
enum ModeSetting { light, dark, auto, custom }

/// Whole numbers, as the editor sets them. RGB is computed, never stored.
final class PartPaint {
  final int hue;          // 0..359
  final int saturation;   // 0..100
  final int brightness;   // 0..100
  final int transparency; // 0..85 body, 0..60 wheel and centre
}

final class CustomLook {
  final String id;        // made once, never reused
  final String name;      // 1..16 characters
  final PartPaint body, wheel, centre;
  final String board;     // 'main-top' | 'main-bottom' | 'copper'; unknown falls back to 'main-top'
  final LookScreen screen;
}

final class CustomLooks {
  final List<CustomLook> looks; // 0..6, in list order
  final String? lookInUse;      // an id in looks, or null
}

JSON is the README's section 10 example, field for field. Reading clamps every number into its range and drops a seventh look and beyond; it never throws on a bad value.

Not stored, always computed: RGB, gradients, ink, the flat flag, the transparency kept.

docs.title: The contrast rule, as numbers
docs.text:
paintPart(PartPaint p, LookPart part, {List<int>? grounds, double need = 4.5}) returns the colours to draw with. It must give the same results as paint() in render.py.

Constant Value Ink 0x000000 or 0xffffff only Target 4.5; 7.0 with Increase Contrast Switch for one flat colour relative luminance 0.179: black at or above, white below Gradient ends, mixed toward white (top) and black (bottom) body 0.10 (stops at 0, 0.45 for the colour itself, 1); wheel 0.06; centre 0.06 Most transparency body 85; wheel 60; centre 60 Step when giving back transparency 5 Mix per channel, in sRGB bytes: round(a + (b - a) * t) Contrast contrastRatio in colour_math.dart (WCAG 2)

Steps:

  1. t = min(p.transparency, most); flat = false; base = hsv(p).
  2. stops = flat ? [base, base, base] : [mix(base, white, amp), base, mix(base, black, amp)].
  3. under = stops, or when t > 0 and grounds is given, every stop composited over every ground: mix(stop, ground, t / 100).
  4. black = min contrast(0x000000, u) over under; white likewise. ink = black >= white ? black : white; worst = max(black, white).
  5. If worst < need and not flat: flat = true, go to 2.
  6. While worst < need and t > 0: t -= 5, go to 2.
  7. Return base, stops, ink, worst, t (the transparency kept) and flat.

grounds is given for the wheel only: the board's frostDark and frostLight. The body and the centre pass none.

Other inks: the phone's status bar is black when relativeLuminance(body.stops[0]) >= 0.179, else white. The wordmark uses the body's ink. Edges: ink at 30 % (60 % with Increase Contrast); groove ink at 22 %; frame outer edge body ink at 16 %. Tints, with t the transparency kept as a fraction: finger on the ring 0.07 + 0.06 t for black ink or 0.08 + 0.06 t for white; pressed 0.13 + 0.10 t or 0.14 + 0.10 t.

Increase Contrast: transparency = 0, then for d = 0, 1, 2, ... try brightness - d then brightness + d (inside 0..100) and take the first whose paintPart(..., need: 7.0).worst >= 7.0.

Check values (from python3 render.py --numbers; base, ink, worst, transparency kept, flat; wheel over main-top):

Look Body Wheel Centre Harbour #2b5370 white 6.28, 0, no #f0e9dd black 15.28, 0, no #23445c white 8.62, 0, no Sea glass #74b2a3 black 7.04, 55, no #dcf5ef black 16.06, 0, no #5c998a black 5.71, 0, no Clear case #dde6eb black 13.30, 85, no #ebf2f5 black 4.86, 60, flat #d8e1e6 black 13.95, 60, no Flare (the README's awkward case) #db1a61 white 4.85, 0, flat #4c172b white 12.16, 0, no #f26118 black 5.77, 0, no

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
Per board, under mobile/assets/boards/ and listed in pubspec.yaml:

File What <id>.webp 1200 x 3120 px, opaque, sRGB. Pixel (600, 2040) is the anchor <id>.frost.webp the same picture, Gaussian blur radius 36 px, saved at 300 x 780 px an entry in boards.json id, name, ground (#rrggbb), frostDark, frostLight

mobile/tool/build_board.dart (or a script beside it) makes the frost copy and measures frostDark and frostLight: the darkest and lightest pixel, by relative luminance, of the frost copy inside radius 384 px (at full size) of the anchor.

The pictures do not exist yet. Build with placeholders: export the three from this folder's render.py (board_svg) and keep their PLACEHOLDER · NOT A NEUPOD BOARD lettering. Ids main-top, main-bottom, copper; names Main board, top, Main board, bottom, Copper only. Never add a picture of a board that is not neuPod's own. Real pictures are the owner's to supply (README Open question 2); a release check in step 9 keeps placeholders out of a store build.

Drawing a picture: scale W / 1200; put the anchor on the wheel's centre; paint ground wherever the picture does not reach.

docs.text:
• 2026-11-25: Design written. Board pictures are placeholders made by render.py; boards/ is empty.

Increase Contrast comes from MediaQuery.highContrast; its item and golden are still open. The frost pair is measured from the saved frost copy by tool/build_board.dart; the white-wheel asset test treats black to white as the worst pair (it keeps exactly 50 %). The wordmark badge uses line height 1.2 as in render.py.

The Increase Contrast golden (device_393x852_custom_seaglass_increase_contrast) is in; the Reduce Transparency one (device_393x852_custom_clear_reduce_transparency) is #178's. A value off the grid first lands on the grid (a detent), so 218 degrees reaches 205 in three detents.
  • 2026-11-28 (#177): domain/style/board_list.dart is now generated from boards.json by tool/build_board.dart (#178). The board picker's pane is a plain tile until there are pictures.

Follow-ups from the #178 review, for before a store release: the placeholder check runs only with NEUPOD_STORE_BUILD=1, so an Xcode Product > Archive skips it (also run it when ACTION = install) and Android should hook bundleRelease unconditionally; the Gradle hook calls bare dart (use $FLUTTER_ROOT/bin/dart); the board picture re-decodes, and a see-through body shows solid for a moment, on every window-width change (iPad Stage Manager): round the width up or keep the last image until the new one is ready.

  • svg/: one SVG per glyph on Lucide's 24 px grid, and the app icon masters;
  • mockups/: the sheets as standalone HTML and PNG;
  • render.py: draws the sheets. It builds the new glyphs into a small font and rasterises every glyph with lv_font_conv 1.5.3 at 1 bpp, the tool and flags tools/gen_ui_fonts.sh already uses, so the 1-bit pixels on the sheets are the firmware's own bitmaps, not an approximation.

docs.title: The app icon (AP-2)
docs.text:
Direction What it is For Against A · Monogram nP from the wordmark, Montserrat Medium outlines, Harbour blue on warm white No likeness risk at all; reads as a name Says nothing about music; two letters get thin at 20 px B · Turning wheel (recommended) The device view's wheel in the Harbour starter look: blue body, warm white ring, blue centre in its groove; four dots mark the button sectors; a 50° wedge is the device view's touch tint, a finger mid-turn Says "this is the player you hold", ties the icon to the device view and Custom mode, survives monochrome and tint as a pure shape Any wheel invites the Apple comparison: see below C · Trace An n routed as a copper PCB trace with pads and a via, on solder-mask green Open hardware, the clear-case story; nobody else's Reads as electronics, not music

Decided: B (owner, 26 November 2026). It is the one an owner recognises on a crowded home screen, and it is already neuPod's own drawing. How it differs from Apple's click wheel and product artwork (constitution VI):

  • no MENU, no transport legends: four plain dots mark the sectors of the device view's hit-zone geometry instead;
  • the device view's proportions (centre 0.36 D, groove 0.44 R), not the 5G/6G's;
  • no screen, no body outline, no device silhouette: just the wheel, so it is not a picture of a product;
  • coloured in neuPod's Harbour look; the touch wedge is neuPod's own state from the device view;
  • no Apple glyph, apple, iPod name or SF Symbol anywhere.

A and C are kept as masters for the record only.

docs.title: iOS and Android
docs.text:
• iOS (svg/app-icon-master.svg, -dark, -tinted): full-bleed 1024 squares, iOS applies the mask. Dark uses the black body finish with the ring in a lighter Harbour blue (#4d93d6 to #2c6fae) so it holds on black. Tinted is grayscale on black: white ring, dark grey centre.
  • Android (svg/android-foreground.svg, -background, -monochrome): 108 dp canvas; the wheel is 62 dp across, inside the 66 dp safe circle, so circle, squircle and rounded-square masks all keep it whole. Monochrome is one colour with the four dots cut out and the groove open, so the system tint keeps the wheel's structure.
  • Directions A and C exist as single masters only (svg/app-icon-direction-a-monogram.svg, -c-trace.svg), enough to choose from. Variants are drawn for the chosen direction.

docs.title: The glyphs
docs.text:
Glyph (svg/) Base Code point Meaning Where it shows jack-plug new (redrawn on the Lucide grid from classic-status-states.html) U+EF00 Output set to Line Status bar, output slot fast-forward Lucide fast-forward U+E0BD Scanning forward (Next held) Status bar, play-state slot rewind Lucide rewind U+E147 Scanning back (Previous held) Status bar, play-state slot loader-circle Lucide loader-circle U+E10A Opening / loading (network streaming) Status bar, play-state slot play-off Lucide play-off U+E6FE Can't play Status bar, play-state slot; greyed row with its reason record new U+EF01 Recording Status bar, play-state slot ellipsis Lucide ellipsis U+E0B6 Busy: library update in the background Status bar, right zone, first speaker Lucide speaker U+E166 Output is an external speaker (Wi-Fi, AirPlay or other) Status bar, output slot; output pickers download Lucide download U+E0B2 Download (an action) App rows and menus cloud-download Lucide cloud-download U+E089 Downloading: an iCloud file not yet on the phone; the reason is on the row App rows star Lucide star U+E176 Rating, unlit Lists, Now Playing page 2 star-filled new, derived from Lucide star U+EF02 Rating, lit Lists, Now Playing page 2 bluetooth-connected Lucide bluetooth-connected U+E1B8 Headset connected or in use Status bar, Bluetooth slot

Lucide code points are the Lucide font's own (1.72.0, as pinned in tools/gen_ui_fonts.sh). The three new glyphs take U+EF00 to U+EF02, a private-use block above Lucide's highest (U+E853) and below the Font Awesome symbols (U+F001 up).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Lucide wherever Lucide has it. Nine of the thirteen are unmodified Lucide glyphs: they come through the existing pipeline with only new code points. Only the plug, the record mark and the lit star are drawn.
  2. The jack plug is redrawn on the grid, 2 px stroke, round caps and joins: a 6-unit tip with one insulating ring, a 10-unit body with rounded bottom, a 3-unit cable. It keeps the drawing's meaning and its upright stance, and stays distinct from Lucide plug (a mains plug with two prongs). At 16 px the tip closes to a solid pin and still reads.
  3. Fills only for "on". The rule allows fills only where the UI styles already use them. Two glyphs mean lit, and the fill is their non-colour cue: the lit star (filled versus outline) and the record mark (a solid dot in a ring; the dot is the universal sign, red is extra). Nothing else is filled.
  4. Ratings in the device's way: lit in the style's accent (#1858c8 Classic Light; #6db3f5 Classic Dark; the art's light tint, #f2a586 in the mock-up, on Modern), unlit in line grey. Filled versus outline carries the meaning without colour. List size is the icon font's small size (16 / 24 / 30 px by profile), Now Playing the large (24 / 36 / 45). This replaces the Font Awesome star (UI_SYMBOL_STAR) so ratings match the rest of the icons.
  5. Bluetooth gets a shape cue (Gate 2, owner decision 13): connected or in use is bluetooth-connected (the glyph with a tick each side) and blue; saved but not connected is plain bluetooth in the dim colour. The app already ships bluetooth-connected.svg; this brings the firmware into line.
  6. Busy dots sit first in the right zone, before Wi-Fi: a background job is device state, like the radios, and the left zone belongs to playback. The firmware keeps drawing them as three shapes that light in turn (ui_icons.h says so); the ellipsis glyph is for the app and for static places. Lucide's dots land unevenly at 16 px (see the x4 cell), which is why the drawn shapes stay.
  7. External speaker is Lucide speaker, never AirPlay's glyph (owner decision 13), for every wireless or network output that is not a Bluetooth headset.
  8. Opening uses loader-circle as a static glyph. It may turn in 45° steps on hosted builds; on the microcontroller it stays still.
  9. Contrast. Every glyph colour meets 4.5:1 against the worst point under it (for the status bar, its darkest or lightest gradient stop; for Modern, the bar over a bright art backdrop). This moved three Classic Light values from the 21 November table, as Gate 2 asked:
Style Role Colour Worst ground Ratio Classic Light glyph #3a3d42 bar #b6bbc2 5.65 Classic Light dim (was #9a9ea5) #474b52 bar #b6bbc2 4.54 Classic Light Bluetooth active (was #1858c8) #123f8f bar #b6bbc2 5.10 Classic Light recording #8a1a15 bar #b6bbc2 4.86 Classic Light star lit / unlit #1858c8 / #737373 #ffffff 6.42 / 4.74 Classic Dark* glyph / dim #dfe2e6 / #b5bac1 bar #45484e 7.06 / 4.70 Classic Dark* Bluetooth active / recording #9ccbff / #ffa79e bar #45484e 5.41 / 4.92 Classic Dark* star lit / unlit #6db3f5 / #8e939a #0d0e10 8.66 / 6.24 Modern Dark glyph / dim (was #7a7a7a) #f0f0f0 / #9a9a9a bar over a gold wash #2f2a1f 12.5 / 5.07 Modern Dark Bluetooth active / recording #5aa2ff / #ff7b70 #2f2a1f 5.47 / 5.65 Modern Dark star lit / unlit #f2a586 / #7c7c7c #050608 10.1 / 4.86

* Classic Dark is still not designed (UI styles open question 1). Its colours here are provisional, chosen only so the glyphs could be checked on a dark Classic ground. They are not a design for Classic Dark.

With the dim colour this dark, saved and connected Bluetooth are told apart by shape, not by shade, which is why decision 5 matters.

docs.title: The status bar
docs.text: Six states, in all three styles, at 600x450 (icons 30 px) and 320x240 (16 px), every glyph 1-bit from the real font: scanning forward with a headset connected; scanning back with a saved headset and wired headphones; opening a stream to a wireless speaker; a library update while locked; a track that can't play with Line out; recording. The right zone order is: busy, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, output (headphones, jack plug or speaker), lock, battery.

docs.text:

docs.title: Licences
docs.text: Everything drawn here is the project's own: the sheets and this text CC BY 4.0, the SVGs and the app icon alongside the firmware under MPL-2.0. Nine glyphs are unmodified Lucide icons and star-filled is derived from Lucide star: all ten are ISC (Lucide 1.72.0). Correction (firmware PR #173, checked against lucide-static 1.72.0's LICENSE): download and ellipsis (Feather's more-horizontal) derive from Feather (MIT), as do headphones and monitor, which the firmware also draws. Add them to the Lucide row of LICENSE.md (now "the 15 icons of the design system and the 5 of the boot splash" plus these 10) and to the Licences screen (app/ui/ui_licence_data.c), which tests/test_licences.c checks. jack-plug, record and the app icon are entirely neuPod's; direction A's letters are Montserrat Medium outlines (SIL OFL 1.1, already in the table).

docs.title: Implementation brief: icon set (26 November 2026)
docs.text: For the engineers building the icon set. The README holds the decisions; this file says what to do with them. Tick items off in PROGRESS.md as they merge. Firmware first (ADR-0022: it is the reference), then the app in the same or the next PR, or a backlog item for the gap.

docs.title: 1. Files in this folder
docs.text: Path What Use svg/<glyph>.svg (13) 24x24, stroke="currentColor", 2 px, round caps and joins Source of truth for every glyph svg/app-icon-master.svg 1024x1024, light iOS AppIcon, light svg/app-icon-master-dark.svg 1024x1024, dark iOS AppIcon, dark svg/app-icon-master-tinted.svg 1024x1024, grayscale on black iOS AppIcon, tinted svg/android-foreground.svg, -background.svg, -monochrome.svg 108x108 dp viewBox Android adaptive icon layers svg/app-icon-direction-a-monogram.svg, -c-trace.svg 1024 masters Not chosen; kept for the record render.py Builds the preview font and the sheets Re-run after any SVG change

docs.title: 2. Firmware: getting the glyphs into the icon font
docs.text:
Today tools/gen_ui_fonts.sh turns lucide-static 1.72.0's lucide.ttf into app/ui/fonts/neupod_icons_{16,24,30,36,45}.c at 1 bpp, with the code points in ICONS and the defines in app/ui/ui_icons.h.

2a. Lucide glyphs (no new step). Add these code points to ICONS, in this order after the existing ones:

# scanning, opening, can't play, busy, speaker, download, downloading, star, bluetooth connected
0xe0bd,0xe147,0xe10a,0xe6fe,0xe0b6,0xe166,0xe0b2,0xe089,0xe176,0xe1b8

2b. New glyphs (one extra step). jack-plug, record and star-filled are not in Lucide. Build them into a small TrueType font from svg/ and merge it into the same lv_font_conv call, so they come out in the same neupod_icons_* fonts with the same settings:

  1. Add tools/build_icon_extra_font.py (Python, fonttools and picosvg): for each new SVG, expand strokes to outlines with picosvg, scale to Lucide's grid (24 units to 1000 per em, y' = 1000 - y * 1000 / 24, ascent 1000, descent 0, advance 1000), and map them to U+EF00 jack-plug, U+EF01 record, U+EF02 star-filled. Output build/neupod-icons-extra.ttf (not committed). build_extra_font() in this folder's render.py is a working reference: lift it.
  2. In gen_ui_fonts.sh, call it before the icon loop and pass a second font to the same command: --font lucide.ttf -r "$ICONS" --font "$EXTRA_TTF" -r 0xef00-0xef02. Flags stay as they are (--bpp 1 --no-compress --no-prefilter, sizes 16, 24, 30, 36, 45).
  3. Pin picosvg and fonttools versions in the script header, as lv_font_conv and lucide-static are pinned, so the generated .c files are reproducible. Record the SVGs' sha256 in the generated header comment.

2c. Defines in app/ui/ui_icons.h (UTF-8 of each code point):

Define Code point Glyph UI_ICON_FAST_FORWARD U+E0BD fast-forward UI_ICON_REWIND U+E147 rewind UI_ICON_OPENING U+E10A loader-circle UI_ICON_CANT_PLAY U+E6FE play-off UI_ICON_BUSY U+E0B6 ellipsis (static places only; the status bar keeps its drawn dots) UI_ICON_SPEAKER U+E166 speaker UI_ICON_DOWNLOAD U+E0B2 download UI_ICON_DOWNLOADING U+E089 cloud-download UI_ICON_STAR U+E176 star (unlit) UI_ICON_STAR_FILLED U+EF02 star-filled (lit) UI_ICON_BLUETOOTH_CONNECTED U+E1B8 bluetooth-connected UI_ICON_JACK_PLUG U+EF00 jack-plug UI_ICON_RECORD U+EF01 record

Once page 2 uses the new stars, remove UI_SYMBOL_STAR and its code point 61445 (U+F005) from SYMS in gen_ui_fonts.sh (check nothing else draws it first), and keep ui_text_has_glyph() in step.

2d. Which code draws which glyph

Place Today Change Status bar, play-state slot (ui_status_*) play / pause, then shuffle / repeat Add: scanning (FAST_FORWARD / REWIND while a seek key is held), OPENING while a stream opens, CANT_PLAY when the current track failed, RECORD while recording. Mode glyphs follow as today Status bar, right zone Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, headphones, lock, battery Order: busy dots (drawn), Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, output, lock, battery. Bluetooth: BLUETOOTH_CONNECTED + active colour when connected or in use, BLUETOOTH + dim when saved only. Output: HEADPHONES, JACK_PLUG (Line) or SPEAKER (external) Now Playing page 2, rating Font Awesome star STAR_FILLED in the accent token for lit, STAR in the line-grey token for unlit, icon font large List rows with a rating none Same pair at the icon font's small size Greyed row that can't play text reason CANT_PLAY before the reason (the reason stays)

2e. Theme tokens. Glyph colours come from theme tokens like text (ui_icon()). New or changed values, per the README's contrast table: Classic Light status_dim #474b52, bt_active #123f8f, recording #8a1a15, rating_lit = selection blue #1858c8, rating_unlit #737373; Modern status_dim #9a9a9a, recording #ff7b70, rating_lit = the art's light tint (the progress fill's colour), rating_unlit #7c7c7c. Flat fills stay RGB565-exact on the LCD: round these with the existing helper and re-check 4.5:1 after rounding. Classic Dark values in render.py are provisional and are not to be added as a theme.

docs.title: 3. App (Flutter, mobile/)
docs.text:
3a. Glyphs. The app draws icons from SVG path data (lib/ui/style/icons/neupod_glyphs.dart) with the SVGs kept in assets/icons/lucide/. Copy the 13 SVGs from svg/ into assets/icons/ (Lucide ones into lucide/, the three new ones into a new assets/icons/neupod/ with this folder's licence note) and add their path data to neupod_glyphs.dart under the same names. star-filled and record need the painter to honour fill="currentColor": check svg_shapes.dart does, or add it. Use them in the same places as the firmware (2d), plus:

  • Download (an action) on album and song rows and menus: download;
  • an iCloud file not yet on the phone: cloud-download on the row, with the reason in the row's second line;
  • output picker: speaker for every external output that is not a Bluetooth headset. Never Apple's AirPlay glyph, even where iOS's route picker would offer it.

3b. App icon, one source for both platforms. Add flutter_launcher_icons (dev dependency, version pinned) and export PNGs from the SVG masters with rsvg-convert in a small script, mobile/tool/export_app_icon.sh, run by hand when the masters change (the PNGs are committed, the SVGs stay the source here):

rsvg-convert -w 1024 -h 1024 svg/app-icon-master.svg        -o mobile/assets/app_icon/icon.png
rsvg-convert -w 1024 -h 1024 svg/app-icon-master-dark.svg   -o mobile/assets/app_icon/icon_dark.png
rsvg-convert -w 1024 -h 1024 svg/app-icon-master-tinted.svg -o mobile/assets/app_icon/icon_tinted.png
rsvg-convert -w 432  -h 432  svg/android-foreground.svg     -o mobile/assets/app_icon/android_fg.png
rsvg-convert -w 432  -h 432  svg/android-background.svg     -o mobile/assets/app_icon/android_bg.png
rsvg-convert -w 432  -h 432  svg/android-monochrome.svg     -o mobile/assets/app_icon/android_mono.png

flutter_launcher_icons:
  android: true
  ios: true
  image_path: assets/app_icon/icon.png
  image_path_ios_dark_transparent: assets/app_icon/icon_dark.png
  image_path_ios_tinted_grayscale: assets/app_icon/icon_tinted.png
  remove_alpha_ios: true
  adaptive_icon_foreground: assets/app_icon/android_fg.png
  adaptive_icon_background: assets/app_icon/android_bg.png
  adaptive_icon_monochrome: assets/app_icon/android_mono.png

Run dart run flutter_launcher_icons and commit the generated AppIcon.appiconset and mipmap-* resources. The iOS dark master is opaque (black body finish); if a reviewer prefers Apple's transparent dark style, export it without its first <rect> (the background) and keep remove_alpha_ios off for that file only.

docs.title: 4. Checks
docs.text:
• Snapshot tours (firmware and app) for the status bar in each state of the README's sheet, at 320x240 and 600x450.
  • A host test that every UI_ICON_* define has a glyph in each neupod_icons_* font (no tofu at 16 px).
  • tests/test_licences.c and LICENSE.md updated together (README, Licences).
  • Compare the generated 1-bit glyphs with mockups/glyphs-1bit-*.png: they are made by the same lv_font_conv call, so any difference means the build step drifted.
  • Phone: icon checked on a real home screen in light, dark and tinted (iOS) and with themed icons on (Android).

Do not change behaviour beyond what is listed: this brief adds glyphs and the app icon, nothing else.
